children.title: Coupling Hypergraph Representations
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial models for objective, constraint, and variable coupling.

children.title: Variable-Interaction Patterns
children.top_down_role: Coupling patterns induced by polynomial supports.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(H)\) records exactly the variable pairs coupled by at least one polynomial support term.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the standard support hypergraph and its two-section interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines support-induced hyperedges and their pairwise interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For polynomials \(p_0,\ldots,p_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For every exponent \(\alpha\in\bigcup_{j=0}^m\operatorname{supp}(p_j)\), define \(I(\alpha)=\{i\in V:\alpha_i>0\}\). The variable-interaction hypergraph is \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\), where \(\mathcal E\) consists of the nonempty sets \(I(\alpha)\), optionally after removing duplicate or contained hyperedges. Its two-section graph \(G(H)\) has edge \(\{i,k\}\) exactly when some \(E\in\mathcal E\) contains both \(i\) and \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial supports define hyperedges of jointly occurring variables; their two-section graph connects every pair appearing together in at least one supported monomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Interaction Patterns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the terminal and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable citation supports the particular hypergraph convention, including removal of contained hyperedges.

children.title: Constraint-to-Block Assignment
children.top_down_role: Organization of constraints within overlapping variable blocks.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_r\subseteq\{1,ldots,n\}\) are prescribed variable blocks.
Each constraint polynomial \(g_j\) has variable set \(V_j=\bigcup_{\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(g_j)}I(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every assigned localizing constraint depends only on variables of its assigned block.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Block containment is the standard validity predicate for assigning sparse localizing constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the containment condition for assigning polynomial constraints to overlapping blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraint \(g_j(x)\geq0\), define its eligible-block set by \(A_j=\{k\in\{1,\ldots,r\}:V_j\subseteq C_k\}\). A single-block assignment is valid when \(A_j\neq\varnothing\) and \(a(j)\in A_j\). More generally, a replicated assignment chooses a nonempty set \(B_j\subseteq A_j\). In either case, every moment or localizing expression generated from \(g_j\) uses only variables indexed by a containing block; if \(A_j=\varnothing\), the proposed block family cannot represent that constraint locally without enlargement or decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint may be assigned only to blocks containing every variable in its polynomial support; no eligible block signals an invalid sparse organization.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-to-Block Assignment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-containment condition fits the terminal, but it lacks a source. The first assumption also has malformed notation: \(\{1,ldots,n\}\) should use \(\ldots\).

children.title: Chordal Clique Organization
children.top_down_role: Graph completion and clique organization preceding sparse relaxation construction.

children.title: Chordal-Completion Families
children.top_down_role: Completion choices distinguished by fill and clique structure.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each member of \(\mathfrak C(G)\) preserves every original interaction edge while eliminating all induced cycles of length at least four.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The definition of a chordal completion by added fill edges is standard graph theory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines all chordal supergraphs on the fixed interaction-graph vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fill set is any \(F\subseteq\binom{V}{2}\setminus E\) such that \(G_F=(V,E\cup F)\) is chordal, meaning that every cycle of length at least four in \(G_F\) has a chord. The chordal-completion family is \(\mathfrak C(G)=\{G_F:F\text{ is a fill set}\}\). A completion is minimal when no proper subset of \(F\) is a fill set; it is minimum-fill when \(|F|\) is smallest over all fill sets. These notions need not select the same completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal-completion family contains all chordal supergraphs formed by adding interaction edges, with minimal and minimum-fill completions distinguished.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal-Completion Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes minimal from minimum-fill completions and fits the terminal, but no authoritative graph-theory locator is supplied.

children.title: Clique-Tree Representations
children.top_down_role: Clique organizations used for local models and separator coupling.

children.title: Maximal Clique Extraction
children.top_down_role: Identification of maximal variable blocks from chordal sparsity patterns.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal.
\((v_1,\ldots,v_n)\) is a perfect elimination ordering of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inclusion-maximal sets among \(C_1,ldots,C_n\) are exactly the maximal cliques of \(G\).

notation.meaning: Neighbors of \(v_i\) occurring later in the ordering.
Clique candidate generated at elimination step \(i\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Perfect-elimination ordering yields all maximal cliques through inclusion-maximal elimination neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extracts maximal cliques from a perfect elimination ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a chordal graph \(G=(V,E)\) and a perfect elimination ordering \((v_1,\ldots,v_n)\). For each \(i=1,\ldots,n\), form \(N_i^+=\{v_j:j>i,\{v_i,v_j\}\in E\}\) and the candidate \(C_i=\{v_i\}\cup N_i^+\). Because the ordering is perfect, every \(C_i\) is a clique. Remove duplicate candidates and every candidate strictly contained in another candidate. Output the remaining sets; they are precisely the maximal cliques of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Form each vertex's later-neighbor clique under a perfect elimination ordering, then discard duplicates and proper subsets to obtain all maximal cliques.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Clique Extraction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is standard and appropriately classified, but it has no citation. Its conclusion also contains malformed \(C_1,ldots,C_n\) notation.

children.title: Clique Tree Representations
children.top_down_role: Tree organizations of maximal cliques for sparse local models.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite chordal graph with maximal cliques \(\mathcal C=\{C_1,\ldots,C_r\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A tree on \(\mathcal C\) represents the clique overlaps exactly when it satisfies the running-intersection property.

notation.meaning: Tree whose vertices are maximal cliques.
Unique tree path between clique nodes.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the standard junction-tree characterization of maximal cliques of a chordal graph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the running-intersection characterization of a clique tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A clique tree for \(G\) is a tree \(T\) with vertex set \(\mathcal C\) such that, for every variable vertex \(v\in V\), the set \(\{C\in\mathcal C:v\in C\}\) induces a connected subtree of \(T\). Equivalently, for all \(C_i,C_j\in\mathcal C\), every clique \(C\) on the unique path \(P_T(C_i,C_j)\) satisfies \(C_i\cap C_j\subseteq C\). Every finite chordal graph admits such a tree, and its edges encode the overlaps used for local consistency constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique tree connects maximal cliques so that every variable's containing cliques form a connected subtree, equivalently satisfying running intersection along every path.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique Tree Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique-tree representation and running-intersection equivalence fit the terminal, but the existence and characterization claims require an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Separator Structure
children.top_down_role: Clique intersections governing local-model coupling.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a clique tree on maximal cliques \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each edge \(e\), the overlap \(S_e\) separates variables exclusive to the two components of \(T-e\).

notation.meaning: The two components obtained by deleting edge \(e\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Intersections on clique-tree edges are standard complete separators in chordal graphs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes edge intersections as separators between clique-tree branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an edge \(e=\{C,D\}\) of \(T\), define \(S_e=C\cap D\). Deleting \(e\) partitions \(T\) into components \(T_C\) and \(T_D\). Let \(U_C=(\bigcup_{K\in T_C}K)\setminus S_e\) and \(U_D=(\bigcup_{K\in T_D}K)\setminus S_e\). Then no edge of the chordal graph joins a vertex of \(U_C\) to a vertex of \(U_D\); consequently, \(S_e\) is a complete vertex separator whenever both sides are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each clique-tree edge intersection is a complete separator between variables belonging exclusively to the two branches created by deleting that edge.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separator property is correctly scoped to clique-tree edge intersections, but the graph-separation claim has no supporting citation.

children.title: Clique Tree Quality Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for comparing alternative clique trees.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a clique tree with clique set \(\mathcal C\) and edge separators \(S_e\).
\(d\in\mathbb N\) is a fixed relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed profile permits componentwise comparison of clique trees without claiming a universally optimal scalar criterion.

notation.meaning: Order-\(d\) monomial count on variables indexed by \(U\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Clique and separator sizes induce directly checkable sparse-relaxation dimension criteria.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a multi-criterion profile tied to sparse moment-block and separator dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the order-\(d\) quality profile by \(Q_d(T)=(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4)\), where \(q_1=\max_{C\in\mathcal C}b_d(C)\), \(q_2=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}b_d(C)^2\), \(q_3=\sum_{e\in E(T)}\binom{|S_e|+2d}{2d}\), and \(q_4=\operatorname{diam}(T)\). A tree \(T_1\) dominates \(T_2\) under these criteria when every component of \(Q_d(T_1)\) is no larger and at least one is smaller. Scalar rankings require explicitly chosen weights because these criteria can conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique trees can be compared by largest block, aggregate block cost, separator-consistency count, and diameter; these criteria may rank trees differently.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique Tree Quality Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed profile is an unsupported bespoke collection of criteria, especially the squared block-cost and diameter components. It is a definition or representation rather than a condition, and a source is needed to justify its relevance to sparse relaxations.

children.title: Completion-Quality Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Effects of fill, clique size, and separators on relaxation dimensions.

assumptions_latex: \(G_F\) is a chordal completion with maximal cliques \(\mathcal C_F\).
A sparse moment relaxation of order \(d\) uses all monomials of degree at most \(d\) within each clique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Completion quality is governed primarily by the induced clique and separator profile, not by fill count alone.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Monomial counting gives the stated block and overlap dimensions in dense clique-local bases.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies how completion-induced cliques and separators determine sparse relaxation dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(C\in\mathcal C_F\), the order-\(d\) moment matrix has dimension \(s_d(C)=\binom{|C|+d}{d}\). Thus a block-structured formulation contains PSD blocks of these dimensions, while equality of separator moments through degree \(2d\) contributes up to \(\binom{|S_e|+2d}{2d}\) scalar matches on edge \(e\). Adding fill edges can merge or enlarge maximal cliques, increasing PSD dimensions superlinearly, yet may alter separator sizes or decomposition structure beneficially. Therefore minimum fill need not minimize relaxation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fill edges affect relaxation cost through maximal-clique and separator sizes; a minimum-fill completion need not minimize semidefinite block dimensions or consistency work.
knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Quality Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monomial counts are plausible under the stated dense clique-local basis, but the separator count and assertion that minimum fill need not minimize relaxation cost require a supporting source or explicit documented example.

children.title: Running Intersection Principle
children.top_down_role: The structural principle supporting compatible clique-wise moment and positivity constructions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The ordered-overlap condition on variable blocks, together with its stated role in the sparse representation under discussion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordered family I_1,\ldots,I_p has the running intersection property if, for every k=1,\ldots,p-1, there exists s\leq k such that I_{k+1}\cap\left(\bigcup_{j=1}^{k}I_j\right)\subseteq I_s. In the sparse representation governed by this condition, the absence of variable coupling in the original polynomial data is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordered collection of variable blocks has the running intersection property when each new block's overlap with all earlier blocks is contained in one earlier block. In the associated sparse representation, this condition preserves the original lack of variable coupling.
assumptions_latex: I_1,\ldots,I_p\text{ are ordered variable-index sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{RIP}(I_1,\ldots,I_p)\iff\forall k\in\{1,\ldots,p-1\}\ \exists s\leq k:\ I_{k+1}\cap\left(\bigcup_{j=1}^{k}I_j\right)\subseteq I_s

source_evidence.locator: Positive polynomials and moment problems / 2.6. Representations with sparsity properties / Definition 2.6-extra-3

children.title: Clique-Tree Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency organization across neighboring clique intersections.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a clique tree with clique nodes \(\mathcal C\).
For each \(C\in\mathcal C\), \(y^C=(y^C_\alpha)\) is local moment data through degree \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Edgewise equality implies equality of all available moments on every clique intersection.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Running intersection propagates edgewise agreement along the unique clique-tree path.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States edgewise moment matching and its propagation through a clique tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The local data are clique-tree consistent through degree \(2d\) when, for every edge \(e=\{C,D\}\in E(T)\), \(y^C_\alpha=y^D_\alpha\) for every multi-index \(\alpha\) satisfying \(|\alpha|\leq2d\) and \(\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq S_e=C\cap D\). If this condition holds, then for arbitrary cliques \(C,D\) and every such \(\alpha\) supported in \(C\cap D\), the running-intersection property places its support in every clique on the path from \(C\) to \(D\), so successive edge equalities yield \(y^C_\alpha=y^D_\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching shared moments on each clique-tree edge propagates along paths, giving agreement on every pairwise clique intersection.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Tree Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The edgewise consistency condition and its propagation through running intersection are mathematically well scoped, but no authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: Local-Measure Gluing
children.top_down_role: Measure-theoretic assembly of compatible local moment data.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite clique tree on subsets \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
Each \(X_i\) is a standard Borel space, and \(\mu_C\) is a probability measure on \(X_C=\prod_{i\in C}X_i\).
For every edge \(\{C,D\}\), the marginals of \(\mu_C\) and \(\mu_D\) on \(X_{C\cap D}\) coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a global probability measure \(\mu\) whose marginal on every \(X_C\) equals \(\mu_C\).

notation.meaning: Marginal projection onto coordinates indexed by \(S\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the junction-tree gluing theorem for compatible probability marginals on standard Borel spaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite standard-Borel version of compatible marginal gluing along a clique tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^nX_i\). Under the stated assumptions, there exists a probability measure \(\mu\) on \(X\) such that \((\pi_C)_\#\mu=\mu_C\) for every clique \(C\). Coordinates not belonging to \(\bigcup_{C\in\mathcal C}C\) may be assigned arbitrary probability laws. The conclusion concerns full representing measures, not merely agreement of finitely truncated moment sequences; truncated positive semidefinite moment data require additional representability conditions before this gluing result applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible clique probability measures on a running-intersection tree glue to a global measure; finite truncated moments need separate representability assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Measure Gluing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite standard-Borel gluing theorem is precisely stated and distinguishes full measures from truncated moments, but a theorem of this strength requires an inspectable source.

children.title: Failure Boundary Without Running Intersection
children.top_down_role: Consistency and convergence failures caused by inadequate overlap structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise overlap consistency without running intersection does not guarantee a global representing measure.

notation.meaning: Uniform pair law supported on equal bits.
Uniform pair law supported on unequal bits.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The displayed binary marginal family directly verifies the obstruction by contradictory parity constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A three-block binary obstruction showing that pairwise consistency alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu_{12}\) and \(\mu_{23}\) assign probability \(1/2\) to each of \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\), while \(\mu_{13}\) assigns probability \(1/2\) to each of \((0,1)\) and \((1,0)\). Every one-variable marginal is uniform, so the three pair measures agree on all pairwise block intersections. Nevertheless, any joint measure with the first two marginals would satisfy \(X_1=X_2=X_3\) almost surely, whereas the third requires \(X_1\neq X_3\) almost surely. Hence no joint measure exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three pairwise-consistent binary marginals can impose two equality relations and one contradictory inequality, preventing any global measure when running intersection fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Boundary Without Running Intersection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary marginal construction is a correct and appropriately classified counterexample for the stated failure boundary, but the record supplies no citation.

children.title: Newton-Polytope Support Reduction
children.top_down_role: Convex-geometric restriction of candidate monomials and certificate supports.

children.title: Half-Newton-Polytope Bases
children.top_down_role: Support-restricted bases for Gram representations.

assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) is a sum of squares.
\(P=\operatorname{Newt}(p)=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{supp}(p))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An SOS Gram representation of \(p\) may use the monomial basis indexed by \((\tfrac12P)\cap\mathbb N^n\).

notation.meaning: Lattice exponents in the half Newton polytope.
Column vector of monomials indexed by \(B\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support reduction for SOS summands and their positive-semidefinite Gram basis.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Sum of Squares Representations and Semi-definite Optimization p. 16
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p=\sum_{k=1}^sq_k(x)^2\), then every exponent occurring in any \(q_k\) lies in \(B=(\tfrac12P)\cap\mathbb N^n\). Consequently, with \(z_B(x)=(x^\beta)_{\beta\in B}\), there exists a symmetric matrix \(Q\succeq0\) such that \(p(x)=z_B(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_B(x)\). Conversely, any \(Q\succeq0\) satisfying this coefficient identity yields an SOS decomposition of \(p\). Thus exponents outside the half Newton polytope are unnecessary in an SOS Gram basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOS polynomial has a positive-semidefinite Gram representation using only monomials whose exponents are lattice points in half its Newton polytope.
knowledge_statements.title: Half-Newton-Polytope Bases

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Sum of Squares Representations and Semi-definite Optimization p. 16
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

children.title: Face Decomposition of Supports
children.top_down_role: Support decompositions induced by faces of Newton polytopes.

assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) is a sum of squares.
\(F=\{\alpha\in\operatorname{New}(p):w^{\mathsf T}\alpha=c\}\) is an exposed face on which \(w^{\mathsf T}\alpha\) is minimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_F=\sum_j (q_j)_{F/2}^2\), so the support of the face polynomial is generated independently by monomials whose doubled exponents lie in \(F\).

notation.meaning: sum of terms of p with exponents in F
sum of terms of q whose exponents lie in the scaled face F/2

review_flags: locator supports SOS optimization generally; exact face-restriction statement requires source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposed-face restriction of a finite-dimensional SOS representation.

source_refs.locator: 5.2 Unconstrained Polynomial Optimization p. 111
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=\sum_j q_j^2\) and let \(F\) be an exposed face of \(\operatorname{New}(p)\), defined by the minimum \(c\) of \(w^{\mathsf T}\alpha\). For each \(q_j\), retain only terms \(x^\beta\) satisfying \(2\beta\in F\), and denote the resulting polynomial by \((q_j)_{F/2}\). Then the part of \(p\) supported on \(F\) satisfies \[p_F=\sum_j (q_j)_{F/2}^{2}.\] Consequently, every exposed face of the support induces an independent SOS subrepresentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting an SOS polynomial to an exposed Newton-polytope face yields another SOS, formed from the corresponding half-face monomials.
knowledge_statements.title: Face Decomposition of Supports

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2 Unconstrained Polynomial Optimization p. 111

children.title: Term-Sparsity Graphs
children.top_down_role: Monomial graphs encoding possible interactions in positivity certificates.

children.title: Support-Extension Families
children.top_down_role: Support-enlargement families used to strengthen term-sparse models.

assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb{N}^n\) is a finite monomial basis.
\(S_0\subseteq B+B\) is the initial exponent support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \((S_k)\) is increasing and defines a support-extension family whose limit is closed under clique sums.

notation.meaning: graph on exponent vectors in B induced by S

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotone clique-sum closure is a standard abstract support-extension construction
needs a term-sparsity source fixing the intended extension convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract clique-sum closure used in term-sparse SOS models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\subseteq B+B\), define \(G(S)\) on vertex set \(B\) by joining distinct \(\beta,\gamma\) when \(\beta+\gamma\in S\). Let \(\mathcal C(S)\) be a prescribed clique cover of a chordal extension of \(G(S)\). A support-extension family generated from \(S_0\) is the sequence \[S_{k+1}=S_k\cup\bigcup_{C\in\mathcal C(S_k)}(C+C),\qquad k\geq0.\] Thus every extension retains the preceding support and adds all exponent sums represented inside the selected term blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support-extension family repeatedly adds all exponent sums generated within selected cliques of the current term-interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Extension Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the prescribed chordal extension and clique-cover update constitute a particular support-extension convention. No source establishes that this is the intended term-sparsity family.

children.title: Term-Graph Chordalization
children.top_down_role: Chordal decomposition in monomial-interaction space.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a chordal graph on a finite monomial basis \(B\).
The diagonal and edge entries of a symmetric partial matrix \(Q\) are specified according to \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) has a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if \(Q[C_r,C_r]\succeq0\) for every maximal clique \(C_r\).

notation.meaning: partial Gram matrix indexed by B

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: chordal PSD-completion theorem is standard
needs an authoritative chordal matrix source and a source connecting it to monomial-interaction graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal PSD completion applied to a graph indexed by monomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\). A symmetric partial matrix \(Q\), whose specified positions are the diagonal and edges of \(H\), admits a completion \(\widehat Q\succeq0\) if and only if \[Q[C_r,C_r]\succeq0\qquad(r=1,\ldots,m).\] When \(Q\) is a polynomial Gram matrix indexed by \(B\), these clique constraints replace one global completion constraint by positive-semidefinite constraints in monomial-interaction space, with consistency imposed on entries shared by cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordal monomial graph, a partial Gram matrix is PSD-completable exactly when every maximal-clique principal matrix is PSD.
knowledge_statements.title: Term-Graph Chordalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chordal PSD-completion theorem is stated correctly and the theorem container fits, but no authoritative source is supplied for either the completion theorem or its application to monomial-interaction Gram matrices.

children.title: Term-Block Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Limiting block structures produced by repeated support refinement.

assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb{N}^n\) is finite.
The support update \(T:2^{B+B}\to2^{B+B}\) is extensive and monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration stabilizes at a fixed support \(S_\infty\) after at most \(|B+B|-|S_0|\) strict extensions.
review_flags: needs a source for its specialized term-block interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite stabilization of monotone support refinement on a fixed basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(S_0\subseteq B+B\), set \(S_{k+1}=T(S_k)\). Extensivity gives \(S_k\subseteq S_{k+1}\), and the finite ambient set \(B+B\) permits at most \(|B+B|-|S_0|\) strict inclusions. Hence some \(K\leq |B+B|-|S_0|\) satisfies \[S_K=S_{K+1}=S_{K+2}=\cdots=:S_\infty,\qquad T(S_\infty)=S_\infty.\] The connected components or chordal cliques of the graph induced by \(S_\infty\) are the stabilized term blocks for this update rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any extensive monotone term-support refinement on a finite basis reaches a fixed support and hence a limiting block structure in finitely many steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Term-Block Stabilization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Finite stabilization and the stated strict-extension bound are correct. A source is still required for identifying components or chordal cliques of the limiting graph as the intended stabilized term blocks.

children.title: Parity-Symmetry Support Blocks

children.title: Parity-Block Structure
children.top_down_role: Monomial blocks induced by exponent parity classes.

assumptions_latex: \(A\subset\mathbb{N}^n\) is the joint support of the polynomial data.
\(B\subset\mathbb{N}^n\) is a finite Gram or moment basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Monomials in distinct equivalence classes cannot interact in an invariant Gram representation, so the Gram matrix may be chosen block diagonal by parity class.

notation.meaning: binary sign-symmetry space annihilating the support parities
equivalence of monomial exponents under all detected signs

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: character decomposition of a finite sign-symmetry group
needs a source specializing symmetry-adapted Gram matrices to polynomial support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block decomposition by characters of a binary sign-symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[G=\{s\in\mathbb F_2^n:s^{\mathsf T}(\alpha\bmod2)=0\text{ for every }\alpha\in A\}.\] For \(\beta,\gamma\in B\), put \(\beta\sim_G\gamma\) exactly when \(s^{\mathsf T}(\beta-\gamma)=0\) in \(\mathbb F_2\) for every \(s\in G\). The equivalence classes collect monomials carrying the same character under \(x_i\mapsto(-1)^{s_i}x_i\). Averaging any feasible Gram representation over \(G\) yields an equally feasible representation whose entries between distinct classes vanish; hence its matrix is block diagonal with these classes as blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detected sign symmetries partition monomials by binary characters, and symmetry averaging produces a Gram matrix that is block diagonal across those parity classes.
knowledge_statements.title: Parity-Block Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The character-class representation matches the parity-block leaf and is mathematically plausible, but the Gram-matrix averaging and block-diagonalization claim lacks a source specialized to polynomial support symmetries.

children.title: Sign-Symmetry Detection
children.top_down_role: Detection of invariant support classes before model construction.

assumptions_latex: \(A\subset\mathbb{N}^n\) is the union of supports of all polynomial data whose invariance must be preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed nullspace is exactly the group of coordinate sign changes leaving every supported monomial invariant.

notation.meaning: binary vector encoding a coordinate sign change

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invariance reduces directly to binary linear equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact detection of coordinate sign-flip symmetries from support parity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form a binary matrix \(M\) with one row \(\alpha\bmod2\) for each \(\alpha\in A\), and compute \[G=\ker_{\mathbb F_2}M.\] For each basis vector \(s\) of \(G\), record the transformation \(x_i\mapsto(-1)^{s_i}x_i\). A monomial transforms as \(x^\alpha\mapsto(-1)^{s^{\mathsf T}\alpha}x^\alpha\); therefore every recorded transformation fixes every term in the data. Output a basis of \(G\), or equivalently generators of the full coordinate sign-symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduce every support exponent modulo two and compute the binary nullspace; its vectors encode exactly the coordinate sign flips preserving all polynomial data.
knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Symmetry Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary-nullspace algorithm correctly detects coordinate sign changes fixing every supported monomial, and algorithm is the appropriate content kind. No polynomial symmetry-reduction source is provided.

children.title: Clique-First Term Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Term-sparsity decomposition performed within correlative cliques.

assumptions_latex: \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) cover the correlative sparsity graph.
Every polynomial datum is assigned to a clique containing all variables on which it depends.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output consists only of PSD blocks indexed by term cliques inside variable cliques, and no monomial mixes variables from different correlative cliques.

notation.meaning: local monomial basis for clique I_l

review_flags: needs a source specifying the clique-first combined correlative-term hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Term decomposition performed independently inside correlative variable cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input correlative cliques \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\), assigned polynomial supports, and relaxation order \(d\). For each \(\ell\), construct the local basis \(B_\ell=\{\beta\in\mathbb N^n:\operatorname{supp}(\beta)\subseteq I_\ell,\ |\beta|\leq d\}\). Build the term-interaction graph on \(B_\ell\), choose a chordal extension with maximal cliques \(C_{\ell r}\), and introduce one constraint \(Q_{\ell r}\succeq0\) per term clique. Match coefficients after summing all local clique contributions. Output the resulting two-level sparse Gram or moment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First split polynomial data by variable cliques, then construct and chordalize a separate monomial-interaction graph inside each clique.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-First Term Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique-first procedure matches the leaf, but no source fixes the combined hierarchy. The record also blends Gram and moment relaxations even though its coefficient-matching construction and PSD variables are specified only in Gram form.

children.title: Joint Variable-Support Refinement
children.top_down_role: Coupled refinement of variable and monomial block structures.

assumptions_latex: The candidate variable-edge set and every local term-edge set are finite.
Both variable and term update maps are extensive and monotone in all edge-set arguments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled iteration terminates at a simultaneous fixed point of the variable and term updates.

notation.meaning: family of local term-edge sets at iteration k

review_flags: abstract formulation pending a source defining the intended joint-refinement operators
exact polynomial-specific edge update is source-dependent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite coupled closure of variable and monomial interaction structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the variable graph \(E_V^0\) from joint variable occurrences and initialize \(E_T^0\) from supported exponent sums inside its cliques. Iterate \[E_V^{k+1}=\Phi_V(E_V^k,E_T^k),\qquad E_T^{k+1}=\Phi_T(E_V^{k+1},E_T^k),\] where \(\Phi_V\) adds variable interactions required by current term blocks and \(\Phi_T\) adds term interactions required by the updated variable cliques. Stop at the first \(K\) with \((E_V^{K+1},E_T^{K+1})=(E_V^K,E_T^K)\), and output the associated variable cliques and term blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately enlarge variable and monomial interaction graphs until neither level creates new interactions at the other level.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Variable-Support Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract alternating algorithm fits the leaf, but the polynomial-specific update maps and their fixed finite ambient edge sets are not defined. A source is needed to determine the intended coupled refinement and justify the fixed-point claim in that setting.

children.title: Two-Level Block Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Strength and size tradeoffs across correlative and term-sparsity levels.

assumptions_latex: Every block of decomposition \(\mathcal D_1\) is contained in a block of decomposition \(\mathcal D_2\).
Both decompositions use the same polynomial basis and coefficient-matching equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma(\mathcal D_1)\subseteq\Sigma(\mathcal D_2)\), so the denser decomposition gives no weaker SOS lower bound but generally requires larger PSD blocks.

notation.meaning: cone generated by SOS polynomials supported on blocks of D

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cone inclusion follows from nested block supports
needs a source documenting the combined-sparsity strength-size tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strength and matrix-size comparison for nested block decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a block family \(\mathcal D\), let \(\Sigma(\mathcal D)\) be the cone of sums of SOS polynomials, each represented on one block. If every block in \(\mathcal D_1\) lies in a block of \(\mathcal D_2\), then \[\Sigma(\mathcal D_1)\subseteq\Sigma(\mathcal D_2).\] Consequently, in a lower-bound relaxation \(f-\lambda\in\Sigma(\mathcal D)\), the optimum for \(\mathcal D_2\) is at least that for \(\mathcal D_1\). This gain is accompanied by block size \(b(\mathcal D_2)\geq b(\mathcal D_1)\) whenever the containment strictly merges a largest block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging nested variable or term blocks enlarges the sparse SOS cone and can strengthen bounds, but it generally increases the largest PSD constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Level Block Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-block cone inclusion and resulting lower-bound monotonicity are correctly stated, and property fits the tradeoff leaf. A source documenting this comparison for combined correlative-term sparsity is absent.

children.title: Support-Based Basis Pruning
children.top_down_role: Basis reduction using support geometry and closure structure.

assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) admits an SOS representation.
\(B\subset\mathbb N^n\) is a candidate basis containing the supports of all squared factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every exponent outside \(\tfrac12\operatorname{New}(p)\cap\mathbb N^n\) may be removed from \(B\) without destroying SOS representability.
review_flags: locator supports unconstrained SOS optimization; exact Newton-polytope basis theorem requires confirmation

source_refs.locator: 5.2 Unconstrained Polynomial Optimization p. 111

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p=\sum_j q_j^2\), then every squared factor satisfies \[\operatorname{supp}(q_j)\subseteq\tfrac12\operatorname{New}(p)\cap\mathbb N^n.\] Hence, from any candidate monomial basis \(B\), one may delete every \(\beta\) for which \(2\beta\notin\operatorname{New}(p)\). The remaining basis \(B'=B\cap(\tfrac12\operatorname{New}(p))\) still contains the support of each \(q_j\), so the same SOS polynomial has a Gram representation indexed by \(B'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOS factor needs only monomials whose doubled exponents lie in the polynomial's Newton polytope; all other candidate basis monomials can be pruned.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Based Basis Pruning

children.title: Coefficient-Kernel Pruning Calculus
children.top_down_role: Basis reduction using coefficient identities and nullspace information.

children.title: Coefficient-Identity Pruning
children.top_down_role: Basis removal supported by coefficient identities.

assumptions_latex: \(p=z_B^{\mathsf T}Qz_B\) with \(Q\succeq0\).
\(2\beta\) has the unique representation \(2\beta=\gamma+\delta\) with \(\gamma,\delta\in B\), namely \(\gamma=\delta=\beta\).
The coefficient of \(x^{2\beta}\) in \(p\) is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\beta\beta}=0\) and hence \(Q_{\beta\gamma}=0\) for every \(\gamma\in B\); therefore \(x^\beta\) can be removed from the Gram basis.
review_flags: exact coefficient-identity pruning lemma is not identified by the supplied locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique diagonal coefficient identity as a PSD pruning certificate.

source_refs.locator: 5.2 Unconstrained Polynomial Optimization p. 111
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Coefficient matching in \(p=z_B^{\mathsf T}Qz_B\) gives \[p_{2\beta}=\sum_{\gamma+\delta=2\beta}Q_{\gamma\delta}.\] Under the uniqueness assumption this identity reduces to \(p_{2\beta}=Q_{\beta\beta}\). Thus \(p_{2\beta}=0\) implies \(Q_{\beta\beta}=0\). Since \(Q\succeq0\), a zero diagonal entry forces the entire corresponding row and column to vanish. The monomial \(x^\beta\) therefore makes no contribution to the representation and is safely prunable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a missing coefficient corresponds uniquely to one Gram diagonal entry, PSD forces that entry's entire row and column to vanish, certifying basis removal.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Identity Pruning

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2 Unconstrained Polynomial Optimization p. 111

children.title: Kernel-Based Pruning
children.top_down_role: Basis removal supported by numerical or algebraic kernel information.

assumptions_latex: The Gram feasibility system is \(\mathcal A(Q)=c\) with \(Q\succeq0\).
There exist \(y\) and a nonzero vector \(v\) such that \(\mathcal A^*y=vv^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\langle y,c\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible \(Q\) satisfies \(Qv=0\), so the Gram representation may be restricted to \(v^\perp\).
review_flags: locator supports Gram formulations generally; facial or kernel pruning certificate requires exact sourcing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adjoint coefficient identity certifying a common Gram-matrix kernel.

source_refs.locator: 5.2 Unconstrained Polynomial Optimization p. 111
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every feasible \(Q\), the adjoint identity gives \[v^{\mathsf T}Qv=\langle vv^{\mathsf T},Q\rangle=\langle\mathcal A^*y,Q\rangle=\langle y,\mathcal A(Q)\rangle=\langle y,c\rangle=0.\] Positive semidefiniteness then implies \(Qv=0\). Thus \(v\) is a verifiable common kernel direction, and one may parameterize \(Q=URU^{\mathsf T}\), where the columns of \(U\) span \(v^\perp\) and \(R\succeq0\). If \(v\) is a coordinate vector, this removes the corresponding monomial directly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adjoint coefficient identity equal to a rank-one matrix can certify a kernel direction shared by every feasible PSD Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Based Pruning

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2 Unconstrained Polynomial Optimization p. 111

children.title: Joint Pruning Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of coefficient-based reductions with kernel-based reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Pruning Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for simultaneous coefficient-identity and Gram-kernel pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_B(x)\) be a finite monomial vector and let \(\mathcal A_B:\mathbb S^{|B|}\to\mathbb R^M\) map a Gram matrix to the coefficients of \(z_B(x)^\top Qz_B(x)\). Let \(U\in\mathbb R^{|B|\times r}\) have full column rank and let \(P:\mathbb R^M\to\mathbb R^J\) retain the coefficient identities imposed by the relaxation. The two pruning operations are jointly compatible for target coefficients \(c\) precisely when
\[\{R\succeq0:P\mathcal A_B(URU^\top)=Pc\}\neq\varnothing\]
and every discarded coefficient identity is implied on the restricted subspace:
\[P\mathcal A_B(URU^\top)=Pc\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal A_B(URU^\top)=c.\]
Under this condition, imposing both reductions preserves exactly the feasible Gram representations of the target polynomial within the kernel-restricted face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint pruning is compatible when the retained coefficient equations are feasible on the restricted Gram face and imply every discarded coefficient equation there.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb N^n\) is finite.
\(U\) has full column rank.
\(c\in\mathbb R^M\) is the target coefficient vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{URU^\top:R\succeq0,\ P\mathcal A_B(URU^\top)=Pc\}=\{Q\succeq0:Q=URU^\top,\ \mathcal A_B(Q)=c\}.\)

notation.meaning: Gram-to-coefficient linear map for the monomial basis
basis matrix for the retained Gram subspace

review_flags: Exact joint-pruning formulation needs a source specific to coefficient-kernel pruning.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is plausible and fits the leaf, but its precise necessity-and-sufficiency formulation for combined coefficient and kernel pruning has no cited support.

children.title: Adaptive Basis Enrichment
children.top_down_role: Repair and enlargement of initially reduced bases.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Basis Enrichment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repair loop for a monomial basis that is initially too small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a polynomial optimization relaxation order \(d\), an initial monomial set \(B_0\subseteq\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:|\alpha|\le d\}\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), set \(k=0\). Solve the relaxation constructed from \(B_k\). If it is feasible and its coefficient residual and dual-separation residual do not exceed \(\varepsilon\), return \(B_k\) and the relaxation solution. Otherwise, select at least one omitted exponent implicated by a violated coefficient identity, a separating dual functional, or a required product support, form \(E_k\) from those exponents and any closure exponents required by the relaxation, and update
\[B_{k+1}=B_k\cup E_k.\]
Stop with failure only when \(B_k\) is the full degree-bounded basis and the residual test still fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve on a reduced monomial basis, add omitted monomials identified by residual or separation tests, enforce required closure, and stop after certification or full-basis exhaustion.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb N\) fixes a finite ambient monomial basis.
\(B_0\) contains all monomials mandated by normalization.
\(\varepsilon>0\) is the acceptance tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_0\subseteq B_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\{\alpha:|\alpha|\le d\}\), so the enrichment loop terminates after finitely many strict enlargements.

notation.meaning: monomial basis at enrichment iteration k
new exponents and required closure exponents

review_flags: Selection oracle and closure rule vary across sparse SOS methods; a method-specific source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the container, but the residual tests, exponent-selection oracle, and closure rule are method-dependent and insufficiently specified without a source.

children.title: Equality Elimination
children.top_down_role: Coordinate reduction obtained from polynomial equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination by polynomial parametrization of an equality variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to polynomial equalities \(h_i(x)=0\) and inequalities \(g_j(x)\ge0\). Suppose a polynomial map \(\phi:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^n\) and a set \(T\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) satisfy
\[\phi(T)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_i(x)=0\ \forall i,\ g_j(x)\ge0\ \forall j\}.\]
Then equality elimination replaces the original problem exactly by
\[\inf_{t\in T} f(\phi(t)),\]
with inequalities \(g_j(\phi(t))\ge0\) included in the description of \(T\) when they are not already encoded. Feasible points and objective values are preserved through \(x=\phi(t)\); injectivity of \(\phi\) is unnecessary for equality of infima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parametrization whose image is exactly the feasible equality variety eliminates those equalities while preserving all feasible objective values and the infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h_i,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(\phi\) is polynomial and its image of \(T\) equals the original feasible set.

children.title: Quotient-Ring Coordinates
children.top_down_role: Coordinate models formed modulo an equality ideal.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Ring Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinates of polynomial classes modulo equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_m\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be the ideal generated by polynomial equality constraints. The quotient ring is
\[\mathbb R[x]/I=\{[p]_I:p\in\mathbb R[x]\},\qquad [p]_I=[q]_I\ \Longleftrightarrow\ p-q\in I.\]
For a chosen vector-space basis \(\mathcal B=([b_\beta]_I)_{\beta\in\Lambda}\) of the quotient, the quotient-ring coordinates of \([p]_I\) are the unique scalars \((a_\beta)_{\beta\in\Lambda}\), with finite support, satisfying
\[[p]_I=\sum_{\beta\in\Lambda}a_\beta[b_\beta]_I.\]
Thus equality-equivalent polynomials receive identical coordinates; when the quotient is infinite-dimensional, only the degree-truncated coordinate space used by a relaxation is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quotient-ring coordinates express a polynomial class modulo the equality ideal in a chosen basis, assigning identical coordinates to polynomials differing by an ideal element.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is an ideal of \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\).
\(\mathcal B\) is a vector-space basis of \(\mathbb R[x]/I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([p]_I=[q]_I\) if and only if \(p\) and \(q\) have the same coordinates in \(\mathcal B\).

notation.meaning: residue class of p modulo I

review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers quotient-ring coordinates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a mathematically standard definition with consistent finite-support qualifications, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Normal-Form Basis Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduced polynomial bases represented through ideal normal forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Form Basis Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gröbner normal forms as canonical reduced polynomial coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a monomial order and a Gröbner basis \(G\) of an ideal \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\). Let \(\operatorname{Std}(I)\) be the monomials not divisible by any leading monomial of \(G\). Every polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) has a unique remainder
\[\operatorname{NF}_G(p)=\sum_{\alpha\in\operatorname{Std}(I)}c_\alpha x^\alpha,\qquad p-\operatorname{NF}_G(p)\in I.\]
Consequently, replacing each polynomial in an equality-constrained relaxation by its normal form removes monomials reducible modulo \(I\) without changing its residue class. At relaxation degree \(d\), the retained basis consists of the standard monomials actually occurring in the required normal forms, subject to the degree convention adopted after reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gröbner basis gives each polynomial a unique remainder supported on standard monomials, permitting removal of monomials reducible modulo the equality ideal.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a Gröbner basis of \(I\) for the fixed monomial order.
\(p\in\mathbb R[x]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([p]_I=[\operatorname{NF}_G(p)]_I\), and \(\operatorname{NF}_G(p)\) is supported on \(\operatorname{Std}(I)\).

notation.meaning: normal form of p with respect to G
standard monomials of the leading-term ideal

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the Gröbner normal-form statement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gröbner normal-form representation is standard and fits the leaf, but the record supplies no source locator supporting the canonical-remainder and basis-reduction claims.

children.title: Quotient Reduction Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where quotient preprocessing preserves the intended optimization model.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient Reduction Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of replacing equality-constrained polynomials by quotient representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reduction modulo \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_m\rangle\) preserves polynomial values on the real equality set because \(p-q\in I\) implies \(p(x)=q(x)\) whenever \(h(x)=0\). The converse generally fails: equality on the real variety implies only \(p-q\in I(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\), not necessarily \(p-q\in I\). Moreover, a degree-truncated SOS or moment cone need not be invariant under arbitrary replacement by congruent representatives, since normal-form reduction can change degrees and multiplier spaces. Therefore quotient reduction is exact for algebraic identities modulo \(I\), but preservation of a finite relaxation requires compatible truncation and reduction of every objective, constraint, multiplier, and moment relation used by that relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Congruence modulo the equality ideal preserves values on its variety, but finite SOS relaxations may change unless truncation, multipliers, and all polynomial data are reduced compatibly.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_m\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\).
The optimization model enforces \(h_i(x)=0\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p-q\in I\Rightarrow p|_{V_{\mathbb R}(I)}=q|_{V_{\mathbb R}(I)}\), while the reverse implication and invariance of degree-truncated relaxation cones require additional hypotheses.

notation.meaning: real variety of the ideal I
ideal of polynomials vanishing on the real variety

review_flags: A source is needed for truncation-compatible quotient reduction and its precise failure boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic implication is standard, but the claims about invariance and compatible reduction of finite SOS or moment relaxations require a specific source.

children.title: Redundant-Constraint Management
children.top_down_role: Selection and localization of redundant constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Constraint Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe removal and localization of constraints in polynomial optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a basic semialgebraic set
\[K=\{x:h_i(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\ge0\},\]
a constraint \(g_k(x)\ge0\) is redundant when it is implied by the remaining constraints, equivalently when
\[\inf\{g_k(x):h_i(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\ge0\ \text{for }j\ne k\}\ge0.\]
Deleting a certified redundant constraint preserves \(K\) and hence preserves the original polynomial optimization problem. It need not preserve a fixed-order moment or SOS relaxation, because the removed constraint also removes its localizing-matrix condition. Consequently, finite-order deletion is safe only after separately establishing that the omitted localizing condition is implied by the retained relaxation constraints at that order; otherwise the constraint should remain or be localized selectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A logically implied constraint may be removed from the original problem, but its finite-order SOS localizing condition requires a separate implication certificate before deletion.

The redundancy test is evaluated over the feasible set defined by all other constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{-k}=K\) when \(\inf_{x\in K_{-k}}g_k(x)\ge0\), but equality of fixed-order relaxation feasible sets requires an additional conic implication.

children.title: Facial-Rank Reduction Calculus

children.title: Exposed-Face Reduction
children.top_down_role: Restriction of conic models to structurally identified exposed faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Exposed-Face Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a conic relaxation to a face exposed by a dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space and let \(W\in K^*\). The set
\[F=K\cap W^\perp=\{X\in K:\langle W,X\rangle=0\}\]
is an exposed face of \(K\). If every feasible point of a conic relaxation satisfies \(\langle W,X\rangle=0\), then replacing \(X\in K\) by \(X\in F\) preserves its feasible set and objective values. For \(K=\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(W\in\mathbb S_+^n\), let \(r=\dim(\ker W)\) and let \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(U)=\ker W\). Then
\[F=\{URU^\top:R\in\mathbb S_+^r\},\]
so substituting \(X=URU^\top\) yields an equivalent lower-dimensional positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual exposing vector confines every feasible conic point to an exposed face; for the positive-semidefinite cone, that face has a smaller Gram parametrization over the kernel of the exposing matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
\(W\in K^*\) and every feasible \(X\) satisfies \(\langle W,X\rangle=0\).
For the positive-semidefinite formula, \(K=\mathbb S_+^n\), \(W\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{range}(U)=\ker W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\cap W^\perp\Longleftrightarrow \exists R\in\mathbb S_+^r\text{ such that }X=URU^\top\), where \(r=\dim(\ker W)\).

notation.meaning: hyperplane orthogonal to the exposing vector
basis matrix for the kernel of W
dimension of the kernel of W

children.title: Kernel-Induced Face Detection
children.top_down_role: Face identification using kernel information from conic blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Induced Face Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel vectors certify a proper face containing a PSD feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\) be the feasible matrix set of a semidefinite relaxation. Suppose a matrix \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times s}\) with full column rank satisfies
\[XV=0\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal F.\]
Then \(W=VV^\top\succeq0\) is a verifiable exposing certificate because
\[\langle W,X\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(V^\top XV)=0\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal F.\]
Hence all feasible matrices lie in the face
\[F_V=\{X\succeq0:XV=0\}=\mathbb S_+^n\cap W^\perp.\]
If \(s>0\), this is a proper face. The certificate is valid only when the universal kernel relation follows exactly from the relaxation constraints or another exact certificate, not merely from a numerically small eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common exact kernel of all feasible PSD matrices yields an exposing matrix and certifies a proper face; approximate numerical kernels alone do not suffice.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\).
\(V\) has full column rank and \(XV=0\) for every \(X\in\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\subseteq F_V=\{X\succeq0:XV=0\}=\mathbb S_+^n\cap(VV^\top)^\perp.\)

notation.meaning: matrix whose columns span the certified common kernel
kernel-induced face of the PSD cone

children.title: Low-Rank Cone Restriction
children.top_down_role: Reduction to lower-dimensional conic structure suggested by rank profiles.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Cone Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced PSD parametrization after a common kernel has been certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times s}\) have full column rank, and let \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), where \(r=n-s\), have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker(V^\top)\). The kernel-restricted positive-semidefinite face admits the bijective representation
\[\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:XV=0\}=\{URU^\top:R\in\mathbb S_+^r\}.\]
The inverse coordinate map is \(R=U^\top XU\). Therefore a conic relaxation whose feasible matrices all satisfy \(XV=0\) may substitute \(X=URU^\top\), transform each linear matrix functional accordingly, and replace an order-\(n\) PSD variable by an order-\(r\) PSD variable without changing feasibility or objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After certifying a common kernel, every feasible PSD matrix has a unique smaller PSD coordinate matrix, allowing an equivalent lower-order cone restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times s}\) has full column rank.
\(U^\top U=I_r\) and \(\operatorname{range}(U)=\ker(V^\top)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\succeq0,\ XV=0\Longleftrightarrow \exists!R\succeq0\text{ such that }X=URU^\top.\)

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis of the retained subspace

children.title: Reduction Degeneracy Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Degeneracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: When facial reduction is unsafe, incomplete, or numerically unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A PSD face restriction \(X=URU^\top\) is exact only when \(\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(U)\) holds for every feasible \(X\). If the discarded direction is inferred solely from an approximate kernel, there may exist a feasible \(X\succeq0\) with \(v^\top Xv>0\), and enforcing \(Xv=0\) then removes feasible points. Conversely, an exposing certificate may identify a face that still lacks a relative-interior feasible point; further facial-reduction steps can be required. Numerically, nearly dependent exposing vectors or an ill-conditioned basis \(U\) can amplify residuals in transformed constraints. Thus exact universal kernel certificates, rank-revealing tolerances, and a relative-interior or termination test delimit reliable reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial reduction can delete feasible points when based on approximate kernels, can require repeated exposure, and can become unstable when exposing directions or reduced bases are ill-conditioned.
assumptions_latex: The original cone is \(\mathbb S_+^n\).
A proposed restriction uses a retained subspace \(\operatorname{range}(U)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists X\in\mathcal F\text{ with }\operatorname{range}(X)\nsubseteq\operatorname{range}(U)\Rightarrow\{R\succeq0:URU^\top\in\mathcal F\}\) is not an exact representation of \(\mathcal F\).

notation.meaning: basis of the proposed retained subspace

children.title: Variable Scaling

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible diagonal-affine scaling of polynomial optimization variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a polynomial optimization problem have variable \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), objective \(f(x)\), and feasible set \(K\). Choose \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\), and set
\[x=a+Dy.\]
Define \(\widetilde f(y)=f(a+Dy)\) and \(\widetilde K=\{y:a+Dy\in K\}\). Then the affine map is bijective and
\[\inf_{x\in K}f(x)=\inf_{y\in\widetilde K}\widetilde f(y).\]
Polynomial objectives and constraints remain polynomial after substitution. For bounded coordinates \(\ell_i<u_i\), taking \(a_i=(u_i+\ell_i)/2\) and \(d_i=(u_i-\ell_i)/2\) maps each interval exactly to \([-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular diagonal-affine change of variables preserves the optimization problem exactly and can normalize bounded coordinate intervals to the unit box.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is diagonal with \(d_i\ne0\) for every \(i\).
The original objective and constraints are polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto y=D^{-1}(x-a)\) bijects \(K\) with \(\widetilde K\) and preserves corresponding objective values.

children.title: Domain Normalization
children.top_down_role: Transformations placing feasible domains into numerically favorable ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine normalization of a nondegenerate polynomial optimization box to the unit box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\}\), where \(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i\). Define \(c_i=(u_i+\ell_i)/2\), \(s_i=(u_i-\ell_i)/2\), and \(x=c+Sz\), with \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\). Then \(z\mapsto c+Sz\) is a bijection from \([-1,1]^n\) onto \(K\). For every polynomial \(p\), the transformed polynomial \(\widehat p(z)=p(c+Sz)\) satisfies \(\deg \widehat p\le\deg p\). Consequently, polynomial objectives and constraints transformed by this substitution have corresponding feasible points and the same optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine substitution maps any nondegenerate box to the unit box while preserving feasibility, optimal value, and polynomial degree.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\ell_i<u_i\) for all \(i\).
All objective and constraint functions being transformed are polynomials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=c+Sz\) bijectively maps \([-1,1]^n\) to \(K\) and yields an equivalent polynomial optimization problem.
review_flags: Exact supporting locator for affine polynomial domain normalization is absent from the supplied inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically precise, correctly delimited, and well matched to Domain Normalization, but no source reference or inspectable locator supports the affine normalization and optimization-equivalence claims.

children.title: Geometry-Aware Scaling

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Aware Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ellipsoidal coordinate scaling determined by a positive-definite geometric model of the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:(x-c)^{\mathsf T}H(x-c)\le1\}\), where \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). Geometry-aware ellipsoidal scaling is the substitution \(x=c+H^{-1/2}z\). It maps the Euclidean unit ball \(\{z:\|z\|_2\le1\}\) bijectively onto \(E\). For a polynomial \(p\), the scaled polynomial is \(\widehat p(z)=p(c+H^{-1/2}z)\); it has degree at most \(\deg p\). Unlike coordinatewise scaling, the transformation may rotate and mix variables to reflect the domain's principal directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite ellipsoidal model supplies an affine transformation that maps the unit ball onto the modeled domain and respects its principal directions.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
A fixed symmetric positive-definite square root \(H^{1/2}\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=c+H^{-1/2}z\) maps the unit ball bijectively onto \(E\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports ellipsoidal geometry-aware polynomial scaling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the geometry-aware scaling container and correctly states the ellipsoidal bijection and degree behavior, but it has no supporting source or locator.

children.title: Scaling Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric or numerical regimes where scaling degrades the model.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of invertibility or uniform conditioning under degenerate or highly anisotropic coordinate ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For box scaling \(x=c+Sz\), let \(S=\operatorname{diag}(w_1/2,\ldots,w_n/2)\), where \(w_i=u_i-\ell_i\). If some \(w_i=0\), then \(S\) is singular and no bijective full-dimensional normalization exists. If every \(w_i>0\), then \(\kappa_2(S)=\max_i w_i/\min_i w_i\). Hence, along any family of boxes for which \(\min_i w_i/\max_i w_i\to0\), the scaling becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned. Diagonal normalization therefore cannot provide a uniform conditioning bound for degenerate or increasingly anisotropic domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Box scaling fails to be invertible at zero width and becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned as the ratio of largest to smallest width diverges.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) with widths \(w_i=u_i-\ell_i\ge0\).
Conditioning is measured in the Euclidean operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is singular if some \(w_i=0\); otherwise \(\kappa_2(S)=\max_iw_i/\min_iw_i\).
review_flags: A source explicitly treating these scaling failure regimes was not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification is appropriate and the singularity and spectral-condition-number statements are correct, but the record supplies no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Coefficient Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Balancing of polynomial and conic-model coefficient magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating diagonal balancing of nonzero polynomial coefficient rows and monomial columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a coefficient matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times N}\), tolerance \(\tau>1\), and iteration limit \(K\). Initialize \(R=I_m\), \(C=I_N\), and \(B=A\). At each iteration, set \(r_i=1/\max_j|B_{ij}|\) for every nonzero row and replace \(B\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(r)B\), \(R\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(r)R\). Then set \(c_j=1/\max_i|B_{ij}|\) for every nonzero column and replace \(B\leftarrow B\operatorname{diag}(c)\), \(C\leftarrow C\operatorname{diag}(c)\). Stop when all nonzero row and column maxima lie in \([\tau^{-1},\tau]\), or after \(K\) iterations; output \((B,R,C)\), where \(B=RAC\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating positive row and column scalings balance the nonzero coefficient magnitudes, returning the equilibrated matrix and its diagonal transformations.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite polynomial or conic-model coefficient matrix.
Zero rows and columns are left unchanged.
\(\tau>1\) and \(K\in\mathbb N\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs diagonal \(R,C\) and an equilibrated matrix \(B=RAC\).

notation.meaning: Accumulated diagonal row and column scalings.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate content kind for the stated iterative procedure, but no source supports this particular max-norm update rule, stopping test, or the description of the iteration-limited output as equilibrated. children.title: Orthogonal Polynomial Bases
children.top_down_role: Univariate or multivariate orthogonal coordinates for polynomial models.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal Polynomial Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-degree polynomial bases orthogonal under a domain-supported measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mu\) be a positive measure on \(K\) having finite moments through degree \(2d\), and let \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le d}\) be the polynomials of total degree at most \(d\). A family \(\{\phi_\alpha\}_{|\alpha|\le d}\) is an orthogonal polynomial basis relative to \(\mu\) if it spans \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le d}\) and \(\int_K\phi_\alpha(x)\phi_\beta(x)\,d\mu(x)=0\) whenever \(\alpha\ne\beta\). It is orthonormal if the same integral equals \(\delta_{\alpha\beta}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonal polynomial basis spans the finite-degree polynomial space and has pairwise zero inner products under a chosen positive measure.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu\) is positive and has finite moments through degree \(2d\).
The polynomial inner product is nondegenerate on \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le d}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\phi_\alpha\}_{|\alpha|\le d}\) is orthogonal exactly when it spans \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le d}\) and its distinct elements are \(L^2(\mu)\)-orthogonal.

notation.meaning: Positive measure defining the polynomial inner product.
Basis polynomial indexed by a multi-index.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly addresses orthogonal polynomial bases.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits Orthogonal Polynomial Bases, including the needed nondegeneracy assumption, but no source reference or locator is provided.

children.title: Tensor-Product Polynomial Bases
children.top_down_role: Product-structured bases for multivariable polynomial computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Tensor-Product Polynomial Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multivariate bases formed as coordinatewise products of univariate polynomial bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each coordinate \(i\), let \(\{\phi_{i,k}:0\le k\le d_i\}\) be a basis of univariate polynomials of degree at most \(d_i\). For \(\alpha\in\prod_{i=1}^n\{0,\ldots,d_i\}\), define \(\Phi_\alpha(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n\phi_{i,\alpha_i}(x_i)\). Then \(\{\Phi_\alpha\}\) is the tensor-product polynomial basis of the coordinatewise-degree space \(\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\mathbb R[x_i]_{\le d_i}\). If each univariate family is orthonormal for \(\mu_i\), then the tensor-product family is orthonormal for the product measure \(\mu_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mu_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Products of coordinatewise univariate basis functions form a multivariate tensor-product basis and inherit orthonormality under the product measure.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\{\phi_{i,k}\}_{k=0}^{d_i}\) is a univariate polynomial basis.
For the orthonormality claim, every family is orthonormal in \(L^2(\mu_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\Phi_\alpha\}\) spans the tensor-product polynomial space and is orthonormal under \(\bigotimes_i\mu_i\) when its factors are orthonormal.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports tensor-product polynomial bases.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes a coordinatewise-degree tensor-product space from a total-degree space and states the product-measure orthonormality claim accurately, but it lacks a source and locator.

children.title: Symmetry-Adapted Polynomial Bases
children.top_down_role: Polynomial coordinates aligned with invariant subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Adapted Polynomial Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-space decomposition into invariant isotypic components for a finite group action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act linearly on a finite-dimensional polynomial space \(V\) through \(T_g p=p\circ g^{-1}\). For each irreducible complex character \(\chi_\rho\) of degree \(d_\rho\), define \(P_\rho=(d_\rho/|G|)\sum_{g\in G}\chi_\rho(g^{-1})T_g\). Then \(P_\rho\) is the projector onto the \(\rho\)-isotypic component, the projectors are mutually orthogonal idempotents, and \(V=\bigoplus_\rho P_\rho V\). A polynomial basis obtained by concatenating bases of the nonzero spaces \(P_\rho V\) is symmetry-adapted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Character projectors decompose an invariant polynomial space into isotypic components; bases chosen componentwise form a symmetry-adapted basis.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts linearly on a finite-dimensional complex polynomial space \(V\).
\(V\) is invariant under every operator \(T_g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V=\bigoplus_\rho P_\rho V\), and componentwise bases constitute a symmetry-adapted polynomial basis.

notation.meaning: Polynomial representation operator induced by group element g.
Irreducible character indexed by representation rho.

review_flags: No supplied source locator covers finite-group symmetry adaptation of polynomial bases.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate content kind, and the character-projector construction matches the symmetry-adapted basis container. However, the complex representation convention and the claim that the projectors are orthogonal require an authoritative source and a specified invariant inner product if orthogonality is meant analytically rather than algebraically.

children.title: Polynomial Basis Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Numerical conditioning considerations across structured basis families.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Basis Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning of coefficient-to-polynomial conversion under a measure-induced norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_N\) be a basis of a polynomial space with inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\), and let \(G_{ij}=\langle\phi_i,\phi_j\rangle\). For every coefficient vector \(a\in\mathbb R^N\), the polynomial \(p=\sum_i a_i\phi_i\) satisfies \(\|p\|^2=a^{\mathsf T}Ga\). If \(G\) is positive definite, then \(\lambda_{\min}(G)\|a\|_2^2\le\|p\|^2\le\lambda_{\max}(G)\|a\|_2^2\). Thus the coefficient-to-polynomial map has condition number \(\sqrt{\kappa_2(G)}\); an orthonormal basis has \(G=I\) and condition number one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basis Gram matrix controls coefficient-to-polynomial norm distortion; orthonormal bases are perfectly conditioned in the defining norm.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_N\) are linearly independent.
The inner product is positive definite on their span.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient map has norm condition number \(\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(G)/\lambda_{\min}(G)}\).

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of the polynomial basis.
Spectral condition number of the Gram matrix.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the basis-conditioning formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly relates the Gram matrix to the norm condition number of the coefficient-to-polynomial map and fits the terminal container, but no supporting source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Moment Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-matrix blocks indexed only by monomials supported on one variable clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be a variable clique and let \(y^I=(y^I_\gamma)\) be a truncated sequence indexed by multi-indices supported in \(I\) with degree at most \(2d\). The order-\(d\) local moment block is the symmetric matrix \(M_d^I(y^I)\), indexed by \(\alpha,\beta\) supported in \(I\) with \(|\alpha|,|\beta|\le d\), whose entries are \([M_d^I(y^I)]_{\alpha,\beta}=y^I_{\alpha+\beta}\). If \(y^I\) is represented by a positive measure, then \(M_d^I(y^I)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local moment block uses only moments and monomial indices supported on one clique; representable local sequences produce positive-semidefinite blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(y^I\) contains all clique-supported moments through degree \(2d\).
