knowledge_statements.title: Localizing Constraint Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-local localizing matrices encoding polynomial inequality constraints in truncated moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x_I)=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma x^\gamma\) be supported on clique \(I\), let \(\delta=\deg g\), and suppose \(y^I\) is available through degree \(2d\). Set \(r=d-\lceil\delta/2\rceil\). The localizing constraint block is the matrix \(M_r^I(g\,y^I)\), indexed by clique-supported \(\alpha,\beta\) with \(|\alpha|,|\beta|\le r\), and defined by \([M_r^I(g\,y^I)]_{\alpha,\beta}=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma y^I_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}\). If \(y^I\) has a representing measure supported where \(g\ge0\), then \(M_r^I(g\,y^I)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localizing block weights clique moments by a clique-supported constraint polynomial; support on the constraint set implies positive semidefiniteness.
assumptions_latex: \(g\in\mathbb R[x_I]\) and \(\deg g=\delta\le2d\).
\(y^I\) contains clique-supported moments through degree \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([M_r^I(g\,y^I)]_{\alpha,\beta}=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma y^I_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}\), with positivity under a representing measure supported on \(\{g\ge0\}\).

children.title: Clique Block Indexing
children.top_down_role: Assignment of monomials and constraints to local blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Block Indexing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monomial indexing convention for clique-local moment and localizing matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a clique \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and degree \(d\), define \(\mathcal A_d(I)=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq I,\ |\alpha|\le d\}\). Fix a total order on \(\mathcal A_d(I)\), such as graded lexicographic order, and let \(v_d^I(x)=(x^\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_d(I)}\) in that order. A clique block uses rows and columns indexed by \(\mathcal A_d(I)\); its entry associated with \((\alpha,\beta)\) references the moment labeled by \(\alpha+\beta\). The block dimension is \(|\mathcal A_d(I)|=\binom{|I|+d}{d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique blocks are indexed by bounded-degree monomials supported on that clique, giving a block size determined only by clique cardinality and degree.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(d\in\mathbb N\).
A fixed total order is used consistently within each block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rows and columns are indexed by \(\mathcal A_d(I)\), and the block size is \(\binom{|I|+d}{d}\).

notation.meaning: Clique-supported multi-indices of degree at most d.
Coordinates where the multi-index is nonzero.

children.title: Local Block Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility requirements across local moment and localizing structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Block Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality of duplicated truncated moments on intersections of variable cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I,J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be cliques with local truncated moment sequences \(y^I\) and \(y^J\), each defined through degree \(2d\). The two local blocks are overlap-compatible through order \(2d\) if \(y^I_\alpha=y^J_\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\) satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq I\cap J\) and \(|\alpha|\le2d\). A family \(\{y^{I_k}\}_{k=1}^q\) is locally compatible when this equality holds for every pair of cliques, or equivalently for every tested edge of a clique tree when the running-intersection structure is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local moment blocks are compatible when every duplicated moment supported on a clique overlap has the same value in both blocks.
assumptions_latex: Each local sequence contains all moments through degree \(2d\) supported on its clique.
For edge-only testing, the cliques are organized as a running-intersection clique tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^I_\alpha=y^J_\alpha\) for all \(\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq I\cap J\) with \(|\alpha|\le2d\).

notation.meaning: Truncated moment sequences attached to cliques I and J.

review_flags: A source for overlap consistency and the running-intersection edge reduction is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct content kind, and pairwise equality of overlap moments is precisely stated. The stronger equivalence between all-pair compatibility and testing clique-tree edges under the running-intersection property requires a specific supporting source and locator.

children.title: Overlap-Consistency Models
children.top_down_role: Coupling of shared marginal information across cliques.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlap-Consistency Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for truncated clique-local moment sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the variable cliques be \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(y^{(k)}=(y^{(k)}_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^{I_k},\,|\alpha|\le 2d_k}\) be the truncated moment sequence for clique \(I_k\). The family is overlap-consistent when, for every pair \(k,\ell\) and every multi-index \(\alpha\) supported in \(I_k\cap I_\ell\) with \(|\alpha|\le 2\min\{d_k,d_\ell\}\), one has \[y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(\ell)}_\alpha.\] Thus all clique models assign the same truncated moments to every monomial representable on their common variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique-local moment sequences are overlap-consistent when they assign identical values to every shared monomial available at both truncation orders.
assumptions_latex: \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\).
\(d_k\in\mathbb N\) and each \(y^{(k)}\) contains moments through degree \(2d_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(\ell)}_\alpha\) on every common supported monomial within both truncations.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Localization Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible assignments of polynomial constraints to clique-local blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\), a constraint-localization assignment chooses a nonempty set \(A_j\subseteq\{k:\operatorname{supp}(g_j)\subseteq I_k\}\) for every \(j\). At local order \(d_k\), each assignment \(k\in A_j\) imposes \[M_{d_k-\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil}(g_jy^{(k)})\succeq0.\] A valid redundant inequality \(b(x)\ge0\) may likewise be placed in any clique containing \(\operatorname{supp}(b)\). Single-placement, replicated-placement, and redundant-bound variants differ only through these assignment sets and added valid inequalities.

children.title: Clique SOS Certificate Blocks

knowledge_statements.title: Clique SOS Certificate Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order sparse nonnegativity certificate assembled from clique-local SOS blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_j\) assign each constraint \(g_j\) to compatible cliques. A clique-block certificate of order \(d\) for the lower bound \(\gamma\) is the polynomial identity \[f-\gamma=\sum_{k=1}^m\left(\sigma_{0k}+\sum_{j:\,k\in A_j}\sigma_{jk}g_j\right),\] where every \(\sigma_{0k},\sigma_{jk}\in\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\) is a sum of squares, \(\deg(\sigma_{0k})\le2d\), and \(\deg(\sigma_{jk}g_j)\le2d\). Because every summand is nonnegative on \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\), the identity is directly verifiable and certifies \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial lower bound is certified by expressing its residual as a sum of clique-local SOS multipliers times localized constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(g_j)\subseteq I_k\) whenever \(k\in A_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in K\).

children.title: Moment–SOS Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between local moment models and clique SOS certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment–SOS Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order SDP duality between sparse moment constraints and clique SOS certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(f=\sum_k f_k\) with \(f_k\in\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\). At order \(d\), minimize \(\sum_k L_{y^{(k)}}(f_k)\) over normalized clique moment sequences satisfying their moment matrices, assigned localizing matrices, and overlap-consistency equalities. Its semidefinite dual maximizes \(\gamma\) subject to an order-\(d\) clique SOS identity for \(f-\gamma\). Weak duality always gives \(\gamma\le\sum_k L_{y^{(k)}}(f_k)\). If either SDP has a strictly feasible point and both optimal values are finite, conic strong duality yields \[\rho_d^{\mathrm{mom}}=\rho_d^{\mathrm{SOS}},\] with attainment on the opposite side under the usual finite-dimensional SDP duality conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The clique-local moment relaxation and clique SOS certificate problem form an SDP primal-dual pair and have equal values under strict feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(f=\sum_k f_k\) with \(f_k\in\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\).
The order-\(d\) primal and dual SDPs are finite-dimensional.
At least one side is strictly feasible and both values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{mom}}=\rho_d^{\mathrm{SOS}}\).

notation.meaning: Linear moment functional for clique k.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Quadratic-Module Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse positivity cone obtained by summing clique-local quadratic modules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each clique \(I_k\), let \(J_k\) index constraints whose supports lie in \(I_k\). The sparse quadratic module generated by these localized constraints is \[Q_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)=\sum_{k=1}^m\left\{\sigma_{0k}+\sum_{j\in J_k}\sigma_{jk}g_j:\ \sigma_{0k},\sigma_{jk}\in\Sigma[x_{I_k}]\right\}.\] Its order-\(d\) truncation additionally requires \(\deg(\sigma_{0k})\le2d\) and \(\deg(\sigma_{jk}g_j)\le2d\). Membership of \(f-\gamma\) in the truncation supplies a clique-structured SOS lower-bound certificate without introducing products of distinct constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sparse quadratic module sums local SOS multipliers and individual localized constraints over the variable cliques.

\(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\).

children.title: Sparse Degree Bounds
children.top_down_role: Certificate-degree bounds controlled by sparse structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Degree Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-complexity measure for membership in a truncated sparse positivity cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_d\) be the order-\(d\) truncation of a fixed sparse quadratic module or sparse preordering, with \(C_d\subseteq C_{d+1}\). For a polynomial \(p\) admitting a sparse certificate, define its sparse certificate order by \[B_C(p)=\min\{d\in\mathbb N:p\in C_d\}.\] For a class \(\mathcal P\), a sparse degree bound is a function \(D\) of specified numerical and structural data such that \(B_C(p)\le D(p)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal P\). Equivalently, all SOS-weighted clique products in the resulting certificate have total degree at most \(2D(p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse degree bound controls the least relaxation order required to represent a polynomial in a truncated sparse positivity cone.
assumptions_latex: \(C_d\subseteq C_{d+1}\) for all \(d\in\mathbb N\).
\(p\in\bigcup_{d\in\mathbb N}C_d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_C(p)\le D(p)\), hence a certificate exists with term degrees at most \(2D(p)\).

notation.meaning: Minimum sparse certificate order of p.
Degree-bound function on the chosen polynomial class.

children.title: Local Convergence Rates
children.top_down_role: Rate behavior governed by clique-local relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Convergence Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation-gap rate induced by a degree bound near the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\), and let \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in C_d\}\). Suppose constants \(C>0\), \(a>0\), and \(\varepsilon_0>0\) satisfy \[B_C(f-f^*+\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{-a}\qquad(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0).\] Then every integer \(d\ge C\varepsilon_0^{-a}\) satisfies \[0\le f^*-\rho_d\le\left(\frac{C}{d}\right)^{1/a}.\] Thus a polynomial certificate-order bound in the inverse positivity margin yields an explicit local convergence rate for the sparse lower-bound hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If certificate order grows at most polynomially in the inverse optimality tolerance, the sparse relaxation gap decays at the reciprocal polynomial rate.
assumptions_latex: \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\) is finite.
\(C_d\subseteq C_{d+1}\) and \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in C_d\}\).
\(B_C(f-f^*+\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{-a}\) for \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f^*-\rho_d\le(C/d)^{1/a}\) for \(d\ge C\varepsilon_0^{-a}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inversion from a certificate-order estimate to the displayed gap rate is coherent, but no source supports the assumed sparse degree estimate or identifies a hierarchy for which it holds.

children.title: Structural Rate Parameters

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Rate Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem data on which a uniform sparse certificate-rate estimate may depend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a clique decomposition and a polynomial \(p>0\) on \(K\), define the structural rate tuple \[\theta=(\omega,q,\delta,R,\eta),\qquad \omega=\max_k|I_k|,\quad q=\max_k|J_k|,\quad \delta=\max_j\deg(g_j),\quad \eta=\min_Kp,\] where \(R\) is a stated Archimedean or coefficient-size bound. A structural sparse degree estimate has the form \(B_C(p)\le D(\theta,\deg p,\|p\|)\). Such a statement is meaningful only after the polynomial norm, scaling, clique assignment, and the precise interpretation of \(R\) have been fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse rate estimates depend on local clique size, local constraint count, degrees, quantitative boundedness, positivity margin, scaling, and the chosen polynomial norm.
assumptions_latex: \(p(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\).
Each localized constraint set \(J_k\) is fixed.
A norm and an Archimedean or coefficient-size convention are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_C(p)\le D(\theta,\deg p,\|p\|)\) is a structurally parameterized degree estimate.

notation.meaning: Tuple of structural and quantitative rate parameters.
Maximum clique size, local constraint count, and constraint degree.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed tuple is family-dependent and unsourced. Moreover, p>0 on K alone does not ensure that min_K p exists and is positive unless suitable compactness or attainment assumptions are stated.

children.title: Rate Deterioration Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sparse regimes associated with weak or unavailable rate guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate Deterioration Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniformity in certificate-derived sparse convergence rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider instances indexed by \(t\) satisfying \[B_{C_t}(f_t-f_t^*+\varepsilon)\le C_t\varepsilon^{-a_t}\qquad(\varepsilon>0),\] where \(C_t>0\) and \(a_t>0\). The induced estimates are \[f_t^*-\rho_{t,d}\le\left(\frac{C_t}{d}\right)^{1/a_t}.\] These estimates provide a uniform rate precisely when \[\lim_{d\to\infty}\sup_t\left(\frac{C_t}{d}\right)^{1/a_t}=0.\] This condition fails if \(\sup_t C_t=\infty\). It also fails when some sequence \(t_r\) satisfies \(a_{t_r}\to\infty\) and \(C_{t_r}\ge c>0\). Unbounded exponents without such control on \(C_t\) do not by themselves imply deterioration. Failure of this uniform estimate does not disprove pointwise convergence for a fixed instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate estimates give a uniform rate exactly when their worst-case displayed bound tends to zero. Unbounded constants cause failure, while diverging exponents cause failure when the associated constants do not vanish; neither failure rules out convergence for each fixed instance.
assumptions_latex: \(B_{C_t}(f_t-f_t^*+\varepsilon)\le C_t\varepsilon^{-a_t}\) for every \(t\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).
\(C_t>0\) and \(a_t>0\) for every \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform decay from the displayed estimates holds if and only if \(\lim_{d\to\infty}\sup_t(C_t/d)^{1/a_t}=0\).

notation.meaning: Order-d lower bound for instance t.

knowledge_statements.title: Waki-Lasserre Sparse Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correlative-sparsity moment-SOS relaxation with clique-local semidefinite blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a polynomial optimization problem, cliques \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\), compatible objective pieces \(f=\sum_kf_k\), localized constraint sets \(J_k\), and an initial admissible order \(d\). For each clique introduce \(y^{(k)}\), impose \(y^{(k)}_0=1\), \(M_d(y^{(k)})\succeq0\), and \(M_{d-\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil}(g_jy^{(k)})\succeq0\) for \(j\in J_k\), together with overlap-consistency equalities. Minimize \(\sum_kL_{y^{(k)}}(f_k)\), report the lower bound \(\rho_d\), and increase \(d\) until a prescribed gap, certificate, or extraction condition is met. Under an appropriate sparse Archimedean condition and running-intersection structure, the hierarchy satisfies \(\rho_d\uparrow f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hierarchy solves increasing-order clique moment SDPs with localized constraints and overlap consistency, producing convergent lower bounds under standard sparse compactness assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The objective and every constraint are supported within designated cliques.
The cliques satisfy the required running-intersection property.
The associated sparse quadratic module satisfies an Archimedean condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\le f^*\) and \(\lim_{d\to\infty}\rho_d=f^*\).

children.title: Sparse Bounded-Degree SOS
children.top_down_role: Sparse relaxations controlling local certificate degrees.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Bounded-Degree SOS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse BSOS-style hierarchy with fixed local SOS degrees and expanding constraint products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume each clique constraint has been scaled as \(0\le g_j\le1\) on \(K\). Fix local SOS caps \(r_k\). At level \(q\), maximize \(\gamma\) subject to \[f-\gamma=\sum_{k=1}^m\left(s_k+\sum_{\substack{\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^{J_k}\\|\alpha|+|\beta|\le q}}\lambda_{k,\alpha,\beta}\prod_{j\in J_k}g_j^{\alpha_j}(1-g_j)^{\beta_j}\right),\] where \(s_k\in\Sigma[x_{I_k}]\), \(\deg(s_k)\le2r_k\), and \(\lambda_{k,\alpha,\beta}\ge0\). Increase \(q\) while keeping the local SOS caps fixed, and output the best lower bound or stop when the requested gap or certificate condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This sparse bounded-degree scheme fixes each clique SOS degree while enlarging the collection of nonnegative local constraint products.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le g_j(x)\le1\) on \(K\) after valid scaling.
\(J_k\subseteq\{j:\operatorname{supp}(g_j)\subseteq I_k\}\).
\(r_k\in\mathbb N\) are fixed local SOS-degree caps.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Order Sparse Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a correlative-sparse moment relaxation with clique-dependent truncation orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be variable cliques, and assign each constraint to a clique containing its variables. A multi-order sparse relaxation is specified by integers \(d_i\) satisfying \(2d_i\ge\deg f_i\) and \(2d_i\ge\deg g_j\) for every polynomial assigned to clique \(I_i\). It uses a local truncated moment sequence \(y^{(i)}\), imposes \(M_{d_i}(y^{(i)})\succeq0\) and \(M_{d_i-\lceil\deg g_j/2\rceil}(g_jy^{(i)})\succeq0\), and equates moments indexed by monomials shared by overlapping cliques.

children.title: TSSOS Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Support-extension hierarchies based on term-sparsity graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: TSSOS Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-extension construction for unconstrained or constrained term-sparse moment-SOS relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given relaxation order \(d\), form a graph whose vertices are monomials \(x^\alpha\) with \(|\alpha|\le d\); connect \(x^\alpha\) and \(x^\beta\) when \(\alpha+\beta\) belongs to the current support set. At support-extension step \(k\), choose a chordal extension, replace each positive-semidefinite moment or localizing matrix by positive-semidefinite principal blocks indexed by its maximal cliques, and enlarge the support by all exponent sums generated inside those blocks. Repeat until the graph and support stabilize. The resulting semidefinite optimum is the \((d,k)\)-level TSSOS bound; increasing \(k\) yields nested block-support closures at fixed \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: TSSOS repeatedly builds term graphs, chordally completes them, imposes PSD clique blocks, and extends supports using exponent sums generated within those blocks.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial objective and constraints have finite monomial supports.
The order \(d\) is at least the degree threshold required by the moment and localizing matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{d,k}\) is the semidefinite bound produced after \(k\) support-extension steps.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: term-sparsity graphs and iterative support extension are standard TSSOS mechanics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the container, but the precise graph construction, chordal-extension rule, support update, and nesting claim require a primary TSSOS source.

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal-TSSOS Hierarchies

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At relaxation order \(d\) and support-extension level \(k\), let \(G_{d,k}\) be the term-sparsity graph and let \(\widehat G_{d,k}\) be a chordal extension with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\). The chordal-TSSOS positive-semidefinite constraint is represented by clique matrices \(M_d(y)[C_\ell,C_\ell]\succeq0\) for \(\ell=1,\ldots,q\), together with equality of duplicated entries on clique intersections. Equivalently, the partially specified moment matrix indexed by \(\widehat G_{d,k}\) must admit a positive-semidefinite completion. Localizing matrices are decomposed analogously using their constraint-specific term graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal extension converts each term-sparse PSD constraint into consistent PSD constraints on maximal-clique principal blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat G_{d,k}\) is a chordal extension of the term-sparsity graph.
All clique blocks use entries induced by one common truncated moment sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(y)\vert_{\widehat G_{d,k}}\) admits a positive-semidefinite completion exactly when its consistent maximal-clique blocks are positive semidefinite.

children.title: Compact Archimedean Sparse Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Archimedean Sparse Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic convergence of the correlative-sparse hierarchy under clique-local Archimedeanity and running intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be variable cliques, let \(f=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_{I_i})\), and assign each constraint \(g_j(x)\ge 0\) to a clique containing all variables of \(g_j\). For each clique \(I_i\), let \(Q_i\subseteq\mathbb R[x_{I_i}]\) be the quadratic module generated by its assigned constraints. If the clique family satisfies the running-intersection property, every \(Q_i\) is Archimedean, and the order-\(d\) sparse moment-SOS truncations are nested, then their optimal values \(\rho_d\) are valid lower bounds satisfying \(\rho_d\le \rho_{d+1}\le f^*\) and \(\lim_{d\to\infty}\rho_d=f^*\), where \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under running intersection, clique-local Archimedeanity, and nested truncations, the correlative-sparse moment-SOS lower bounds increase to the global minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_{I_i})\), and every constraint is supported in an assigned clique.
The clique family \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\) satisfies the running-intersection property.
Every local quadratic module \(Q_i\) is Archimedean.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d\uparrow f^*\) as \(d\to\infty\).

children.title: Finite Stabilization Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Stabilization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank and ideal conditions sufficient for finite termination of a sparse moment hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At relaxation order \(d\), let \(y^{(i)}\) be an optimal local moment sequence for clique \(I_i\). A finite-stabilization regime holds when there exist integers \(t_i\le d\) and degree offsets \(\delta_i\) such that \(\operatorname{rank}M_{t_i}(y^{(i)})=\operatorname{rank}M_{t_i-\delta_i}(y^{(i)})\) for every clique, the resulting finite atomic measures have identical marginals on clique intersections, and their atoms satisfy all assigned constraints. Under these conditions the local measures glue to a feasible global measure supported on finitely many points, so the relaxation value equals the global optimum and higher compatible orders cannot improve the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite stabilization occurs when every clique moment matrix is flat and the recovered atomic marginals agree on all clique overlaps.
assumptions_latex: An optimal sparse moment solution exists at order \(d\).
Clique-local flat extensions hold at truncation orders \(t_i\).
Recovered overlap marginals are mutually consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d=f^*\), and the hierarchy stabilizes at every higher compatible order.

children.title: Sparse Variety Geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Variety Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric regime in which clique projections of the feasible variety are finite and compatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the real variety defined by the equality constraints, and let \(\pi_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{I_i}\) be clique projection. The sparse variety has finite compatible geometry when every \(V_i=\pi_i(V)\) is finite and, for every edge of a running-intersection clique tree, the projections of \(V_i\) and \(V_j\) onto \(I_i\cap I_j\) coincide. If the feasible set is contained in \(V\), local moment functionals supported on the sets \(V_i\) can have only finitely many atoms; global recovery additionally requires compatible choices across all separators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse variety geometry is finite when each clique projection is finite and adjacent projections agree on their separator coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The equality constraints define a real variety \(V\).
The clique family admits a running-intersection tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|V_i|<\infty\) for every \(i\), with separator-compatible clique projections.

children.title: Clique-Local Ideal Structure

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Local Ideal Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local algebraic condition supporting finite-dimensional clique moment quotients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For clique \(I_i\), let \(J_i\subseteq\mathbb R[x_{I_i}]\) be the ideal generated by assigned equalities, optionally enlarged by polynomials known to vanish on the clique projection of the feasible set. The clique-local ideal structure is finite when \(\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathbb R[x_{I_i}]/\sqrt[\mathbb R]{J_i}<\infty\) for every \(i\). Compatibility requires that the contraction ideals on each separator agree: \(\sqrt[\mathbb R]{J_i}\cap\mathbb R[x_{I_i\cap I_j}]=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{J_j}\cap\mathbb R[x_{I_i\cap I_j}]\). These predicates encode finite local varieties and matching algebraic relations on overlaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each clique has a finite-dimensional real-radical quotient, and neighboring clique ideals induce the same relations on shared variables.
assumptions_latex: Each assigned equality belongs to \(\mathbb R[x_{I_i}]\).
Clique overlaps are represented by the common subrings \(\mathbb R[x_{I_i\cap I_j}]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathbb R[x_{I_i}]/\sqrt[\mathbb R]{J_i}<\infty\) with equal separator contractions.

children.title: Extraction at Stabilization

knowledge_statements.title: Extraction at Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery and assembly of minimizers from stabilized clique-local moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an optimal sparse moment solution, select for each clique a flat truncation \(M_{t_i}(y^{(i)})\). Construct multiplication matrices in a basis of its column space, jointly diagonalize the commuting coordinate operators, and recover clique atoms \(z_{i,1},\ldots,z_{i,r_i}\) with positive weights. Match atoms across adjacent cliques by equality of their coordinates on each separator, retaining only globally consistent combinations. Assemble every consistent family into \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), verify all original constraints and \(f(x)=\rho_d\), and output the verified assembled points. If separator matching fails, report that local flatness alone did not certify global extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover atoms from flat clique moments, match them across separators, assemble global points, and verify feasibility and optimal objective value.
assumptions_latex: Every selected clique moment matrix satisfies a flat-extension rank condition.
Local coordinate multiplication matrices commute and are extractable.
Clique atoms can be tested for separator consistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*=\{x:\ x\text{ is assembled, feasible, and }f(x)=\rho_d\}\) is the extracted set of certified minimizers.

children.title: Unbounded Sparse Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Sparse Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why compact sparse convergence does not automatically extend to unbounded feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a clique-local quadratic module \(Q_i\) is not Archimedean, no polynomial \(R-\|x_{I_i}\|^2\) need belong to \(Q_i\), so compact sparse Positivstellensatz arguments do not apply. Consequently, positivity of \(f-f^*+\varepsilon\) on an unbounded feasible set does not by itself imply a finite-degree decomposition into clique-local quadratic modules, and sparse relaxation values need not be proved to converge by the compact theory. Convergence requires additional hypotheses or reformulations, such as coercive level sets compatible with the cliques, homogenization with control at infinity, or explicit perturbations whose errors vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without clique-local Archimedeanity, compact sparse convergence theory fails; coercivity, homogenization, or controlled perturbation is needed to recover guarantees.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is unbounded or some local quadratic module is non-Archimedean.
No redundant clique-wise ball constraints are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-f^*+\varepsilon>0\) on \(K\) does not alone guarantee membership in \(\sum_i Q_i\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic module local to clique i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Archimedean positivity certificates generally require compactness or substitutes

knowledge_statements.title: Term-Sparse Convergence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates finite graph stabilization from dense-order and global optimization convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed moment order \(d\), a term-sparsity support-extension sequence stabilizes after finitely many steps because only finitely many monomial pairs can be added. This graph stabilization means only that the block pattern no longer changes. It does not imply that the stabilized relaxation equals the dense order-\(d\) moment relaxation, nor that its value equals the global optimum. Dense-order recovery requires the stabilized blocks to reproduce the relevant dense positive-semidefinite constraints; global convergence additionally requires passage \(d\to\infty\) and suitable positivity assumptions. Thus finite stabilization in \(k\), dense equivalence at fixed \(d\), and convergence in \(d\) are logically distinct claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A term graph may stabilize finitely without reaching the dense relaxation or the global optimum; these are three distinct convergence notions.
assumptions_latex: The order-\(d\) monomial basis is finite.
Support extension only adds edges or supported exponent sums.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Wise Flatness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local rank-stabilization predicate for sparse atomic moment recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^{(i)}=(y^{(i)}_\alpha)\) be a truncated moment sequence on variables \(x_{I_i}\), feasible for all moment and localizing constraints through order \(d\). For an integer \(t_i\le d\) and offset \(\delta_i\) covering the largest half-degree of the assigned constraints, clique-wise flatness is the condition \(\operatorname{rank}M_{t_i}(y^{(i)})=\operatorname{rank}M_{t_i-\delta_i}(y^{(i)})\). Under positivity of the associated localizing matrices, this condition certifies a finitely atomic representing measure for the clique moments, with exactly \(\operatorname{rank}M_{t_i}(y^{(i)})\) atoms. It does not alone certify compatibility between different cliques.

children.title: Sparse PSD-Completion View
children.top_down_role: Completion-based representation of sparse positive semidefinite structure.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\).
The diagonal and edge entries of a real symmetric partial matrix \(X\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) has a positive semidefinite completion if and only if every fully specified maximal-clique principal submatrix is positive semidefinite.

notation.meaning: Principal partial matrix indexed by clique C

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical positive-semidefinite completion theorem for chordal graphs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal PSD completion for partially specified symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists \(\widehat X\in\mathbb S_+^{|V|}\) satisfying \(\widehat X_{ij}=X_{ij}\) for every specified pair \(i=j\) or \(\{i,j\}\in E\) if and only if \(X[C_k]\succeq0\) for every maximal clique \(C_k\). Thus the cone of chordally patterned partial matrices admitting positive semidefinite completion is represented by clique constraints \(X[C_k]\succeq0\), with common specified entries shared consistently by intersecting cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal sparsity, a partial symmetric matrix has a PSD completion exactly when every maximal-clique principal block is PSD.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse PSD-Completion View

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is the classical chordal PSD-completion theorem and fits the completion-view leaf, but the record supplies no theorem, section, or page citation.

children.title: Clique PSD-Decomposition View
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of sparse PSD structure into clique-supported cones.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\).
\(S\in\mathbb S^{|V|}\) has zeros outside the diagonal and edges of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\succeq0\) if and only if it is a sum of positive semidefinite matrices embedded from the maximal cliques.

notation.meaning: Coordinate selector from V to clique C_k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical chordal decomposition of sparse positive-semidefinite matrices
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-sum representation of the chordal sparse PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The chordally sparse positive semidefinite cone satisfies \[\{S\in\mathbb S_+^{|V|}:S_{ij}=0\text{ if }i\ne j,\ \{i,j\}\notin E\}=\left\{\sum_{k=1}^m E_k^{\mathsf T}Z_kE_k:Z_k\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_k|}\right\}.\] The clique matrices \(Z_k\) need not equal the principal submatrices \(S[C_k]\); their embedded contributions add on clique overlaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordally sparse PSD matrix is exactly a sum of PSD matrices supported on maximal cliques, with overlapping contributions added.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique PSD-Decomposition View

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique-sum representation and its content kind fit the decomposition-view leaf, but the exact cone equality has no inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Primal Chordal Formulations
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing primal models built from chordal sparse structure.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is chordal and the affine objective and constraints use only entries specified by its diagonal-edge pattern.
\(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) are the maximal cliques of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing the global PSD-completion constraint by clique PSD constraints and separator equalities gives an equivalent primal conic formulation.

notation.meaning: Clique-local copy of the primal matrix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: primal conversion induced by the chordal PSD-completion theorem
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-copy extended formulation of a primal sparse SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal constraint that a partial matrix \(X\) admit a positive semidefinite completion, introduce \(X_k=E_kXE_k^{\mathsf T}\) for each maximal clique and impose \(X_k\succeq0\). Along every clique-tree edge \((k,p)\), impose \(X_k[S_{kp}]=X_p[S_{kp}]\), where \(S_{kp}=C_k\cap C_p\). Express each affine constraint and the objective using any consistent allocation of their specified coefficients among the clique copies. The running-intersection property makes the separator equalities sufficient for a unique consistent partial matrix, and the completion theorem makes this extended formulation equivalent to the original primal constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal sparse SDP can use one PSD matrix per clique, coupled by equality of all entries on clique-tree separators.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Chordal Formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique-copy representation fits primal chordal formulations, but the equivalence, separator sufficiency, and coefficient-allocation claims require a specific chordal-SDP source.

children.title: Dual Chordal Formulations

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Chordal Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-sum extended formulation of a dual sparse SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A chordally sparse dual semidefinite constraint \(S(y)\succeq0\) can be written as \[S(y)=\sum_{k=1}^m E_k^{\mathsf T}Z_kE_k,\qquad Z_k\succeq0\quad(k=1,\ldots,m).\] The scalar dual variables \(y\) retain their original affine role, while the matrices \(Z_k\) certify membership of the slack in the sparse positive semidefinite cone. Equality of the displayed matrices couples overlapping clique contributions automatically through coefficient matching; the decomposition theorem makes the formulation equivalent to the original sparse slack constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual sparse PSD slack is represented as a sum of embedded clique PSD blocks linked through the slack equality.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\).
The dual slack \(S(y)=C-\mathcal A^*y\) has the diagonal-edge sparsity pattern of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual slack constraint is equivalent to the existence of clique blocks \(Z_k\succeq0\) satisfying \(S(y)=\sum_kE_k^{\mathsf T}Z_kE_k\).

children.title: Chordal Formulation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relation between primal completion forms and dual decomposition forms.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is chordal and all pairings use the diagonal-edge entries of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The PSD-completable partial-matrix cone and the chordally sparse PSD cone are dual cones, inducing the primal clique-copy and dual clique-sum formulations.

notation.meaning: Cone of G-partial matrices having PSD completions
Cone of PSD matrices supported on G
Trace pairing after zero-filling specified entries

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polar correspondence between chordal completion and sparse PSD cones
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone duality underlying primal and dual chordal conversions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the trace pairing on specified entries, \[\mathcal K_{\mathrm{comp}}(G)^*=\mathcal K_{\mathrm{sp}}(G),\qquad \mathcal K_{\mathrm{sp}}(G)^*=\mathcal K_{\mathrm{comp}}(G).\] For chordal \(G\), the first cone is represented by positive semidefinite maximal-clique principal blocks with consistent overlaps, whereas the second is represented by sums \(\sum_kE_k^{\mathsf T}Z_kE_k\) with \(Z_k\succeq0\). Consequently, applying conic duality to the primal clique-copy formulation yields the dual clique-sum formulation, up to the chosen allocation of affine coefficients on overlaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal completion and sparse PSD cones are dual; clique principal-block constraints correspond to embedded clique-sum certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Formulation Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality kind fits the correspondence leaf and the cone relations are plausible under the stated pairing, but no inspectable source supports the precise dual-cone and formulation-correspondence claims.

children.title: Chordal Duality-Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regularity regimes affecting agreement between chordal primal and dual values.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual chordal formulations are feasible and have finite optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Slater point on either appropriate side guarantees zero duality gap and attainment on the opposite side; without a constraint qualification, chordal conversion alone gives no such guarantee.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard conic Slater duality applied to exact chordal reformulations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-duality and failure regimes for chordally converted SDPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the primal chordal formulation has an affine-feasible point with \(X_k\succ0\) for every clique block, then \(p^*=d^*\) and the dual optimum is attained. The symmetric conclusion holds when the dual has a relative-interior feasible slack decomposition. When both sides lie only on proper faces of their chordal cones, these implications fail: the linear image defining the slack or overlap constraints may be nonclosed, so attainment or zero gap is not guaranteed. Because chordal conversion is value-equivalent, it does not by itself remove a positive gap or nonattainment already caused by failure of constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal reformulation preserves strong duality under Slater conditions, but it cannot by itself cure gaps or nonattainment caused by facial degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Duality-Gap Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the relative-interior condition, attainment conclusions, and nonclosed-image explanation need an authoritative conic-duality source to verify their exact hypotheses.

children.title: Variable-Clique Gram Blocks
children.top_down_role: Gram blocks aligned with correlative sparsity.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) are variable cliques and \(v_d(x_{C_k})\) contains all clique monomials of degree at most \(d\).
The target polynomial has degree at most \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in the variable-clique sparse SOS cone is equivalent to a coefficient-matching representation by positive semidefinite clique Gram blocks.

notation.meaning: Monomial vector in variables of clique C through degree d
Positive semidefinite Gram block for clique k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Gram representation of the correlative-sparsity SOS cone
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gram representation aligned with cliques of the variable graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the variable-clique sparse SOS cone by \[\Sigma_{d,C}=\left\{p:\ p(x)=\sum_{k=1}^m v_d(x_{C_k})^{\mathsf T}Q_kv_d(x_{C_k}),\ Q_k\succeq0\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(p\in\Sigma_{d,C}\) exactly when each quadratic form admits a clique-local sum-of-squares factorization and the sum of their coefficients equals the coefficient vector of \(p\). Each \(Q_k\) is indexed only by monomials supported on variables in \(C_k\); this characterizes the sparse SOS cone, which may be smaller than the unrestricted SOS cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlative sparsity replaces one global Gram matrix by PSD Gram blocks whose monomials use variables from individual cliques.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Clique Gram Blocks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly targets variable-clique Gram blocks and distinguishes the sparse cone from unrestricted SOS, but it lacks a specific sparse-SOS citation.

children.title: Monomial-Clique Gram Blocks
children.top_down_role: Gram blocks aligned with term sparsity.

assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a finite monomial basis and its term-sparsity graph has a chordal extension with maximal monomial cliques \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\).
The polynomial support is contained in \(B+B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Gram matrix in the chordal sparse PSD cone is equivalent to positive semidefinite monomial-clique blocks whose coefficient contributions sum to the polynomial.

notation.meaning: Finite exponent set indexing a monomial basis
PSD Gram block on monomial clique B_k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: chordal Gram decomposition on a monomial term-sparsity graph
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gram blocks aligned with cliques of a monomial sparsity graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_B(x)=(x^\alpha)_{\alpha\in B}\). Restrict a Gram matrix for \(p\) to the chordal sparse PSD cone of the term-sparsity graph. By clique decomposition, this is equivalent to \[p(x)=\sum_{k=1}^m v_{B_k}(x)^{\mathsf T}Q_kv_{B_k}(x),\qquad Q_k\succeq0.\] For every exponent \(\gamma\), coefficient matching requires \(p_\gamma=\sum_k\sum_{\alpha,\beta\in B_k:\alpha+\beta=\gamma}(Q_k)_{\alpha\beta}\). Thus clique membership concerns monomial indices, independently of whether all monomials in a block share one variable clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Term sparsity decomposes a Gram matrix into PSD blocks indexed by chordal cliques of monomials, with their coefficient contributions summed.
knowledge_statements.title: Monomial-Clique Gram Blocks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monomial-clique Gram representation fits the term-sparsity leaf and its coefficient matching is internally consistent, but the chordal term-sparse equivalence has no inspectable source.

children.title: Separator Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coupling induced by shared clique separators.

assumptions_latex: Clique moment sequences \(y^{(k)}\) and \(y^{(p)}\) are truncated through degree \(2d\).
The cliques are adjacent in a clique tree with separator \(S_{kp}=C_k\cap C_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separator coupling holds exactly when the two local sequences assign identical values to every retained moment supported on their separator.

notation.meaning: Truncated moment sequence for clique k
Separator between cliques k and p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality of duplicated separator moments in clique-local moment formulations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear consistency constraints for moments duplicated across cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The separator-coupling predicate for adjacent cliques \(C_k\) and \(C_p\) is \[y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(p)}_\alpha\quad\text{for every }\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\text{ with }|\alpha|\le2d\text{ and }\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq S_{kp}.\] Equivalently, the principal submatrices of the two clique moment matrices indexed by separator monomials agree entrywise. When the cliques satisfy the running-intersection property, imposing these equalities on clique-tree edges propagates equality of every duplicated retained moment across all cliques containing its support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjacent clique moment blocks are coupled by equating every retained moment whose variables lie entirely in their shared separator.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and separator-moment equalities fit the leaf, but the equivalence with separator moment-matrix blocks and propagation along the clique tree require a specific sparse moment-SDP citation.

children.title: Duplicate Moment Entries

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Moment Entries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local copies of a moment indexed by a monomial represented in multiple clique truncations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be variable cliques, let \(d_k\in\mathbb N\), and let \(y^{(k)}=(y^{(k)}_\alpha)_{\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq C_k,\,|\alpha|\leq 2d_k}\) be the truncated moment sequence assigned to \(C_k\). For every global multi-index \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\), define \(D_\alpha:=\{k:\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq C_k,\ |\alpha|\leq 2d_k\}\). If \(|D_\alpha|>1\), then \(\{y^{(k)}_\alpha:k\in D_\alpha\}\) is the family of duplicate moment entries for \(x^\alpha\): distinct local decision variables intended to represent the same global moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A moment entry is duplicated when the same monomial lies within the degree truncations of two or more variable cliques and is represented by a separate local variable in each clique.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) are variable cliques.
\(d_k\in\mathbb N\) is the local relaxation order for clique \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|D_\alpha|>1\) identifies multiple local representations of the moment indexed by \(\alpha\).

children.top_down_role: Reduction of duplicated variables or constraints in converted block models.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlap Redundancy Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-variable representation eliminating repeated moment variables on clique overlaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every multi-index \(\alpha\) with \(|D_\alpha|>1\), introduce one master moment \(z_\alpha\) and substitute \(y^{(k)}_\alpha=z_\alpha\) for every \(k\in D_\alpha\). After substitution, retain \(z_\alpha\) once and remove the corresponding duplicate coordinates from the local decision vectors. This reduced formulation represents exactly the feasible points of the duplicated formulation satisfying \(y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(\ell)}_\alpha\) for all \(k,\ell\in D_\alpha\); reconstruction sets every eliminated coordinate equal to \(z_\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace all consistent copies of each shared moment by one master variable; feasible solutions of the reduced and equality-coupled formulations correspond exactly.
assumptions_latex: All duplicate entries indexed by the same \(\alpha\) represent one global moment.
Duplicate coordinates occur only through affine expressions and local conic blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Master-variable substitution removes overlap redundancy without changing the consistency-constrained feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality condition ensuring that overlapping clique moment blocks define compatible local functionals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let clique \(k\) carry moments through degree \(2d_k\). Local sequences \(y^{(1)},\ldots,y^{(m)}\) are coupling-consistent when, for every pair \(k,\ell\) and every multi-index \(\alpha\) satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq C_k\cap C_\ell\) and \(|\alpha|\leq 2\min(d_k,d_\ell)\), one has \(y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(\ell)}_\alpha\). Equivalently, the restrictions of the local linear functionals agree on every monomial represented by both clique relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two clique moment sequences are consistent exactly when their entries agree for every shared monomial available at both local orders.
assumptions_latex: Clique \(k\) contains moments through degree \(2d_k\).
Identical multi-indices use a common global variable ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed overlap equalities are the coupling-consistency predicate.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Moment Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment matrices formed separately on the monomials supported by each variable clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a clique \(C_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), order \(d_k\), and truncated sequence \(y^{(k)}=(y^{(k)}_\gamma)_{\operatorname{supp}(\gamma)\subseteq C_k,\ |\gamma|\leq2d_k}\), let \(v_{d_k}^{C_k}(x)\) list the monomials \(x^\alpha\) supported in \(C_k\) with \(|\alpha|\leq d_k\). The clique moment block is \[M_{d_k}^{C_k}(y^{(k)})_{\alpha,\beta}:=y^{(k)}_{\alpha+\beta}.\] Moment feasibility imposes \(M_{d_k}^{C_k}(y^{(k)})\succeq0\), together with any required clique-localizing blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique moment block is the moment matrix indexed only by monomials supported on that clique; relaxation feasibility requires it to be positive semidefinite.

The local sequence is available through degree \(2d_k\).

children.title: Gram–Moment Translation
children.top_down_role: Structural translation between clique Gram coordinates and clique moment coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Gram–Moment Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-pairing identity connecting clique Gram matrices and clique moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a clique \(C_k\) and an order \(d\). Let \(v_d^{C_k}(x)\) be its monomial vector, let \(Q_k\) be a symmetric matrix of matching size, and define \(p_k(x):=(v_d^{C_k}(x))^{\mathsf T}Q_kv_d^{C_k}(x)\). For every local sequence \(y^{(k)}\) through degree \(2d\), \[L_{y^{(k)}}(p_k)=\left\langle Q_k,M_d^{C_k}(y^{(k)})\right\rangle.\] Thus \(Q_k\succeq0\) gives a clique-supported sum-of-squares polynomial, while \(M_d^{C_k}(y^{(k)})\succeq0\) makes its moment evaluation nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating a clique Gram polynomial by a moment functional equals the matrix inner product of its Gram matrix and the clique moment matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb N\).
\(Q_k\) is symmetric and conformal with \(v_d^{C_k}\).
The local moments are defined through degree \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{y^{(k)}}((v_d^{C_k})^{\mathsf T}Q_kv_d^{C_k})=\langle Q_k,M_d^{C_k}(y^{(k)})\rangle\).

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Block-Conic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-facing conic form exposing clique cones and overlap equations as separate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit clique block-conic relaxation has the form \[\inf_{X_1,\ldots,X_m,z}\ \sum_{k=1}^m\langle C_k,X_k\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}z\quad\text{subject to}\quad X_k\in K_k,\ \sum_{k=1}^m\mathcal A_k(X_k)+Az=b,\ \mathcal E_k(X_k)=R_kz.\] Here each \(K_k\) is a clique-local semidefinite or product cone, and \(\mathcal E_k(X_k)=R_kz\) explicitly couples duplicated overlap coordinates to master variables. No aggregate positive-semidefinite cone is required in the submitted model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver receives separate clique cone variables, global affine constraints, and explicit equations tying overlapping coordinates to shared master variables.
assumptions_latex: All polynomial relaxation constraints have affine conic representations.
Every shared coordinate is identified by an overlap map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation is represented as independent clique cones linked only by affine coupling constraints.

children.title: Automatic Chordal Conversion

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Chordal Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a chordally sparse aggregate semidefinite constraint into clique constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a partial symmetric matrix variable \(X\) whose specified-entry graph \(G\) is chordal, and compute its maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\). Introduce \(X_k=X[C_k,C_k]\) and impose \(X_k\succeq0\) for every \(k\). For every entry represented in two blocks, add equality constraints between its copies, or replace them by one master variable. Rewrite each affine constraint using the clique copies and output the resulting block-conic model. Under chordality, the consistent blocks admit a common positive-semidefinite completion of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detect chordal cliques, create one positive-semidefinite block per clique, couple repeated entries, and rewrite the aggregate affine constraints in those blocks.
assumptions_latex: The specified-entry graph \(G\) is chordal.
The aggregate constraint means positive-semidefinite completability of the partial matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The converted model is equivalent to the aggregate positive-semidefinite-completion constraint.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm invokes the nontrivial chordal positive-semidefinite completion theorem to claim equivalence. No source or theorem locator is supplied, so that conclusion cannot be reviewed as candidate knowledge.
