knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Solver Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-separable interface supporting local conic solves and shared-coordinate coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the model by local objectives \(f_k(x_k)\), local feasible sets \(K_k\), and interfaces \(E_kx_k=R_kz\). Given \(z^t\), multipliers \(u_k^t\), and penalty \(\rho>0\), each worker independently computes \[x_k^{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x_k\in K_k} f_k(x_k)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|E_kx_k-R_kz^t+u_k^t\|_2^2.\] A coordinator minimizes the summed quadratic penalties over \(z\), then sets \(u_k^{t+1}=u_k^t+E_kx_k^{t+1}-R_kz^{t+1}\). Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each clique solves a local conic subproblem; a coordinator updates shared overlap variables and multipliers until consensus residuals meet specified tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Each local subproblem can be solved to the required accuracy.
The coupling constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface separates clique computation from coordination through \(E_kx_k=R_kz\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes a scaled consensus-ADMM interface and appropriately avoids claiming convergence, but the algorithm and residual-based stopping interface have no cited source.

children.title: Consensus Formulations
children.top_down_role: Consensus representations linking local sparse subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-variable consensus representation of equality-coupled clique relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\in K_k\) collect clique-local variables and let \(E_kx_k\) extract coordinates shared with other cliques. Introduce a global vector \(z\) and selection map \(R_k\) for each clique. The overlap-coupled problem is represented as \[\inf_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\ \sum_{k=1}^m f_k(x_k)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_k\in K_k,\qquad E_kx_k=R_kz\quad(k=1,\ldots,m).\] Eliminating \(z\) yields pairwise equality of every duplicate coordinate assigned to the same global component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each clique retains local variables while equality to a shared global vector enforces agreement of all duplicate overlap coordinates.
assumptions_latex: Each shared coordinate has one global index in \(z\).
The maps \(E_k\) and \(R_k\) select matching coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global consensus constraints are equivalent to equality among all local copies of each shared coordinate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global-consensus representation and its elimination equivalence fit the leaf, but no source is supplied for the formulation.

children.title: Clique Communication Topologies
children.top_down_role: Communication patterns induced by clique and separator organization.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Communication Topologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication graphs induced by overlaps among variable cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), the clique communication graph is \(H=(V,E)\), where \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(\{k,\ell\}\in E\) only if \(C_k\cap C_\ell\neq\varnothing\) and the two workers exchange shared coordinates. A junction-tree topology is a tree \(T\subseteq H\) satisfying the running-intersection property: for every variable \(i\), the vertices \(\{k:i\in C_k\}\) induce a connected subtree. In that case, consistency enforced on tree-edge separators propagates to every pair of cliques containing the same represented moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique workers communicate along overlap edges; a running-intersection junction tree lets separator agreement propagate throughout every clique family sharing a variable.
assumptions_latex: Each edge communicates all moment coordinates assigned to its clique intersection.
The junction tree satisfies the running-intersection property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tree-edge separator consistency implies global consistency among all clique copies connected by the running-intersection subtrees.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record combines a topology definition with a nontrivial running-intersection propagation property. The property may be standard, but it needs a junction-tree source and a precise locator before the mathematical role and conclusion can be accepted.

children.title: Coordination Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Coupling and communication regimes that limit distributed scalability.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordination Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration communication and coordination costs in clique-consensus implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a communication graph have edges \(E\), and let separator \(e\) transmit \(s_e\) scalar coordinates per iteration in each direction. Any synchronous consensus iteration exchanging every separator vector communicates \(2\sum_{e\in E}s_e\) scalars, excluding metadata. If a centralized coordinator forms each shared coordinate by averaging its incident clique copies, its arithmetic work is \(O(\sum_{k=1}^m r_k)\), where \(r_k=\dim(E_kx_k)\), and its synchronization latency is bounded below by the slowest participating local solve plus communication latency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus communication scales with total separator size, while centralized aggregation scales with all local interface sizes and waits for the slowest worker.
assumptions_latex: Every edge exchanges one full separator vector in both directions per synchronous iteration.
Consensus aggregation is coordinatewise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Communication volume is \(2\sum_{e\in E}s_e\) scalars per iteration and aggregation work is \(O(\sum_k r_k)\).

notation.meaning: number of scalar coordinates on separator edge e
dimension of clique k's consensus interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar-count and aggregation bounds are plausible under the stated synchronous model, but no source is provided, and the latency lower bound requires a more explicit communication and scheduling model.

children.title: Adaptive Hierarchy Management
children.top_down_role: Selective refinement and reuse across successive sparse relaxations.

children.title: Adaptive Clique Orders
children.top_down_role: Selective local-order refinement across variable cliques.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Clique Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective refinement of local moment orders using clique-level diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize each clique with an admissible order \(d_k^0\) sufficient for its assigned polynomial degrees. At iteration \(t\), solve the coupled sparse relaxation, compute a diagnostic \(\eta_k^t\geq0\) for every clique, and choose a refinement set \(S_t\). Set \(d_k^{t+1}=d_k^t+1\) for \(k\in S_t\) and \(d_k^{t+1}=d_k^t\) otherwise. Enlarge affected moment and localizing blocks, add newly shared overlap moments and consistency equations, and embed reusable old entries into the enlarged blocks. Stop under a prescribed bound-gap, certificate, or resource criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with admissible local orders, raise only diagnostically selected clique orders, update affected blocks and overlaps, and stop by a declared accuracy or resource rule.
assumptions_latex: Initial orders cover the degrees of all assigned local polynomials.
Each refinement preserves all existing moments and coupling equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm generates componentwise nondecreasing clique orders and nested locally refined sparse relaxations.

notation.meaning: order of clique k at refinement iteration t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits adaptive clique-order management, but the nested-relaxation conclusion depends on compatibility of local order changes, newly introduced overlap coordinates, and constraint assignments. No source or concrete diagnostic-selection rule is supplied.

children.title: Adaptive Support Enrichment
children.top_down_role: Selective enlargement of term-sparse certificate supports.

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation uses a finite monomial support \(S_k\subset\mathbb{N}^n\).
A diagnostic assigns a nonnegative score \(d_k(\alpha)\) to each candidate exponent \(\alpha\in C_k\setminus S_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enriched supports satisfy \(S_k\subseteq S_{k+1}\subseteq S_k\cup C_k\), so previously representable certificates remain representable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone, diagnostic-driven enrichment of finite term-sparse SOS supports.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a threshold \(\tau_k\ge 0\) and a budget \(b_k\in\mathbb{N}\), form \(E_k\) from at most \(b_k\) exponents in \(C_k\setminus S_k\) having the largest scores among those satisfying \(d_k(\alpha)\ge\tau_k\). Set \(S_{k+1}=S_k\cup E_k\), rebuild only Gram or localizing blocks affected by \(E_k\), and solve the resulting relaxation. Stop enrichment when \(E_k=\varnothing\) or an external stopping test holds. Because support is enlarged by union, every polynomial certificate supported on \(S_k\) is also admissible at iteration \(k+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add the highest-scoring missing monomials within a budget, rebuild affected semidefinite blocks, and retain all previously available certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Support Enrichment

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and monotone-support claim fit the leaf, but the cited general SOS-relaxation section does not specifically support diagnostic scoring, budgeted enrichment, or selective block rebuilding.

children.title: Hierarchy State Reuse Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Reuse of solutions, scaling, and decompositions across hierarchy levels.

children.title: Primal Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of primal solution information across related sparse models.

assumptions_latex: The new primal SDP contains every old scalar variable and principal matrix block under an injective coordinate map.
New constraints admit a chosen completion of the embedded old iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed point is a valid interior initialization when all completed cone blocks are positive definite and all required affine-domain conditions hold.

notation.meaning: embedding into the enlarged primal space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding an old sparse-SDP primal iterate into an enlarged relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Embed the old iterate as \(\widehat X_{k+1}=E_k(X_k)\), preserving all common entries. Complete newly introduced entries using values satisfying the new affine-domain equations when available, and initialize each wholly new semidefinite block as \(\delta I\) with \(\delta>0\). If an embedded block is only semidefinite, replace it for initialization by \(\widehat X_{k+1}+\delta I\) on that block, then apply the solver's affine-start restoration. The output is a warm start, not a claim that the old point remains feasible for every newly imposed constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embed common primal blocks, initialize new blocks positively, and restore new affine constraints before passing the point to the SDP solver.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Warm Starts

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits primal warm starts and appropriately disclaims automatic feasibility, but the cited primal-dual overview does not establish this embedding, regularization, and affine-restoration interface.

children.title: Dual Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of dual solution information across related sparse models.

assumptions_latex: Old and new dual SDPs have identified common constraint coordinates and cone blocks.
The initialization routine can restore the new dual affine equations and cone interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output supplies an interior dual initialization but preserves old dual feasibility only when the embedded slack already satisfies every new affine and cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transport of multipliers and slacks between nested sparse-SDP relaxations.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Copy the entries of \(y_k\) attached to unchanged constraints and initialize multipliers for new constraints to zero or to values obtained by dual affine restoration. Assemble \(Z_{k+1}\) from the new dual slack equation. Preserve common slack blocks when compatible; initialize wholly new blocks by \(\delta I\), where \(\delta>0\), and shift any noninterior block by enough identity to make it positive definite. Finally restore the dual affine equations. The resulting pair is used only as a solver initialization unless direct substitution verifies dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Copy compatible multipliers, construct the new slack, regularize it into the cone interior, and restore the new dual equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Warm Starts

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf and algorithm kind match, but a source is needed for a restoration procedure that simultaneously satisfies the new dual slack equation and cone-interiority requirements; separately shifting and restoring can invalidate one another.

children.title: Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of clique factorizations or solver linear algebra.

assumptions_latex: Two consecutive Newton systems have the same sparsity pattern and symbolic elimination ordering.
Only numerical matrix values or a low-rank subset of rows and columns changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Symbolic data may be reused exactly; a numerical factorization may be reused only if its matrix is unchanged, or updated only under a valid update scheme.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for symbolic, numerical, and low-rank factorization reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reuse of the symbolic factorization is valid when \(\operatorname{supp}(K_{k+1})=\operatorname{supp}(K_k)\) under the same permutation and pivoting model. Reuse of the numerical factors without modification is valid only when \(K_{k+1}=K_k\). If \(K_{k+1}=K_k+UV^{\mathsf T}\), updated factors may be used only when the chosen update algorithm applies and its stability tests pass. Any change of dimension, sparsity pattern, pivot sequence, inertia requirement, or unacceptable factor residual forces a new symbolic or numerical factorization as appropriate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse symbolic factors when sparsity is unchanged; reuse numerical factors only for the same matrix or through a validated stable update.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between symbolic reuse, exact numerical reuse, and validated low-rank updates is mathematically appropriate for this leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Scaling Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of numerical scaling across hierarchy levels.

assumptions_latex: Old and new SDP coordinates have an identified common subset.
Stored diagonal scaling entries are finite and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assembled scaling is invertible and preserves the old coordinate normalization on the common subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of safeguarded diagonal equilibration across related SDP relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every unchanged coordinate \(i\), set \((D_{k+1})_{ii}=\min\{d_{\max},\max\{d_{\min},(D_k)_{ii}\}\}\), where \(0<d_{\min}\le d_{\max}<\infty\). Compute scaling entries for new coordinates from their new rows, columns, or cone blocks using the same equilibration rule and the same safeguards. Reuse is accepted only if scaled residuals and coefficient ranges remain within prescribed limits; otherwise recompute all entries. The output \(D_{k+1}\) is positive diagonal and therefore defines an invertible change of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep safeguarded scales on unchanged coordinates, compute scales for new ones, and recompute globally if scaled diagnostics deteriorate.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed safeguarded scaling-reuse algorithm fits the leaf, but its acceptance diagnostics and reuse policy have no cited support.

children.title: Reuse Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model changes that make inherited numerical information unreliable.

assumptions_latex: A stored state was produced for an SDP relaxation with specified coordinates, constraints, cone blocks, and numerical scaling.
A subsequent relaxation modifies at least one of these structures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: State reuse is invalid whenever no compatibility map preserves the relevant affine equations, cone membership, dimensions, and numerical conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural and numerical conditions that invalidate hierarchy-state transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Direct reuse fails if the state \(s_k\) cannot be mapped into the new dimensions, or if copied entries violate \(\mathcal A_{k+1}(X)=b_{k+1}\), dual slack equations, or cone membership. Numerical reuse must also be rejected after incompatible permutation, scaling, precision, or solver conventions, and whenever restored residuals, factorization residuals, or cone-interiority margins exceed their acceptance thresholds. In particular, zero-padding a feasible old primal matrix need not satisfy a newly added moment equality, and copying old dual multipliers need not produce a positive semidefinite new slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject reuse when dimensions, equations, cones, ordering, scaling, precision, or validation residuals are incompatible with the new relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Reuse Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is correct and the listed incompatibilities are plausible, but no source supports the structural and numerical rejection criteria.

children.title: Diagnostic-Driven Hierarchy Control
children.top_down_role: Refinement decisions based on bounds, residuals, and recovery diagnostics.

children.title: Bound-Based Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination decisions based on relaxation-bound behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is a certified lower bound on the global minimum \(f^\star\).
\(x_k\) is feasible for the original minimization problem, with \(U_k=f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The test certifies \(0\le U_k-f^\star\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U_k|,|L_k|\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-relative optimality-gap stopping for polynomial minimization.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\). Stop when \[U_k-L_k\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U_k|,|L_k|\}.\] Since \(L_k\le f^\star\le U_k\), this inequality gives a certified upper bound on the suboptimality of \(x_k\). The test is not valid if \(L_k\) is merely a numerically reported relaxation value lacking a valid lower-bound certificate or if \(U_k\) comes from an infeasible recovered point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when a certified lower bound and a feasible objective value have an acceptably small absolute-relative gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Based Stopping

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

children.title: Residual-Based Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination decisions based on numerical certificate residuals.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation solver reports primal, dual, and complementarity residuals under fixed normalization.
All residual tolerances are nonnegative and measured in the working precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Passing the test certifies approximate solution of the current SDP only, not global optimality of the original polynomial problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical termination of the current SDP relaxation using normalized residuals.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_c\ge0\), declare the current SDP numerically solved only if \(r_p\le	au_p\), \(r_d\le	au_d\), and \(r_c\le	au_c\), together with the solver's cone-feasibility tests. Residuals must be recomputed in a common, documented normalization rather than compared across incompatible scalings. This stopping rule concerns the finite relaxation. Without a certified relaxation gap, exactness condition, or matching feasible upper bound, small residuals alone do not justify terminating the outer polynomial-optimization hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop the SDP solve when normalized feasibility and complementarity residuals pass tolerance, but do not infer global polynomial optimality from residuals alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Stopping

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

children.title: Recovery-Based Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination decisions based on candidate extraction diagnostics.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery-Based Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination after certified feasible-point recovery and comparison with a certified relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluate the original objective and constraints at \(x_k\) using validation precision. If \(x_k\) is certified feasible for the original problem and \(f(x_k)-L_k\le\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\ge0\), stop and return \(x_k\). Because \(L_k\le f^\star\le f(x_k)\), the returned point satisfies \(0\le f(x_k)-f^\star\le\varepsilon\). A flat-extension or rank test may justify extraction, but it does not replace certified feasibility validation and comparison with a certified bound when numerical tolerances are present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop after recovering a point certified feasible for the original problem whose objective is within the permitted gap of the certified relaxation lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation supplies a certified lower bound \(L_k\) on the global minimum \(f^\star\).
A recovery map returns a point \(x_k\) that is certified feasible for the original optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the test passes, \(x_k\) is certified globally near-optimal and satisfies \(0\le f(x_k)-f^\star\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: recovered point certified feasible for the original problem
global minimum value of the original problem

children.title: Relaxation Escalation
children.top_down_role: Movement to stronger or higher-order sparse relaxations.

assumptions_latex: Relaxations are indexed by a partially ordered state \(h_k\) encoding orders, supports, or clique-local orders.
A diagnostic indicates that the current relaxation is insufficient while the numerical SDP solve is reliable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update produces a strictly stronger admissible state \(h_{k+1}\succ h_k\) while retaining every constraint and certificate component selected at \(h_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic selection of a strictly stronger sparse polynomial relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When stopping tests fail and residual diagnostics show that the current SDP is solved reliably, choose \(h_{k+1}\in\mathcal H(h_k)\) with \(h_{k+1}\succ h_k\), using \(q_k\) to select among admissible order or support increases. Require nesting: every moment constraint, localizing constraint, and certificate term present at \(h_k\) remains present at \(h_{k+1}\). Build the added blocks, transfer only compatible state, and solve the stronger relaxation. Terminate escalation only upon a stopping certificate or a declared resource limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the current SDP is reliable but insufficient, select a nested stronger hierarchy state, add its blocks, and solve again.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Escalation

children.title: Precision Escalation
children.top_down_role: Movement to higher-precision numerical computation.

assumptions_latex: A fixed relaxation has failed numerical acceptance tests at working precision \(p_k\).
The relaxation structure and mathematical data remain unchanged during precision escalation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure distinguishes precision-sensitive numerical failure from insufficiency of the relaxation model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Increasing arithmetic precision without changing the polynomial relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If stagnation, inconsistent bounds, loss of cone interiority, or failed residual validation is attributable to numerical error, choose \(p_{k+1}>p_k\). Re-encode problem coefficients at precision \(p_{k+1}\), recompute scaling and numerical factorizations, transfer only state whose values can be represented consistently, and resolve the same relaxation. Recompute all acceptance diagnostics at the higher precision. If validation succeeds, retain the result; if failure persists after the prescribed precision schedule, report numerical failure or escalate the relaxation only when independent diagnostics indicate model insufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raise arithmetic precision, rebuild precision-dependent numerical data, and resolve the same relaxation before deciding that a stronger model is needed.
knowledge_statements.title: Precision Escalation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm cleanly separates arithmetic-precision escalation from relaxation escalation, but no source supports the prescribed rebuilding, transfer, and diagnostic policy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Obstructions to finite convergence of LP polynomial relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the polynomial feasible set, normalized constraint polynomials, index-set mapping, and LP relaxations defined in the source setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf K\subset\mathbb R^n\) and the LP-relaxation bounds \(L_d\) be as in the source setup. Finite convergence cannot occur if either (a) there exists a global minimizer \(\mathbf x^*\in\mathbf K\) such that \(\widehat g_j(\mathbf x^*)>0\) for every \(j=1,\ldots,m\), or (b) there exist \(\mathbf x_0\in\mathbf K\) and a global minimizer \(\mathbf x^*\in\mathbf K\) such that \(f(\mathbf x_0)>f^*\) and \(J(\mathbf x_0)=J(\mathbf x^*)\). Thus \(L_d\ne f^*\) for every \(d\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the specified LP hierarchy, no finite relaxation order attains the global optimum if a global minimizer makes every normalized constraint strictly positive, or if a nonoptimal feasible point has the same source-defined index set J as a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf K\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ and }(L_d)_{d\in\mathbb N}\text{ are defined as in the source setup.}

\left[\exists\mathbf x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf x\in\mathbf K}f(\mathbf x):\ \widehat g_j(\mathbf x^*)>0\ \forall j=1,\ldots,m\right]\lor\left[\exists\mathbf x_0\in\mathbf K,\ \exists\mathbf x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf x\in\mathbf K}f(\mathbf x):\ f(\mathbf x_0)>f^*\land J(\mathbf x_0)=J(\mathbf x^*)\right]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall d\in\mathbb N,\quad L_d\ne f^*.

children.title: Restricted-Gram Cones
children.top_down_role: LP-, SOCP-, and factor-width inner approximations of SOS Gram cones.

children.title: DSOS Family
children.top_down_role: Linear-programming-compatible restricted Gram models.

children.title: Diagonally Dominant Gram Models
children.top_down_role: Gram models organized by diagonal dominance.

assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) has degree at most \(2d\).
\(z_d(x)\) is a fixed vector of monomials of degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership is certified by linear coefficient-matching equations and linear inequalities expressing diagonal dominance of \(Q\), hence by a linear program.

notation.meaning: monomial basis vector through degree d
polynomial represented by the Gram model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard DSOS definition using a diagonally dominant Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polynomial \(p\) is diagonally-dominant-sum-of-squares, or DSOS with respect to \(z_d\), if there exists a symmetric matrix \(Q\) such that \[p(x)=z_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_d(x)\] and \[Q_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}|Q_{ij}|\quad\text{for every }i.\] Equivalently, introduce variables \(t_{ij}\ge0\) satisfying \(-t_{ij}\le Q_{ij}\le t_{ij}\) and \(Q_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}t_{ij}\). Diagonal dominance implies \(Q\succeq0\), so every such polynomial is a sum of squares, although the converse need not hold for the fixed basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial is DSOS when it has a Gram representation whose symmetric Gram matrix is diagonally dominant; membership reduces to linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonally Dominant Gram Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is the standard fixed-basis DSOS Gram model, and the LP formulation and SOS implication are stated consistently, but this specialized definition has no citation.

children.title: LP-Based DSOS Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy families based on polyhedral Gram restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: LP-Based DSOS Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated quadratic-module hierarchy with diagonally dominant Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), set \(g_0=1\), and let \(z_d(x)\) contain all monomials of degree at most \(d\). At order \(r\), the DSOS lower bound is
\[\rho_r^{\mathrm{DSOS}}=\sup\left\{\gamma:f-\gamma=\sum_{j=0}^m \sigma_jg_j,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le 2r,\ \sigma_j=z_{d_j}^{\mathsf T}Q_jz_{d_j},\ Q_j\ \text{diagonally dominant}\right\}.\]
Diagonal dominance is represented by linear inequalities after introducing variables for absolute values, so the bound is computable by linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace SOS multipliers in a truncated polynomial-optimization certificate by diagonally dominant Gram multipliers; the resulting relaxation is a linear program.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(d_j=\lfloor(2r-\deg g_j)/2\rfloor\) whenever \(2r\ge\deg g_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{DSOS}}\le \inf_{x\in K}f(x)\), and the defining relaxation is an LP.

notation.meaning: vector of monomials of degree at most d
Gram matrix of the j-th multiplier

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows the standard replacement of SOS Gram cones by diagonally dominant Gram cones
exact DSOS hierarchy source and convergence qualifications require confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LP-based DSOS construction fits the leaf, but no source is cited for this precise truncated hierarchy. The summation also includes every multiplier although d_j is defined only when 2r is at least deg(g_j); the convention for omitted multipliers requires authoritative confirmation.

children.title: SDSOS Family
children.top_down_role: Second-order-cone-compatible restricted Gram models.

children.title: Scaled Diagonally Dominant Gram Models
children.top_down_role: Gram models organized by scaled diagonal dominance.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Diagonally Dominant Gram Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SDSOS polynomials defined through scaled diagonally dominant Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A symmetric matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S^N\) is scaled diagonally dominant if there exists a positive diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(DQD\) is diagonally dominant, namely
\[(DQD)_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}|(DQD)_{ij}|\quad(i=1,\ldots,N).\]
For a monomial vector \(z(x)\), a polynomial \(p\) is scaled diagonally-dominant-sum-of-squares (SDSOS) relative to \(z\) if
\[p(x)=z(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz(x)\]
for some scaled diagonally dominant \(Q\). This Gram restriction admits a second-order-cone representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDSOS polynomial has a Gram matrix that becomes diagonally dominant after positive diagonal scaling; membership is second-order-cone representable.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(z\) is a fixed monomial vector compatible with \(\deg p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\mathrm{SDSOS}(z)\) if and only if it has a scaled diagonally dominant Gram matrix in the basis \(z\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of scaled diagonal dominance and SDSOS Gram representability
authoritative SDSOS definition and SOCP locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the scaled-diagonally-dominant Gram-model leaf and is mathematically standard, but the scaled-diagonal-dominance convention and SOCP-representability claim have no inspectable citation.

children.title: SOCP-Based SDSOS Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy families based on second-order-cone Gram restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: SOCP-Based SDSOS Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated quadratic-module hierarchy using scaled diagonally dominant Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(g_0=1\). The order-\(r\) SDSOS bound is
\[\rho_r^{\mathrm{SDSOS}}=\sup\left\{\gamma:f-\gamma=\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2r,\ \sigma_j=z_{d_j}^{\mathsf T}Q_jz_{d_j},\ Q_j\ \text{scaled diagonally dominant}\right\}.\]
The scaled-diagonal-dominance constraints decompose into positive-semidefinite constraints on \(2\times2\) principal blocks and therefore yield a second-order-cone program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using SDSOS rather than SOS multipliers produces lower-bounding polynomial relaxations representable as second-order-cone programs.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(d_j=\lfloor(2r-\deg g_j)/2\rfloor\) for every included multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{SDSOS}}\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\), and each finite-order relaxation is an SOCP.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard SDSOS substitution in a truncated quadratic module
exact hierarchy source and any convergence assumptions require confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hierarchy belongs in this leaf, but its exact formulation is uncited. Moreover, scaled diagonal dominance is normally characterized by a sum of PSD matrices supported on coordinate pairs, not simply by PSD constraints on the 2-by-2 principal blocks of Q; a source is needed to establish and correctly state the intended representation.

children.title: Factor-Width Cones
children.top_down_role: Restricted PSD factorization families interpolating between elementary cones and full SDP.

children.title: Fixed Factor-Width Models
children.top_down_role: Cone families indexed by permitted local factor size.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Factor-Width Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite Gram restrictions assembled from bounded-size supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(1\le k\le N\), a matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S^N\) has factor width at most \(k\) if there exist positive-semidefinite matrices \(Q_I\in\mathbb S_+^{|I|}\), indexed by subsets \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) with \(|I|\le k\), such that
\[Q=\sum_{|I|\le k}E_I^{\mathsf T}Q_IE_I,\]
where \(E_I\) extracts the coordinates in \(I\). A fixed-factor-width Gram model requires \(p(x)=z(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz(x)\) with such a matrix \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed factor-width Gram matrix is a sum of positive-semidefinite matrices supported on coordinate subsets of size at most k.
assumptions_latex: \(z(x)\in\mathbb R[x]^N\) is fixed.
\(1\le k\le N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership is representable using positive-semidefinite blocks of order at most \(k\).

notation.meaning: coordinate-extraction matrix for index set I

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard decomposition characterization of bounded factor width
factor-width convention and authoritative locator require confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decomposition is appropriate for the fixed-factor-width leaf, but no source establishes the adopted at-most-k support convention or its equivalence to the intended definition of factor width.

children.title: Block Factor-Width Models
children.top_down_role: Factor-width restrictions adapted to existing block structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Factor-Width Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factor-width restriction measured in blocks of a prescribed coordinate partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal B=(B_1,\ldots,B_b)\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\). A matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S^N\) has block factor width at most \(k\) relative to \(\mathcal B\) if
\[Q=\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,b\},\ |J|\le k}E_{B_J}^{\mathsf T}Q_JE_{B_J},\qquad Q_J\succeq0,\]
where \(B_J=\bigcup_{j\in J}B_j\). A block factor-width polynomial model imposes this restriction on a Gram matrix \(Q\) satisfying \(p(x)=z(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block factor width decomposes a Gram matrix into positive-semidefinite pieces supported on unions of at most k prescribed blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B\) is a fixed partition of the Gram coordinates.
\(1\le k\le b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model uses PSD constraints of size at most \(\max_{|J|\le k}|B_J|\) and preserves the prescribed block structure.

notation.meaning: union of blocks indexed by J
extraction matrix for the block union

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: natural block-partition extension of factor-width decomposition
multiple block factor-width conventions exist; exact intended convention needs a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the block factor-width leaf, but multiple block factor-width definitions occur in the literature. An authoritative source is required for this partition-based decomposition and the associated block-size claim.

children.title: Restricted-Gram Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Enrichment families bridging restricted Gram cones and full SOS.

children.title: Basis-Change Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening through changes of Gram coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Change Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested strengthening obtained by admitting restricted Gram certificates in additional bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z(x)\in\mathbb R[x]^N\), let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N\) be a restricted Gram cone, and let \(T_1,\ldots,T_s\) be nonsingular matrices. Define
\[\mathcal P_s=\left\{p:p(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^s (T_\ell z(x))^{\mathsf T}Q_\ell(T_\ell z(x)),\ Q_\ell\in\mathcal C\right\}.\]
Then \(\mathcal P_s\subseteq\mathcal P_{s+1}\subseteq\mathrm{SOS}\) when the first \(s\) bases are retained. Consequently, replacing a single-basis restricted certificate by the multi-basis certificate can only enlarge the feasible positivity cone and strengthen the associated lower-bound relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding restricted Gram certificates expressed in new invertible bases creates nested inner approximations of the SOS cone and cannot weaken the lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N\) is a convex cone.
\(T_1,ldots,T_{s+1}\) are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_s\subseteq\mathcal P_{s+1}\subseteq\mathrm{SOS}\), so the corresponding maximization lower bounds are nondecreasing.

notation.meaning: positivity cone generated by the first s bases

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cone inclusion follows directly from retaining all previously admitted basis certificates
specific basis-update scheme and literature source are absent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-cone property fits the leaf, but no source identifies this sum-over-bases construction as the intended basis-change strengthening scheme. The assumptions also contain the malformed text "T_1,ldots,T_{s+1}" instead of a properly delimited LaTeX expression.

children.title: Column-Cut Enrichment Calculus
children.top_down_role: Adaptive enrichment of polyhedral and second-order models.

children.title: Column Generation
children.top_down_role: Adaptive enrichment through additional basis or conic columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master enrichment by adding improving Gram atoms or local PSD blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite atom set \(A_0\), solve the restricted master relaxation over \(\operatorname{cone}(A_t)\) and obtain an optimal dual vector \(y_t\). A pricing oracle returns an admissible atom \(a_t\) minimizing reduced cost \(c(a)-\langle y_t,M(a)\rangle\). If this value is below \(-\varepsilon\), set \(A_{t+1}=A_t\cup\{a_t\}\) and re-solve; otherwise stop. The output is the final restricted-master bound together with its generated Gram atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a restricted conic master problem and add an admissible Gram atom having reduced cost below the chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is feasible and attains a dual solution.
The pricing oracle minimizes reduced cost over the admissible atom family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with reduced cost at least \(-\varepsilon\) certifies that no single admissible column improves the current master by more than the pricing tolerance.

notation.meaning: active Gram-atom set at iteration t
master-problem column induced by atom a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic conic column-generation template specialized to Gram atoms
master formulation, sign convention, and restricted-Gram source require specification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Column Generation, but the master problem, optimization direction, atom normalization, and reduced-cost sign convention are unspecified. Reduced cost at least -epsilon alone does not generally bound objective improvement by epsilon, so the stated conclusion requires a precise formulation and source.

children.title: Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Adaptive strengthening through additional valid constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-approximation enrichment using inequalities violated by the current Gram candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite valid-inequality set \(H_0\) for a target Gram cone \(\mathcal K\). At iteration \(t\), optimize the master problem subject to all inequalities in \(H_t\), obtaining \(Q_t\). A separation oracle either returns \((A_t,b_t)\) satisfying \(\langle A_t,Q\rangle\ge b_t\) for every \(Q\in\mathcal K\) but \(\langle A_t,Q_t\rangle<b_t-\varepsilon\), or declares no such violation. In the former case set \(H_{t+1}=H_t\cup\{(A_t,b_t)\}\); otherwise stop and output \(Q_t\) and the master bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve an outer approximation, separate the current Gram matrix from the target cone, add a violated valid inequality, and repeat.
assumptions_latex: Every generated inequality is valid for \(\mathcal K\).
The master problem and separation oracle attain their outputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each added cut excludes \(Q_t\) without excluding any member of \(\mathcal K\); stopping gives \(\varepsilon\)-separation relative to the oracle.
review_flags: restricted-Gram separation source and target-cone convention require confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cutting-plane template fits the leaf, but no source specifies the restricted-Gram target cone, separation model, or the meaning of the oracle-relative epsilon guarantee.

children.title: Pricing Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for identifying useful columns in restricted models.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle contract for detecting an improving column in restricted-Gram enrichment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For dual master vector \(y\), admissible atom family \(\mathcal A\), atom cost \(c(a)\), and column map \(M(a)\), a valid pricing interface returns
\[v(y)=\inf_{a\in\mathcal A}\bigl(c(a)-\langle y,M(a)\rangle\bigr)\]
and, when attained, a minimizing atom. With tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the interface reports an improving column exactly when \(v(y)<-\varepsilon\); otherwise it returns a certificate that every admissible atom has reduced cost at least \(-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pricing oracle minimizes reduced cost over all admissible Gram atoms and either supplies an improving atom or certifies none exceeds tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The master uses the reduced-cost convention \(c(a)-\langle y,M(a)\rangle\).
The oracle is exact or supplies a stated global error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(y)<-\varepsilon\) triggers enrichment; \(v(y)\ge-\varepsilon\) is the pricing stopping condition.

notation.meaning: master column associated with atom a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional reduced-cost oracle contract for column generation
sign convention and restricted-Gram atom family need an authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and oracle contract fit Pricing Interfaces, but the reduced-cost convention is formulation-dependent. The alternative assumption allowing a global error bound is not reconciled with the exact threshold and certificate stated in the conclusion.

children.title: Separation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for identifying violated strengthening constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle contract for separating a candidate from a target Gram cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a closed convex target cone \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb S^N\), a candidate \(Q\in\mathbb S^N\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a separation interface either certifies \(\operatorname{dist}(Q,\mathcal K)\le\varepsilon\), or returns \(A\in\mathbb S^N\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[\langle A,X\rangle\ge b\quad\text{for all }X\in\mathcal K,\qquad \langle A,Q\rangle<b.\]
The returned pair defines a valid cut excluding the candidate while retaining the target cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separation oracle either certifies approximate cone membership or returns a valid linear inequality violated by the candidate Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Distance is measured in a fixed norm declared by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The response is either an \(\varepsilon\)-membership certificate or a separating inequality valid on \(\mathcal K\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard weak-separation oracle specification for a closed convex cone
norm, tolerance model, and restricted-Gram source require confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weak-separation contract fits the leaf, but an authoritative source is needed for the norm-dependent epsilon-membership alternative and its relationship to the returned separating inequality.

children.title: Enrichment Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Criteria governing termination of adaptive column or cut enrichment.

knowledge_statements.title: Enrichment Stopping Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based certificate combining pricing, separation, and master-solution checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(t\), let \(r_t\) be the minimum reduced cost returned by pricing, \(s_t\) the maximum violation returned by separation, and \(g_t\) the primal-dual gap of the restricted master. For prescribed tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_g\ge0\), the enrichment certificate is
\[r_t\ge-\varepsilon_p,\qquad s_t\le\varepsilon_s,\qquad g_t\le\varepsilon_g.\]
When all three inequalities hold and the oracles are globally valid, no admissible column or cut violates its oracle tolerance, and the current master has been solved to its declared optimization tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when pricing finds no improving column, separation finds no violated cut, and the restricted master’s primal-dual gap is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: Pricing and separation bounds are global over their declared families.
The restricted master has valid primal and dual bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities certify oracle-relative and master-relative termination at tolerances \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_g)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: combines conventional column-generation, cutting-plane, and conic-solver termination tests
does not certify exact target-cone optimality unless oracle families are complete

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits Enrichment Stopping Criteria, but the sign and definition of maximum separation violation and the global validity of both oracle bounds require a sourced formulation. The certificate is only oracle-family-relative and does not establish target-cone optimality without completeness assumptions.

children.title: Intermediate LP-SOCP-SDP Families

knowledge_statements.title: Intermediate LP-SOCP-SDP Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested Gram cones interpolate between polyhedral, second-order-cone, and semidefinite models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal C_{m LP}\), \(\mathcal C_{m SOCP}\), and \(\mathcal C_{m SDP}=\mathbb S_+^N\) be Gram cones satisfying
\[\mathcal C_{m LP}\subseteq\mathcal C_{m SOCP}\subseteq\mathcal C_{m SDP}.\]
For a polynomial lower-bound relaxation obtained by requiring each multiplier Gram matrix to lie in one of these cones, denote the optimal bounds by \(\rho_{m LP}\), \(\rho_{m SOCP}\), and \(\rho_{m SDP}\). Whenever all formulations use identical degrees, bases, and polynomial identities,
\[\rho_{m LP}\le\rho_{m SOCP}\le\rho_{m SDP}\le f^*,\]
where \(f^*\) is the original minimization optimum. Additional nested cones give intermediate tractability-strength levels by the same inclusion argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested LP-, SOCP-, and SDP-representable Gram cones yield correspondingly nested lower bounds when all other relaxation choices are fixed.
assumptions_latex: All relaxations use the same polynomial identities, degrees, and bases.
Each Gram cone is an inner approximation of \(\mathbb S_+^N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{m LP}\le\rho_{m SOCP}\le\rho_{m SDP}\le f^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertices of the Intersection of Two Simplices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General simplicial-intersection geometry; the illustrative square example is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_1\) and \(\Delta_2\) be two \(n\)-simplices whose vertices belong to a finite set \(X\). Every vertex of \(\Delta_1\cap\Delta_2\) is either a common vertex of \(\Delta_1\) and \(\Delta_2\) or a circuit intersection point generated by an affine dependency among vertices from their union.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vertices of the intersection of two n-simplices consist of their common vertices together with circuit intersection points arising from their vertex configuration.
assumptions_latex: \Delta_1,\Delta_2\text{ are }n\text{-simplices}
V(\Delta_1)\cup V(\Delta_2)\subseteq X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General point-configuration construction associated with a minimal affine dependency; the square example is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polytope with vertices \(v_i\), let \(\lambda\) be a minimal affine dependency of \(V(X)\), and set \(\Lambda=\sum_{i\in P(\lambda)}\lambda_i\). The relative interiors of \(\operatorname{conv}\{v_i:i\in P(\lambda)\}\) and \(\operatorname{conv}\{v_i:i\in N(\lambda)\}\) intersect at the unique point \[\bar x=\sum_{i\in P(\lambda)}\frac{\lambda_i}{\Lambda}v_i=\sum_{i\in N(\lambda)}-\frac{\lambda_i}{\Lambda}v_i.\] This point is called a circuit intersection point, and \(C(X)\) denotes the set of all circuit intersection points of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a minimal affine dependency, the relative interiors of the convex hulls of its positive and negative vertices meet at one uniquely determined point, called the circuit intersection point. C(X) collects all such points.

children.title: Simplicial-Circuit Families

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial-Circuit Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit polynomials whose outer exponents form an even lattice simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha(0),\ldots,\alpha(r)\in(2\mathbb N)^n\) be affinely independent, let \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}\{\alpha(0),\ldots,\alpha(r)\}\), and write uniquely \(\beta=\sum_{j=0}^r\lambda_j\alpha(j)\), where \(\lambda_j>0\) and \(\sum_j\lambda_j=1\). A simplicial-circuit polynomial is \(f(x)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_jx^{\alpha(j)}+c_\beta x^\beta\), with \(c_j>0\). Its circuit number is \(\Theta_f=\prod_{j=0}^r(c_j/\lambda_j)^{\lambda_j}\). It is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^n\) exactly when \(c_\beta\ge-\Theta_f\) if \(\beta\in(2\mathbb N)^n\), and exactly when \(|c_\beta|\le\Theta_f\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplicial circuit has positive even outer terms and one inner term; its global nonnegativity is characterized exactly by its circuit number.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha(0),\ldots,\alpha(r)\in(2\mathbb N)^n\) are affinely independent.
\(\beta\) lies in the relative interior of their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) precisely under the stated circuit-number inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Support Circuits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction when the inner exponent lies in a proper simplex face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{\alpha(0),\ldots,\alpha(r)\}\), with even affinely independent vertices, and suppose \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}F\) for a proper face \(F\) of \(S\). If \(J\) indexes the vertices of \(F\), then the barycentric coordinates of \(\beta\) satisfy \(\lambda_j>0\) for \(j\in J\) and \(\lambda_j=0\) otherwise. Consequently, \(f=\sum_{j=0}^r c_jx^{\alpha(j)}+c_\beta x^\beta\) decomposes as \(f=q+\sum_{j\notin J}c_jx^{\alpha(j)}\), where \(q=\sum_{j\in J}c_jx^{\alpha(j)}+c_\beta x^\beta\) is the circuit polynomial on \(F\). Thus \(f\ge0\) exactly when \(q\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary-supported circuit reduces to the circuit on the minimal containing face, plus nonnegative outer monomial squares.
assumptions_latex: \(c_j>0\) and every outer exponent is even.
\(\beta\) lies in the relative interior of a proper face \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=q+\sum_{j\notin J}c_jx^{\alpha(j)}\), and \(f\ge0\iff q\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Minimal simplex face containing the inner exponent.
Indices of the vertices of that face.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Dimensional Circuits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuits contained in a proper affine subspace of exponent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le r<n\), let \(\alpha(0),\ldots,\alpha(r)\in(2\mathbb N)^n\) be affinely independent and let \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}\{\alpha(0),\ldots,\alpha(r)\}\). Then \(f(x)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_jx^{\alpha(j)}+c_\beta x^\beta\), with \(c_j>0\), is a lower-dimensional circuit polynomial: its support has affine dimension \(r\), although its variables range over \(\mathbb R^n\). With barycentric coordinates \(\lambda_j\) and circuit number \(\Theta_f=\prod_j(c_j/\lambda_j)^{\lambda_j}\), the usual circuit-number nonnegativity criterion remains valid without requiring full-dimensional support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-dimensional circuit lies in a proper affine subspace of exponent space but obeys the same circuit-number criterion.
assumptions_latex: \(r<n\) and the outer exponents are affinely independent and even.
\(\beta\) lies in their relative interior.
\(c_j>0\) for every outer coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The support has affine dimension \(r\), and nonnegativity is governed by \(\Theta_f\).

notation.meaning: Affine dimension of the circuit support.
Circuit number computed in the support simplex.

children.title: Degenerate Circuit Limits

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Circuit Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous circuit-number limit as barycentric weights approach a simplex face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda^{(k)}\in\mathbb R_{++}^{r+1}\) satisfy \(\sum_j\lambda_j^{(k)}=1\) and \(\lambda^{(k)}\to\bar\lambda\), where some components of \(\bar\lambda\) may vanish. Suppose \(c_j^{(k)}\to\bar c_j>0\). For \(\Theta_k=\prod_j(c_j^{(k)}/\lambda_j^{(k)})^{\lambda_j^{(k)}}\), the convention \(t^t\to1\) as \(t\downarrow0\) gives \(\Theta_k\to\bar\Theta=\prod_{j:\bar\lambda_j>0}(\bar c_j/\bar\lambda_j)^{\bar\lambda_j}\). Hence the limiting circuit inequality is precisely the inequality for the minimal face indexed by the positive components of \(\bar\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When barycentric weights vanish, the circuit number converges to the circuit number on the surviving simplex face.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda^{(k)}>0\), \(\sum_j\lambda_j^{(k)}=1\), and \(\lambda^{(k)}\to\bar\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Theta_k\to\prod_{j:\bar\lambda_j>0}(\bar c_j/\bar\lambda_j)^{\bar\lambda_j}\).

notation.meaning: Circuit number of the surviving face.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The numerical product limit is plausible, but no source is supplied, and the claimed minimal-face interpretation presupposes a fixed exponent simplex and associated exponent sequence that the statement does not introduce.

children.title: Circuit Certificate Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundary regimes where standard circuit certification loses effectiveness.

knowledge_statements.title: Circuit Certificate Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp coefficient boundary beyond which a circuit certificate cannot establish nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the circuit family \(f_c(x)=1+x^2+cx\) on \(\mathbb R\), the outer exponents are \(0\) and \(2\), the inner exponent is \(1\), the barycentric weights are \(1/2,1/2\), and the circuit number is \(\Theta=2\). Therefore \(f_c\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R\) exactly when \(|c|\le2\). At \(|c|=2\), the polynomial has a real double zero. If \(|c|>2\), its minimum equals \(1-c^2/4<0\), so the circuit inequality fails and no nonnegativity certificate for this circuit polynomial exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family 1+x²+cx is nonnegative exactly for |c|≤2; crossing this sharp circuit boundary produces a negative minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(c\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_c\ge0\iff |c|\le2\), while \(\min_x f_c(x)=1-c^2/4<0\) for \(|c|>2\).

notation.meaning: Its circuit number, equal to two.

children.title: Geometric-Programming SONC Models
children.top_down_role: Circuit-certificate formulations connected to geometric programming.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric-Programming SONC Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-allocation formulation of a sufficient SONC certificate as a geometric program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=\sum_{j=1}^s c_jx^{\alpha_j}-\sum_{i=1}^t d_ix^{\beta_i}\), where \(c_j,d_i>0\), every \(\alpha_j\) is even, and each \(\beta_i\) has barycentric weights \(\lambda_{ij}>0\) on a selected affinely independent set \(A_i\) of outer exponents. A SONC certificate is obtained if variables \(a_{ij}>0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i:j\in A_i}a_{ij}\le c_j\) and \(d_i\le\prod_{j\in A_i}(a_{ij}/\lambda_{ij})^{\lambda_{ij}}\). Equivalently, \(d_i\prod_{j\in A_i}(\lambda_{ij}/a_{ij})^{\lambda_{ij}}\le1\); together with the allocation inequalities, these are geometric-program constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocating positive outer coefficients among candidate circuits yields monomial and posynomial constraints forming a geometric-program SONC certificate.
assumptions_latex: All outer exponents \(\alpha_j\) are even and \(c_j>0\).
Each \(\beta_i\) lies in the relative interior of its selected outer simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible allocations \(a_{ij}\) produce a SONC decomposition of \(p\) and a geometric-program feasibility model.

notation.meaning: Outer-exponent simplex assigned to the i-th inner term.
Outer coefficient allocated to circuit i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The allocation model is plausible and fits a representation container, but its exact sufficiency and geometric-program formulation require an authoritative SONC source.

children.title: Second-Order-Cone SONC Models
children.top_down_role: SOCP representations of circuit positivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone SONC Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted SOCP representation for circuit inequalities with rational barycentric weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a circuit inequality \(t\le\prod_{j=0}^r z_j^{\lambda_j}\), where \(z_j\ge0\), \(t\ge0\), \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb Q_{++}\), and \(\sum_j\lambda_j=1\). After clearing denominators and padding the corresponding weighted product to a power of two, introduce auxiliary variables for a binary tree of geometric means. Every tree relation has the form \(u^2\le vw\), with \(u,v,w\ge0\), which is a rotated second-order-cone constraint. Taking \(z_j=a_j/\lambda_j\) and \(t=|c_\beta|\), or \(t=-c_\beta\) for an even inner exponent, gives an exact lifted SOCP representation of the circuit-number constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rational weighted geometric-mean inequalities defining circuit positivity admit exact lifted representations using rotated second-order cones.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb Q_{++}\) and \(\sum_j\lambda_j=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The circuit inequality has a finite lifted representation by constraints \(u^2\le vw\) with nonnegative variables.

notation.meaning: Scaled outer coefficient in the weighted geometric mean.
Magnitude constrained by the circuit number.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An exact rational weighted-geometric-mean lift is plausible, but the padding construction and its applicability to the stated circuit constraint require a specific authoritative source.

children.title: Cancellation-Free SONC Representations
children.top_down_role: Generator decompositions avoiding cancellation among certificate components.

knowledge_statements.title: Cancellation-Free SONC Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SONC decompositions whose component coefficients never cancel at a shared exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=\sum_{k=1}^N q_k+\sum_{\alpha\in E}r_\alpha x^\alpha\), where every \(q_k\) is a nonnegative circuit polynomial and every remainder coefficient satisfies \(r_\alpha\ge0\) with \(\alpha\in(2\mathbb N)^n\). This representation is cancellation-free if, for every exponent \(\gamma\), all nonzero coefficients of \(x^\gamma\) contributed by the summands have one common sign. Equivalently, no pair of summands contributes coefficients \(a\) and \(b\) at the same exponent with \(ab<0\). The coefficient of each monomial of \(p\) is then the sign-consistent sum of its component coefficients, so certificate verification requires no cancellation between circuit generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A SONC decomposition is cancellation-free when all contributions to each shared monomial have the same sign.
assumptions_latex: Each \(q_k\) is a nonnegative circuit polynomial.
Each remainder term is a nonnegative monomial square.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every shared exponent \(\gamma\), component coefficients are sign-consistent and never cancel.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed sign-consistency definition is internally coherent and the content kind fits, but no source establishes that it matches the intended technical meaning of cancellation-free SONC representations.

children.title: SONC Optimization Families

children.title: Unconstrained SONC Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Circuit-based lower-bound families for global nonnegativity.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained SONC Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower bound obtained by shifting a polynomial into a degree-bounded SONC cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), and let \(C_{\mathrm{SONC},d}\) denote the cone generated by nonnegative circuit polynomials and nonnegative monomial squares of degree at most \(2d\). The order-\(d\) unconstrained SONC bound is \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in C_{\mathrm{SONC},d}\}\). Every feasible \(\gamma\) satisfies \(f(x)-\gamma\ge0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), hence \(\rho_d\le f^*=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\). Moreover, nested cones give \(\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\) whenever \(C_{\mathrm{SONC},d}\subseteq C_{\mathrm{SONC},d+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift the polynomial by the largest scalar placing it in a bounded-degree SONC cone; the result is a monotone global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(C_{\mathrm{SONC},d}\) contains only globally nonnegative polynomials.
The degree-truncated cones are nested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\le f^*\).

notation.meaning: Unconstrained global infimum of the polynomial.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound and nesting implications are valid under the stated cone assumptions, but the precise degree-truncated SONC cone and relaxation convention require a SONC source.

children.title: Constrained SONC Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Circuit certificate families adapted to constrained domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained SONC Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-indexed SONC lower bounds using products of nonnegative constraint polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), choose a finite product set \(G_q=\{\prod_{i=1}^m g_i^{
u_i}:
u\in\{0,1\}^m,\ |
u|\le q\}\). At order \(d\), maximize \(\gamma\) subject to \(f-\gamma=\sum_{h\in G_q}s_hh\), where every \(s_h\) is SONC, every product obeys \(\deg(s_hh)\le2d\), and absent terms are assigned zero multipliers. Output the optimal value \(ho_{d,q}\). Since \(s_h(x)h(x)\ge0\) on \(K\), every feasible value satisfies \(ho_{d,q}\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply SONC certificates by bounded products of constraints and increase degree and product order to obtain valid constrained lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each multiplier \(s_h\) belongs to the SONC cone.
All products satisfy the prescribed degree bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs a valid bound \(\rho_{d,q}\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Constraint products of order at most q.
SONC multiplier associated with product h.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed certificate yields a valid bound, but the square-free product hierarchy is a specialized variant without a source, and the admissible domains of d and q are not stated.

children.title: Fewnomial SONC Regime
children.top_down_role: High-degree sparse-support problems naturally aligned with circuit geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Fewnomial SONC Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-combinatorial bound for enumerating candidate circuits in sparse high-degree polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a polynomial support be partitioned into \(A\subseteq(2\mathbb N)^n\), containing \(s\) possible outer exponents, and \(B\subseteq\mathbb N^n\), containing \(t\) possible inner exponents. A candidate simplicial circuit uses an affinely independent subset \(U\subseteq A\) of size at most \(n+1\) and a point \(\beta\in B\cap\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}U\). Consequently, exhaustive support-based enumeration examines at most \(t\sum_{k=1}^{n+1}\binom{s}{k}\) pairs \((U,\beta)\), before affine-independence and containment tests. This bound depends on support cardinalities and dimension, but not on the numerical magnitude of the polynomial degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Candidate SONC circuits can be enumerated from sparse support in a count controlled by support size and dimension, not degree magnitude.
assumptions_latex: Circuit outer sets are affinely independent subsets of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of examined candidates is at most \(t\sum_{k=1}^{n+1}\binom{s}{k}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expression is a plausible upper bound on candidate-pair enumeration, but it excludes the cost of geometric tests and exponent encoding. A source is needed to support its placement as a fewnomial SONC complexity bound.

notation.meaning: Polynomial with one distinguished, potentially negative term.
Circuit number determined by the outer coefficients and barycentric weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit-form polynomial AGE certificate on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the polynomial \(p(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i x^{\alpha_i}+c_\beta x^\beta\), define \(\Theta_p=\prod_{i=1}^m(c_i/\lambda_i)^{\lambda_i}\). If \(\beta\notin(2\mathbb N)^n\) and \(|c_\beta|\le\Theta_p\), then \(p(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). If \(\beta\in(2\mathbb N)^n\), the weaker condition \(c_\beta\ge-\Theta_p\) suffices. Thus the coefficient vector admits an arithmetic-geometric-exponential certificate specialized to polynomial monomials; the distinction between even and non-even \(\beta\) accounts for the possible sign of \(x^\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A circuit polynomial is globally nonnegative when its distinguished coefficient is bounded by the circuit number, with an absolute-value condition for a non-even inner exponent.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial AGE Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the circuit-number criterion. The assumptions also do not explicitly require the inner exponent beta to lie in N^n, which is necessary for p to be a polynomial. An authoritative polynomial AGE/SONC theorem locator is required.

\(c_i\ge0\) for every \(i\ne k\).

The coefficient vector \(c\) belongs to \(C_{\mathrm{AGE},k}(A)\) if and only if there exists \(

children.title: Partial-Dualization SAGE Models
children.top_down_role: SAGE formulations obtained through selective dualization.

assumptions_latex: A SAGE optimization model has a closed convex conic formulation with variables \(z\in K\), affine balance equations \(Bz=b\), and objective \(q^Tz\).
A relative-interior feasible point exists and the primal value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partially dualized saddle model has the same optimal value as the original SAGE conic model.

notation.meaning: Product of AGE relative-entropy or exponential cones.
Multipliers for the selected affine constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic selective dualization of affine coupling in a lifted SAGE model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the SAGE conic problem \[p^*=\inf\{q^Tz:z\in K,\ Bz=b,\ Hz=h\}.\] Dualizing only \(Bz=b\) produces the saddle representation \[p^*=\sup_{y}\ \inf\{q^Tz+y^T(Bz-b):z\in K,\ Hz=h\}.\] The cone membership and the undualized equations \(Hz=h\) remain in the inner convex problem. Under the stated relative-interior condition, selective dualization introduces no duality gap. Choosing \(Bz=b\) as the exponent-balance or coefficient-assembly equations yields partial-dualization SAGE formulations that can reduce explicit coupling while retaining separable AGE cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected affine coupling constraints in a conic SAGE model may be dualized while AGE cone constraints remain primal; under regularity, the resulting saddle model is exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Dualization SAGE Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a generic conic partial-dualization statement rather than a sourced SAGE-specific formulation. A source must identify which SAGE equations are dualized and provide sufficient regularity conditions for the asserted equality of values.

notation.meaning: Best lower bound certified by the polynomial SAGE cone.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level unconstrained lower bound for a fixed polynomial SAGE cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unconstrained polynomial SAGE bound is \[f_{\mathrm{SAGE}}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in C_{\mathrm{PSAGE}}(A\cup\{0\})\}.\] Every feasible \(\gamma\) satisfies \(f(x)-\gamma\ge0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and therefore \(\gamma\le f^*\). Hence \(f_{\mathrm{SAGE}}\le f^*\). The bound is computed by expressing \(f-\gamma\) as a sum of polynomial AGE certificates and optimizing \(\gamma\) through the associated relative-entropy or exponential-cone formulation; equality with \(f^*\) is not guaranteed at the first level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest constant whose subtraction leaves a polynomial SAGE certificate is a valid, tractable lower bound on the unconstrained global minimum.
