knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_r\le f_{r+1}\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-truncated constraint-product hierarchy with polynomial SAGE multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At order \(r\), maximize \(\gamma\) subject to a coefficient identity \[f-\gamma=\sum_{(a,b)\in I_r}s_{a,b}(x)h_{a,b}(x),\qquad h_{a,b}(x)=\prod_{j=1}^s g_j(x)^{a_j}(1-g_j(x))^{b_j},\] where every \(s_{a,b}\) has a polynomial SAGE certificate and \(I_r\) enforces the selected degree bound. Output the optimal value \(f_r\). Since each summand is nonnegative on \(K\), \(f_r\) is a valid lower bound. For nested index and support sets, feasibility at order \(r\) implies feasibility at order \(r+1\), so the bounds are monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained SAGE hierarchy certifies positivity using normalized constraint products with SAGE multipliers, producing monotone lower bounds as the allowed degree increases.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained SAGE Hierarchies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source establishes this particular normalized-product hierarchy with polynomial SAGE multipliers. The index sets, support rules, and nesting conditions must be specified. The record describes a hierarchy construction and may be better classified as a representation unless an actual algorithm is sourced.

children.title: Conditional SAGE Certificates
children.top_down_role: SAGE certificates incorporating convex domain descriptions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(c_i>0\) for \(i\ne k\), while \(c_k\in\mathbb R\).
The support function is interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality certifies \(f(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Signomial with one potentially negative coefficient.
Support function of the convex domain.
Nonnegative AGE weights indexed by i not equal to k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-domain AGE certificate expressed with a support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\exp(\alpha_i^Tx)\). A conditional AGE certificate for the distinguished index \(k\) is a vector \(
u\in\mathbb R_+^{m-1}\) such that, with \[y=\sum_{i
e k}
u_i(\alpha_i-\alpha_k),\] one has \[\sigma_X(y)+D(
u,e c_{-k})\le c_k.\] The weighted arithmetic-geometric-mean inequality then implies \(f(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in X\). A conditional SAGE certificate is a decomposition of the coefficient vector into conditional AGE vectors, possibly with different distinguished indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional SAGE replaces global exponent balance by a support-function inequality, thereby certifying signomial nonnegativity only on a specified convex set.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional SAGE Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional AGE formula requires source verification because the support-function argument may need the opposite sign of the displayed exponent imbalance, depending on convention. That sign directly affects validity of the certificate.

children.title: SONC-SAGE Relationships
children.top_down_role: Shared AM-GM, circuit, and generator structures linking polynomial SONC and SAGE cones.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: A Unified Framework of SAGE and SONC Polynomials
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: A Unified Framework of SAGE and SONC Polynomials

children.title: Polynomial SAGE-SONC Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Equivalence family for polynomial circuit and AM-GM certificates.

assumptions_latex: A finite polynomial support \(A\subset\mathbb N^n\) and a common coefficient-coordinate convention are fixed.
Polynomial AGE generators use even outer exponents and the sign-sensitive inner-exponent rule.
SONC generators are nonnegative circuit polynomials on the same support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{PSAGE}}(A)=C_{\mathrm{SONC}}(A)\).

notation.meaning: Cone generated by polynomial AGE certificates on A.
Cone generated by nonnegative circuit polynomials on A.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-support coefficient-cone equivalence under matched polynomial sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated common support and sign conventions, a polynomial belongs to the polynomial SAGE cone if and only if it belongs to the SONC cone: \[C_{\mathrm{PSAGE}}(A)=C_{\mathrm{SONC}}(A).\] More precisely, every polynomial AGE summand can be decomposed into nonnegative circuit polynomials supported on subsets of \(A\), and every nonnegative circuit polynomial is a polynomial AGE certificate. Taking finite conic sums gives equality of the two coefficient cones. This equivalence concerns polynomial SAGE on all of \(\mathbb R^n\); it does not identify the unrestricted signomial SAGE cone with SONC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With matched supports and sign conventions, polynomial SAGE and SONC generate the same coefficient cone because their elementary nonnegative generators coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial SAGE-SONC Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem-level equality of fixed-support polynomial SAGE and SONC cones needs an authoritative theorem locator. Exact support closure, parity, sign-symmetry, and decomposition conventions can change whether equality holds.

children.title: Common Generator Structure
children.top_down_role: Elementary certificate generators shared by the two frameworks.

assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m\in(2\mathbb N)^n\) are affinely independent.
\(\beta\) lies in their relative interior with barycentric weights \(\lambda_i>0\).
\(c_i>0\) for every outer exponent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elementary polynomial AGE generators and nonnegative circuit generators are the same coefficient rays, up to decomposition along lower-dimensional faces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit-supported generators common to polynomial AGE and SONC cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p(x)=\sum_i c_i x^{\alpha_i}+c_\beta x^\beta\), both frameworks use the same arithmetic-geometric-mean test. If \(\beta\notin(2\mathbb N)^n\), the generator is nonnegative exactly when \(|c_\beta|\le\Theta_p\); if \(\beta\in(2\mathbb N)^n\), it is nonnegative exactly when \(c_\beta\ge-\Theta_p\). In SONC terminology this is a nonnegative circuit polynomial. In polynomial SAGE terminology it is an AGE polynomial with one distinguished coefficient. Conic sums of these common generators produce the corresponding certificate cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative circuit polynomial and an elementary polynomial AGE certificate use the same support geometry, circuit number, and coefficient inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Common Generator Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The circuit-number criterion is plausible, but no citation establishes that these are precisely the common generators under the stated polynomial SAGE convention. The conclusion's reference to coefficient rays and lower-dimensional-face decomposition is also unsupported and not stated precisely.

children.title: Signomial-Polynomial Translation
children.top_down_role: Transfer and limitations between exponential and polynomial coordinates.

assumptions_latex: \(p(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha x^\alpha\) is a real polynomial.
The substitution \(x_j=\exp(y_j)\) is applied componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Signomial nonnegativity transfers exactly to the positive orthant, but without additional symmetry it does not certify polynomial nonnegativity on all of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-orthant translation and its boundary for global polynomial positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The logarithmic substitution gives \[s(y)=p(\exp y)=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha\exp(\alpha^Ty),\] and therefore \(s(y)\ge0\) for all \(y\in\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(p(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). This equivalence does not by itself cover points having zero or negative coordinates. Continuity extends it to \(\mathbb R_+^n\), but extension to all of \(\mathbb R^n\) requires sign-symmetry information, such as even outer exponents and the polynomial AGE treatment of non-even inner exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logarithmic substitution exactly equates signomial positivity with polynomial positivity on the positive orthant, but negative coordinates require additional parity and sign analysis.
knowledge_statements.title: Signomial-Polynomial Translation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logarithmic substitution and positive-orthant limitation are precise and fit the failure-boundary container, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for the claimed transfer and parity limitation.

children.title: Classical LP Positivity Families
children.top_down_role: Linear-programming-compatible positivity families for boxes, simplices, polytopes, and normalized semialgebraic sets.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: An Introduction to Polynomial and Semi-Algebraic Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapter 9 LP relaxations and intermediate hierarchies
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: An Introduction to Polynomial and Semi-Algebraic Optimization

children.title: Handelman-Type Certificates
children.top_down_role: Positivity families based on products of defining affine functions.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) is a nonempty compact polytope.
The affine functions \(\ell_j\) define \(P\).
\(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfies \(f(x)>0\) for every \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) has a finite Handelman representation by nonnegative coefficients and products of the defining affine functions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-positivity form of Handelman's theorem for compact polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist a finite set \(I\subset\mathbb N^m\) and coefficients \(c_\alpha\ge0\) such that \[f(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in I}c_\alpha\prod_{j=1}^m\ell_j(x)^{\alpha_j}.\] Every term in this representation is nonnegative on \(P\), so the identity is directly verifiable as a positivity certificate. Restricting \(|\alpha|\le r\) yields a linear-programming certificate search at order \(r\), because matching polynomial coefficients is linear in \(c_\alpha\). Strict positivity and compact polyhedral geometry are essential hypotheses of this completeness statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every polynomial strictly positive on a compact polytope is a nonnegative linear combination of finite products of its defining affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Handelman-Type Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This theorem requires an authoritative Handelman theorem locator. In particular, the necessary dimensional or interior assumptions and requirements on the affine description must be checked; compact nonempty polytope alone may not match the standard stated theorem.

children.title: Krivine-Stengle LP Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Linear certificate hierarchies based on normalized constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) is compact and \(0\le g_j\le1\) on \(K\).
The algebra generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) equals \(\mathbb R[x]\).
\(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) is strictly positive on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) admits a finite normalized Krivine certificate, and the associated degree-truncated LP lower bounds converge to \(\inf_K f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized strict-positivity certificate and its coefficient-matching LP hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There are finitely many coefficients \(c_{\alpha,\beta}\ge0\) such that \[f=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}c_{\alpha,\beta}g^\alpha(1-g)^\beta.\] Consequently, defining \(f_r\) as the largest \(\gamma\) for which \(f-\gamma\) has such a representation using only indices with \(|\alpha|+|\beta|\le r\) gives a linear program after coefficient matching. The bounds satisfy \[f_r\le f_{r+1}\le f^*,\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}f_r=f^*.\] The convergence follows from applying the strict-positivity certificate to \(f-(f^*-\varepsilon)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized constraints and their complements generate LP certificates for strict positivity; increasing the product degree yields monotone lower bounds converging to the constrained minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Krivine-Stengle LP Hierarchies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate and convergence claims need a specific Krivine–Stengle/Handelman-type theorem locator. The normalization, algebra-generation condition, compactness assumptions, and finite certificate form must be verified together before accepting the hierarchy theorem.

children.title: Bernstein Positivity Methods
children.top_down_role: Basis-dependent positivity and subdivision families.

knowledge_statements.title: Bernstein Positivity Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient certificate on a box, including the effect of repeated subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) have coordinatewise degree at most \(d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\). Its tensor-product Bernstein expansion on \([0,1]^n\) is \[p(x)=\sum_{0\leq\alpha\leq d}b_\alpha B_{\alpha,d}(x),\qquad B_{\alpha,d}(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n\binom{d_i}{\alpha_i}x_i^{\alpha_i}(1-x_i)^{d_i-\alpha_i}.\] Because the basis functions are nonnegative and sum to one, \[\min_\alpha b_\alpha\leq p(x)\leq\max_\alpha b_\alpha\quad\text{for every }x\in[0,1]^n.\] Thus \(b_\alpha\geq0\) for every \(\alpha\) certifies nonnegativity. If \(p>0\) on the box, sufficiently fine repeated box subdivision yields positive local Bernstein coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative Bernstein coefficients certify positivity on a box; their extrema bound the polynomial, and subdivision eventually detects every polynomial that is strictly positive there.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) has finite coordinatewise degree.
The domain is affinely normalized to \([0,1]^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_\alpha\geq0\ \forall\alpha\Longrightarrow p(x)\geq0\ \forall x\in[0,1]^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content and content_kind fit the Bernstein-positivity leaf, but the coefficient bounds and eventual positivity under repeated subdivision are nontrivial claims with no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Alternative-Cone Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Expressiveness and invariance boundaries of restricted and support-sensitive positivity cones.

children.title: Restricted-Gram Basis Dependence
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of DSOS and SDSOS strength to Gram coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Gram Basis Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noninvariance of DSOS and SDSOS Gram restrictions under general basis changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\), where \(z\) is a polynomial basis vector. Under an invertible basis change \(w=Tz\), the same polynomial has Gram matrix \(Q'=T^{-\mathsf T}QT^{-1}\). Positive semidefiniteness is preserved by this congruence, but diagonal dominance and scaled diagonal dominance generally are not. For example, let \(Q=I_3\) and let \(R_\rho\) have diagonal entries \(1\) and off-diagonal entries \(\rho\), where \(1/2<\rho<1\). Then \(R_\rho\succ0\), but it is not scaled diagonally dominant. Choosing \(T=R_\rho^{-1/2}\) gives \(T^{-\mathsf T}QT^{-1}=R_\rho\). Hence restricted-Gram membership can change although the represented polynomial does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD Gram representations are invariant under invertible basis changes, whereas DSOS and SDSOS restrictions can disappear after the same change of coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is invertible.
DSOS and SDSOS mean the existence of diagonally dominant and scaled diagonally dominant Gram matrices, respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\text{ DD or SDD}\not\Longrightarrow T^{-\mathsf T}QT^{-1}\text{ DD or SDD}\).

notation.meaning: Polynomial basis vectors related by an invertible transformation.
Gram matrices representing the same polynomial.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the basis-dependence leaf, and the congruence example is internally coherent. An authoritative source is still required for the DSOS/SDSOS noninvariance claim and the scaled-diagonal-dominance separation.

children.title: SOS-SONC-SAGE Expressiveness
children.top_down_role: Separations and relationships among major positivity cones.

knowledge_statements.title: SOS-SONC-SAGE Expressiveness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-equivalence of algebraic, circuit, and relative-entropy positivity cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SOS, SONC, and SAGE cones encode different structures and are not interchangeable without additional hypotheses. The Motzkin polynomial \[m(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4+1-3x^2y^2\] is a nonnegative circuit polynomial and therefore belongs to SONC, but it is not SOS. Under the substitution \(x_i=\exp(y_i)\), a polynomial supported on exponents \(A\subset\mathbb N^n\) becomes the signomial \(\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha\exp(\alpha^{\mathsf T}y)\); compatible nonnegative circuit decompositions yield AGE, hence SAGE, decompositions on the positive orthant. This correspondence does not make global polynomial SOS, SONC, and SAGE membership equivalent, because their domains and admissible decompositions differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS, SONC, and SAGE exploit different structures. Motzkin separates SONC from SOS, while exponential substitution relates circuit certificates to SAGE only on the positive orthant.
assumptions_latex: SONC uses sums of nonnegative circuit polynomials.
SAGE is interpreted for the signomial obtained on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\in\mathrm{SONC}\setminus\mathrm{SOS}\), and the exponential SONC–SAGE correspondence does not imply equality of the three cones.

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of nonnegative circuit polynomials.
Cone of sums of AM/GM exponentials.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind matches the expressiveness leaf, but Motzkin's SONC-versus-SOS separation and the qualified SONC-SAGE correspondence are specialized claims requiring precise citations, especially for the positive-orthant domain and admissible decompositions.

children.title: Support-Sensitive Certificate Gaps
children.top_down_role: Loss of certificate strength under unfavorable exponent geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Sensitive Certificate Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A combinatorial obstruction to circuit certificates using a fixed polynomial support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha x^\alpha\) and suppose a negative coefficient occurs at exponent \(\beta\in A\). A SONC decomposition using no exponents outside \(A\) can cover that term only through a circuit whose positive outer exponents \(V\subseteq A\) are affinely independent and satisfy \(\beta\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}(V)\). Consequently, if no such subset \(V\) exists among the admissible positive exponents, then no support-preserving SONC certificate exists, irrespective of coefficient optimization. Enlarging the support may remove this obstruction, so failure with the original support is not itself a proof that the polynomial is negative or that no lifted certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative monomial must lie inside a suitable simplex of positive exponents. If the fixed support contains no such simplex, a support-preserving SONC certificate is impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(A\subset\mathbb N^n\) is finite.
The decomposition may use only monomials whose exponents belong to \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists V:\beta\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}(V)\Longrightarrow\) no support-preserving SONC decomposition can cover \(c_\beta x^\beta\).

notation.meaning: Candidate outer-exponent set of a circuit.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the support-sensitive gap leaf. The fixed-support obstruction is plausible, but a source must establish the circuit-support necessity and clarify all admissibility conditions on outer exponents before the mathematical formulation can be accepted.

children.title: Domain-Mismatch Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures outside the natural domain geometry of a certificate family.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Mismatch Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A certificate valid on its natural domain need not certify global nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p(x)=x\). On \([0,1]\), its degree-one Bernstein expansion is \[p(x)=0\cdot(1-x)+1\cdot x,\] so its Bernstein coefficients are nonnegative and certify \(p(x)\geq0\) on that interval. Nevertheless, \(p(-1)=-1<0\), and therefore the certificate does not establish nonnegativity on \(\mathbb R\). More generally, box-based Bernstein certificates, polytope-based Handelman certificates, and positive-orthant signomial certificates retain their meaning only after the target domain has been correctly represented. Extending their conclusions beyond that domain requires an independent argument or a domain-compatible reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polynomial x has a nonnegative Bernstein certificate on [0,1] but is negative at −1. Domain-specific certificates cannot be interpreted as global certificates.
assumptions_latex: The Bernstein certificate is constructed for the domain \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\geq0\text{ on }[0,1]\not\Longrightarrow p\geq0\text{ on }\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Polynomial whose certified and asserted domains are compared.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind is exactly appropriate, and the example correctly distinguishes interval nonnegativity from global nonnegativity. A specific source locator is nevertheless required for the broader claims about Bernstein, Handelman, and positive-orthant certificate domains.

children.title: Floating-Point Certificate Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics separating optimization accuracy, identity accuracy, cone feasibility, and recovery readiness.

children.title: Polynomial-Identity Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Numerical assessment of coefficient and multiplier consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Identity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual test for a floating-point polynomial certificate identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a claimed identity \[f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i,\] expand both sides in one fixed monomial basis through the maximum represented degree. Form the coefficient residual \(r=\operatorname{coeff}(f-\gamma)-\operatorname{coeff}(\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i)\) and the scaled error \[\eta_{\mathrm{id}}=\frac{\lVert r\rVert_\infty}{1+\max\{\lVert\operatorname{coeff}(f-\gamma)\rVert_\infty,\lVert\operatorname{coeff}(\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i)\rVert_\infty\}}.\] Report \(\eta_{\mathrm{id}}\), the largest offending monomial, and all degree or support truncations. Accept numerically only if \(\eta_{\mathrm{id}}\leq\tau_{\mathrm{id}}\); exact certification additionally requires exact zero residual after rational reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand the claimed certificate in one monomial basis, measure its scaled coefficient residual, identify the worst monomial, and require exact zero after rational reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: All polynomial expressions use the same variable ordering and monomial convention.
\(\tau_{\mathrm{id}}>0\) is a declared numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_{\mathrm{id}}\leq\tau_{\mathrm{id}}\) is a numerical consistency test; \(r=0\) exactly is the polynomial-identity certificate.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector of the identity residual.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the diagnostic leaf, but the chosen residual normalization, acceptance protocol, and rational-reconstruction requirement are not supported by a cited numerical-certification source.

children.title: Conic-Feasibility Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Numerical assessment of PSD, SOC, and relative-entropy feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Feasibility Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified residual checks for PSD, second-order, and relative-entropy constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every reported PSD constraint \(Q\succeq0\), compute \(v_{\mathrm{psd}}=(-\lambda_{\min}(Q))_+\). For every second-order constraint \(\lVert u\rVert_2\leq t\), compute \(v_{\mathrm{soc}}=(\lVert u\rVert_2-t)_+\). For every relative-entropy constraint \(D(x,y)=\sum_jx_j\log(x_j/y_j)\leq z\), first verify \(x_j\geq0\) and \(y_j>0\), using the closed perspective convention at \(x_j=0\), and then compute \(v_{\mathrm{re}}=(D(x,y)-z)_+\). Scale each violation by \(1\) plus the corresponding data magnitude, report both componentwise and maximum residuals, and accept only when every scaled residual is below its declared cone-specific tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure negative eigenvalues, SOC excesses, and relative-entropy excesses, including domain violations; scale and compare each residual with a declared cone-specific tolerance.
assumptions_latex: All candidate cone variables are available at sufficient numerical precision.
Each cone family has a declared nonnegative feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{\widehat v_{\mathrm{psd}},\widehat v_{\mathrm{soc}},\widehat v_{\mathrm{re}}\}\leq\tau\) defines numerical conic acceptance, not exact feasibility.

notation.meaning: Positive part, equal to the maximum of a and zero.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the conic-diagnostics leaf. The relative-entropy closure convention needs authoritative specification because requiring y_j>0 does not describe every closed relative-entropy-cone boundary convention, and the phrase corresponding data magnitude does not uniquely define the scaled violations.

children.title: Primal-Dual Bound Consistency Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks linking relaxation values and candidate certificates.

children.title: Primal Feasibility Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Assessment of candidate primal feasibility in sparse relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual test for the primal side of a finite-dimensional conic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic primal problem \[\inf_x\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\},\] evaluate a reported point \(\widehat x\) by the scaled equality residual \[\eta_p^{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\lVert A\widehat x-b\rVert}{1+\lVert A\rVert\lVert\widehat x\rVert+\lVert b\rVert}\] and the scaled cone distance \[\eta_p^K=\frac{\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,K)}{1+\lVert\widehat x\rVert}.\] Report \(c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x\), both residuals, the chosen norms, and the cone projection or violation rule. Declare numerical primal feasibility only if \(\max\{\eta_p^{\mathrm{eq}},\eta_p^K\}\leq\tau_p\). An objective value from a point failing this test is not a certified primal upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check scaled equality and cone-distance residuals for a reported primal point. Its objective is an upper bound only after primal feasibility is established.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The norm, cone-distance rule, and tolerance \(\tau_p\) are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{\eta_p^{\mathrm{eq}},\eta_p^K\}\leq\tau_p\) is numerical primal feasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the primal-feasibility diagnostic leaf. The finite-dimensional residual formulas and tolerance-based acceptance rule are coherent but require a specific numerical conic-optimization source; tolerance acceptance must remain distinguished from exact feasibility.

children.title: Dual Feasibility Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Assessment of candidate dual certificate feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Feasibility Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual test for the dual side of a finite-dimensional conic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the dual problem associated with \(\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), namely \[\sup_{y,s}\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\},\] evaluate \((\widehat y,\widehat s)\) using \[\eta_d^{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\lVert A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+\widehat s-c\rVert}{1+\lVert A\rVert\lVert\widehat y\rVert+\lVert\widehat s\rVert+\lVert c\rVert},\qquad \eta_d^{K^*}=\frac{\operatorname{dist}(\widehat s,K^*)}{1+\lVert\widehat s\rVert}.\] Report \(b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\) and both residuals. Declare numerical dual feasibility only if their maximum is at most \(\tau_d\); otherwise the reported objective is not a certified lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check the dual affine equation and distance of the slack to the dual cone. The dual objective is a lower bound only after feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K^*\) is the dual cone of the closed convex cone \(K\).
The norm, cone-distance rule, and tolerance \(\tau_d\) are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{\eta_d^{\mathrm{eq}},\eta_d^{K^*}\}\leq\tau_d\) is numerical dual feasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the dual-feasibility diagnostic leaf, and the displayed dual convention is consistent with the primal formulation. The residual normalization and numerical acceptance protocol have no supporting source locator.

children.title: Bound Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Consistency assessment across computed bounds and candidate objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering test for independently validated lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Suppose \(L\) is justified by a valid lower-bound certificate and \(U=f(\widehat x)\) is obtained from a feasible point \(\widehat x\in X\). Exact bound consistency is the chain \[L\leq f^*\leq U.\] In floating-point arithmetic define \[v_{\mathrm{ord}}=\frac{(L-U)_+}{1+|L|+|U|}.\] Report \(L\), \(U\), their independent feasibility residuals, and \(v_{\mathrm{ord}}\). The pair is numerically order-consistent when \(v_{\mathrm{ord}}\leq\tau_{\mathrm{ord}}\); a larger reversal indicates an invalid certificate, infeasible incumbent, sign-convention error, or excessive numerical error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower bound cannot exceed a feasible upper bound. Test their scaled reversal only after validating both bounds independently.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) has an independently validated lower-bound certificate.
\(\widehat x\in X\) has independently validated feasibility and \(U=f(\widehat x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\leq U\) exactly, or \(v_{\mathrm{ord}}\leq\tau_{\mathrm{ord}}\) numerically, is required for bound consistency.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound and feasible upper bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind appropriately captures the required ordering relation. The exact chain is standard, but the scaled reversal metric, tolerance rule, and diagnostic interpretation constitute a specific protocol that requires a cited source.

children.title: Duality-Gap Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Assessment of numerical disagreement between primal and dual values.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap and complementarity checks after separate primal and dual feasibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-dual conic pair with feasible candidates \(\widehat x\) and \((\widehat y,\widehat s)\), compute the signed gap \[g=c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x-b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\] and the scaled gap \[\eta_g=\frac{|g|}{1+|c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x|+|b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y|}.\] Under exact primal and dual feasibility, weak duality requires \(g\geq0\), and the affine equations give \(g=\langle\widehat x,\widehat s\rangle\). Report \(g\), \(\eta_g\), the scaled complementarity mismatch, and both feasibility residuals. Treat \(g<0\) beyond tolerance as inconsistency; treat \(\eta_g\leq\tau_g\) as numerical near-optimality only when feasibility has already been accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After validating both sides, compute the signed and scaled primal-dual gap and compare it with complementarity. A significant negative gap signals inconsistency.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual sign conventions are those displayed in the sibling diagnostic records.
Primal and dual feasibility have been assessed independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\geq0\) under exact feasibility, and \(\eta_g\leq\tau_g\) indicates numerical near-optimality only with accepted feasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the duality-gap diagnostic leaf, and the signed-gap identity is consistent with the displayed primal-dual convention. A source is required for the numerical protocol, and the requested scaled complementarity mismatch is not actually defined in the statement.

children.title: Rank-Flatness Extraction Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Assessment of numerical rank stabilization and extraction readiness.

children.title: Numerical Rank Profiles
children.top_down_role: Observed rank patterns across moment or Gram blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Rank Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-indexed singular-value profiles for moment and localizing matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric moment or localizing matrices \(M_k\) for orders \(k=k_0,\ldots,t\), compute singular values \(\sigma_1(M_k)\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_{N_k}(M_k)\geq0\). For a relative threshold \(\tau>0\), define \[r_k(\tau)=\#\{j:\sigma_j(M_k)>\tau\max(1,\sigma_1(M_k))\}.\] Report the full normalized spectra, \(r_k(\tau)\) over a declared grid of thresholds, and adjacent spectral-gap ratios where denominators are nonzero. A rank is numerically stable only when it persists across a meaningful threshold interval. A single threshold-dependent rank value is diagnostic evidence, not an exact rank or a flat-extension certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute normalized spectra and ranks across several tolerances. Stable plateaus support a numerical rank estimate; one threshold alone does not certify exact rank or flatness.
assumptions_latex: Each \(M_k\) is symmetrized before spectral analysis.
The threshold grid and numerical precision are reported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k(\tau)\) is a numerical rank profile; persistence in \(\tau\), not one cutoff, supports rank assessment.

notation.meaning: Moment or localizing matrix at order k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the numerical-rank-profile leaf and correctly avoids treating a single cutoff as an exact flatness certificate. The particular relative threshold, threshold-grid protocol, and stability interpretation require an inspectable source on numerical moment-matrix rank diagnostics.

children.title: Flatness Detection
children.top_down_role: Numerical assessment of flat extension behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2t}\) is a truncated real moment sequence with moment matrices \(M_s(y)\) for \(s\le t\).
A numerical rank uses \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau M:=\#\{i:\sigma_i(M)>\tau\}\) for a fixed \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) is declared numerically flat at order \(t\) and tolerance \(\tau\) precisely when \(r_t(\tau)=r_{t-1}(\tau)\), subject to positive-semidefiniteness and constraint-localizing residual checks. The common value \(r\) is the candidate number of atoms. Exact flatness is the corresponding equality \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-1}(y)=r\); under the standard flat-extension hypotheses it supports extraction of an \(r\)-atomic representing measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-matrix flatness diagnostic using adjacent relaxation orders and a fixed singular-value tolerance.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sigma_1(M)\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_m(M)\ge0\) denote the singular values of a symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix. Define \(r_s(\tau):=\#\{i:\sigma_i(M_s(y))>\tau\}\). Flatness is detected at order \(t\) when \(r_t(\tau)=r_{t-1}(\tau)\), while the negative-eigenvalue and localizing-matrix residuals remain within their prescribed feasibility tolerances. A stable common rank over a nontrivial interval of \(\tau\) is stronger numerical evidence than equality at one tolerance. In exact arithmetic, the diagnostic targets \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-1}(y)\), the rank condition used by flat-extension extraction results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flatness is detected when consecutive moment matrices have the same numerical rank, feasibility residuals are acceptable, and preferably the rank equality persists over a tolerance interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Flatness Detection

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

children.title: Rank-Tolerance Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of rank conclusions on numerical thresholds.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Tolerance Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of adjacent-order numerical flatness to singular-value threshold selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s\in\{t-1,t\}\), the function \(r_s(\tau)=\#\{i:\sigma_i(M_s)>\tau\}\) is nonincreasing and changes when \(\tau\) reaches a singular value. Thus a flatness declaration at rank \(r\) is stable on \(I=[\tau_-,\tau_+]\) if and only if \(r_t(\tau)=r_{t-1}(\tau)=r\) for every \(\tau\in I\). Equivalently, both ranks equal \(r\) at \(\tau_-\), and neither matrix has a singular value in \((\tau_-,\tau_+]\). Equality confined to a narrow tolerance region indicates numerical fragility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flatness decision is stable on a closed tolerance interval exactly when both adjacent numerical ranks are equal and constant throughout that interval; under a strict singular-value cutoff, transitions occur at singular values above the lower endpoint and through the upper endpoint.
assumptions_latex: \(M_t\) and \(M_{t-1}\) are symmetric numerical moment matrices.
The tested tolerance interval is \(I=[\tau_-,\tau_+]\subset(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The flatness decision is tolerance-stable on \(I\) exactly when \(r_t(\tau)=r_{t-1}(\tau)=r\) for every \(\tau\in I\). Under the convention \(r_s(\tau)=\#\{i:\sigma_i(M_s)>\tau\}\), this is equivalent to equality at \(\tau_-\) and absence of singular values of either matrix in \((\tau_-,\tau_+]\).

children.title: Extraction Readiness
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic evidence supporting attempted minimizer extraction.

assumptions_latex: A candidate truncated moment sequence and its moment and localizing matrices have been computed.
A rank \(r\), tolerance interval \(I\), and residual bounds are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Extraction is declared ready only if the rank-flatness equality is stable on \(I\), all required semidefinite and localizing residuals satisfy their bounds, and the multiplication operators constructed on the rank-\(r\) quotient basis have acceptable commutator and relation residuals. The diagnostic certifies readiness to attempt extraction, not the correctness of the resulting atoms; extracted atoms and weights must subsequently be validated against the moments and constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational precondition for attempting finite-atomic extraction from numerical moment data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numerical moment solution is extraction-ready at rank \(r\) when: \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau M_t=\operatorname{rank}_\tau M_{t-1}=r\) throughout the declared interval \(I\); moment and required localizing matrices satisfy their semidefinite residual bounds; a rank-revealing quotient basis is well conditioned; and its compressed multiplication matrices \(X_i\) satisfy the prescribed relation and commutator bounds, including \(\|X_iX_j-X_jX_i\|\). These tests authorize an extraction attempt. They do not replace posterior verification that recovered atoms satisfy the constraints and reproduce the supplied moments within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extraction is ready when flatness is tolerance-stable, feasibility residuals are small, and the compressed multiplication operators are sufficiently consistent and commuting.
knowledge_statements.title: Extraction Readiness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operational condition fits Extraction Readiness and appropriately distinguishes readiness from posterior validation, but the combined rank, conditioning, commutator, relation, and residual criteria have no inspectable source.

children.title: Rational SOS Certificate Recovery
children.top_down_role: Numerical-symbolic families converting approximate SOS data into exact rational certificates.

children.title: Rounding-Projection Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery families combining rational approximation with projection onto polynomial identities.

children.title: Rational Gram Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Rational reconstruction of approximate Gram data.

assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb Q[x]\), \(z(x)\) is a fixed monomial vector, and \(\widehat Q\in\mathbb S^m\) is an approximate Gram matrix.
The coefficient map \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^m\to\mathbb R^N\) satisfies \(z(x)^\top Qz(x)=p(x)\iff\mathcal A(Q)=b\), with \(b\in\mathbb Q^N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is accepted as a rational Gram certificate only when \(Q\in\mathbb S^m(\mathbb Q)\), \(\mathcal A(Q)=b\) holds exactly, and \(Q\succeq0\) is established exactly, for example by a rational \(LDL^\top\) decomposition with nonnegative diagonal pivots. These checks imply the exact identity \(p(x)=z(x)^\top Qz(x)\) and hence an exact rational SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational recovery of a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix from floating-point data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((p,z,\widehat Q)\), choose denominator bounds and reconstruct each independent entry of \(\widehat Q\) as a rational number, producing \(Q_0\in\mathbb S^m(\mathbb Q)\). Correct \(Q_0\) within the rational affine space \(\{Q:\mathcal A(Q)=b\}\), or reject it if no admissible correction is found. Then verify exactly that \(\mathcal A(Q)=b\) and \(Q\succeq0\). A valid output \(Q\) yields \(p(x)=z(x)^\top Qz(x)\). Failure of exact identity matching or exact positive-semidefiniteness returns no certificate, regardless of the floating-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruct rational Gram entries, enforce coefficient identities exactly, and accept only after exact positive-semidefiniteness verification.
knowledge_statements.title: Rational Gram Reconstruction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Rational Gram Reconstruction and correctly requires exact identity and positive-semidefiniteness checks, but no source or locator supports the reconstruction-and-correction procedure.

children.title: Identity-Space Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection onto the affine space of polynomial identities.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^m\to\mathbb R^N\) is linear, \(b\in\operatorname{range}\mathcal A\), and \(Q_0\in\mathbb S^m\).
The matrix space carries the Frobenius inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Frobenius-nearest matrix satisfying the polynomial identity is \(Q_{\mathrm{aff}}=Q_0-\mathcal A^*(\mathcal A\mathcal A^*)^\dagger(\mathcal A(Q_0)-b)\). It obeys \(\mathcal A(Q_{\mathrm{aff}})=b\). This projection enforces coefficient matching but does not generally preserve \(Q_{\mathrm{aff}}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Affine projection of the Gram matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal projection of Gram data onto exact coefficient-matching equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the affine identity space \(\mathcal F:=\{Q\in\mathbb S^m:\mathcal A(Q)=b\}\). Its Frobenius projection is 
\[Q_{\mathrm{aff}}=Q_0-\mathcal A^*(\mathcal A\mathcal A^*)^\dagger\bigl(\mathcal A(Q_0)-b\bigr).
\]
Because \(b\in\operatorname{range}\mathcal A\), this matrix lies in \(\mathcal F\) and minimizes \(\|Q-Q_0\|_F\) over \(Q\in\mathcal F\). If the data and a compatible linear-system solution are rational, the correction can instead be computed by exact rational elimination. Projection onto \(\mathcal F\) alone gives no positive-semidefiniteness guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the approximate Gram matrix orthogonally onto the affine coefficient-identity space; this restores the identity but may destroy positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.title: Identity-Space Projection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine projection formula is mathematically standard and fits Identity-Space Projection, including the warning that projection need not preserve positive semidefiniteness. An inspectable linear-algebra source locator is nevertheless required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rational positive-semidefinite guarantee for identity-space projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The parameters epsilon, delta, and tau, the rounded matrix, and the affine identity space retain their definitions from the rounding-projection construction preceding the extracted theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume $\delta<\epsilon$ and choose $\tau\le\sqrt{\epsilon^2-\delta^2}$. Then the orthogonal projection $\Pi_{\mathcal L}(\widetilde Q)$ is rational and positive semidefinite and therefore is a valid rational SOS Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated rounding and projection error bound, projecting the rounded matrix onto the affine polynomial-identity space produces a rational positive-semidefinite Gram matrix and hence a valid rational SOS decomposition.
assumptions_latex: \epsilon,\delta,\tau,\widetilde Q,\mathcal L\ \text{are as defined in the rounding-projection construction}
\delta<\epsilon
\tau\le\sqrt{\epsilon^2-\delta^2}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi_{\mathcal L}(\widetilde Q)\in\mathbb{Q}^{N\times N}\cap\mathbb{S}_+^N\quad\text{and is a valid rational SOS Gram matrix}

children.title: Simultaneous Identity-Cone Repair
children.top_down_role: Recovery balancing exact identities with conic feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A(Q)=b\) encodes the required polynomial identity and \(Q_0\in\mathbb S^m\) is approximate.
The intersection \(\{Q:\mathcal A(Q)=b,\ Q\succeq0\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A simultaneous repair is any computed minimizer \(Q_*\) of \(\min\{\|Q-Q_0\|_F:\mathcal A(Q)=b,\ Q\succeq0\}\). It satisfies identity and cone feasibility together. For an exact rational certificate, a rational feasible \(Q\) must subsequently be recovered and both conditions verified in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint restoration of coefficient identities and positive-semidefinite Gram feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Q_0\), solve the convex repair problem
\[Q_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Q\in\mathbb S^m}\ \|Q-Q_0\|_F\quad\text{subject to}\quad \mathcal A(Q)=b,\quad Q\succeq0.
\]
Stop when primal identity and cone residuals meet the chosen numerical tolerances, then attempt rational reconstruction inside the same affine-conic intersection. Accept only a rational matrix whose identity and positive-semidefiniteness are verified exactly. Alternating affine and cone projections may supply an initializer, but finite termination or exact rational feasibility does not follow merely from small alternating-projection residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair the Gram matrix by minimizing its change subject to coefficient identities and positive semidefiniteness simultaneously, then verify any rational recovery exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Identity-Cone Repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex repair formulation matches the terminal container and correctly separates numerical repair from exact rational certification, but neither the joint-repair method nor its stated workflow has cited support.

children.title: Precision-Perturbation Recovery Pipeline
children.top_down_role: Precision escalation and interior perturbation preceding exact conversion.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: On Exact Polya and Putinar's Representations

children.title: Arbitrary-Precision Conic Solves
children.top_down_role: High-precision numerical solves used to improve recovery margins.

assumptions_latex: The conic relaxation has rational input data and admits a numerically accessible solution.
A sequence of working precisions \(p_1<p_2<\cdots\) and residual targets is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns the first high-precision solution whose primal, dual, and cone residuals and eigenvalue margin meet the reconstruction thresholds, together with its precision and diagnostics; otherwise it reports failure at the precision limit. Increased precision improves numerical resolution but alone does not certify exact feasibility or rational reconstructibility.

notation.meaning: Working binary or decimal precision at stage k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precision-escalation procedure for producing conic data with recoverable residuals and spectral margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k=1,2,\ldots\), solve the conic relaxation at working precision \(p_k\), warm-starting from the preceding iterate when available. Compute independently the primal identity residual, dual residual, duality gap, cone violation, and relevant smallest positive eigenvalue, and collect them in \(\rho_k\). Stop when \(\rho_k\) is below the reconstruction target and the spectral margin exceeds the projected rounding-error bound; output \((X_k,p_k,\rho_k)\). If the maximum precision is reached first, return failure. Every accepted exact certificate must still undergo rational reconstruction and exact identity and cone checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve at higher precision until residuals and spectral margins support reconstruction; high precision remains numerical evidence, not an exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary-Precision Conic Solves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The precision-escalation algorithm is plausible, but the underlying conic model and solver are unspecified, while eigenvalue margins apply specifically to semidefinite blocks rather than arbitrary cones. A source is needed to determine the valid residual and stopping criteria.

children.title: Interior-Perturbation Certification
children.top_down_role: Exactification families using controlled interior perturbations.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^m(\mathbb Q)\to\mathbb Q^N\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^N\), and \(Q_0\in\mathbb S^m(\mathbb Q)\) satisfy \(Q_0\succ0\).
The exact affine correction is \(\Delta=-\mathcal A^*(\mathcal A\mathcal A^*)^\dagger(\mathcal A(Q_0)-b)\) and is rational.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\|\Delta\|_2<\lambda_{\min}(Q_0)\), then \(Q=Q_0+\Delta\) satisfies \(\mathcal A(Q)=b\) and \(Q\succ0\). Thus the exact rational identity together with the strict spectral-margin inequality certifies conic feasibility after projection.

notation.meaning: Interior rational Gram matrix before correction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-margin certificate ensuring that exact affine correction remains inside the positive-definite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Start from a rational interior matrix \(Q_0\succ0\), possibly obtained by adding a controlled rational perturbation to the target certificate family. Compute an exact rational correction \(\Delta\) satisfying \(\mathcal A(\Delta)=b-\mathcal A(Q_0)\). If
\[\|\Delta\|_2<\lambda_{\min}(Q_0),
\]
then Weyl's eigenvalue bound gives \(\lambda_{\min}(Q_0+\Delta)>0\). Consequently \(Q=Q_0+\Delta\) is an exact rational solution of \(\mathcal A(Q)=b\) lying in the cone interior. The perturbation parameter must also be tracked algebraically so that the certified identity corresponds to the intended polynomial statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact affine correction preserves positive definiteness when its spectral norm is smaller than the starting matrix's exact interior eigenvalue margin.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Perturbation Certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral-margin certificate is mathematically coherent and fits Interior-Perturbation Certification, but the exactification construction and its relationship to the perturbed polynomial family lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Rank-Basis Compression Calculus
children.top_down_role: Compression of Gram data before exact reconstruction.

children.title: Numerical Rank Compression
children.top_down_role: Compression of Gram data using numerical rank information.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^m\) has eigendecomposition \(Q=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)U^\top\) with \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_m\ge0\).
A threshold \(\tau>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compressed approximation is \(Q_\tau=U_r\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)U_r^\top\), where \(r=\#\{i:\lambda_i>\tau\}\). It is positive semidefinite, has rank \(r\), and satisfies \(\|Q-Q_\tau\|_2=\lambda_{r+1}\) and \(\|Q-Q_\tau\|_F^2=\sum_{i>r}\lambda_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral truncation of a numerical positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Compute the symmetric eigendecomposition of \(Q\), select \(r=\#\{i:\lambda_i>\tau\}\), and form
\[Q_\tau=U_r\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)U_r^\top.
\]
Return \((Q_\tau,U_r,r)\) together with the discarded spectral tail. The output is positive semidefinite and has rank \(r\). Moreover, \(\|Q-Q_\tau\|_2=\lambda_{r+1}\) and \(\|Q-Q_\tau\|_F^2=\sum_{i>r}\lambda_i^2\), with \(\lambda_{m+1}:=0\). This is a numerical compression; exact polynomial identities must be rechecked after truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard eigenmodes below a threshold, report the retained rank and spectral tail, and recheck polynomial identities because truncation changes the Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Rank Compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral truncation algorithm and error identities are correctly stated and fit Numerical Rank Compression, but no matrix-approximation source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Basis Compression
children.top_down_role: Reduction of polynomial coordinates before exact reconstruction.

assumptions_latex: \(z(x)\in\mathbb R[x]^m\), \(w(x)\in\mathbb R[x]^r\), and \(z(x)=Bw(x)\) for a full-column-rank matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\).
\(Q\in\mathbb S^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With \(R=B^\top QB\), the Gram representation compresses exactly as \(z(x)^\top Qz(x)=w(x)^\top Rw(x)\). If \(Q\succeq0\), then \(R\succeq0\). Conversely, any \(R\succeq0\) supplies a positive-semidefinite Gram representation in the reduced polynomial basis \(w\).

notation.meaning: Original and reduced polynomial basis vectors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact congruence representation after replacing a redundant polynomial basis by a smaller spanning basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the original polynomial vector factors as \(z(x)=Bw(x)\), where the columns of \(B\) embed the reduced basis into the original one. Then
\[z(x)^\top Qz(x)=w(x)^\top\bigl(B^\top QB\bigr)w(x).
\]
Thus \(R=B^\top QB\) is the compressed Gram matrix. Congruence preserves positive semidefiniteness from \(Q\) to \(R\). For exact recovery, \(B\) and \(w\) should be represented over the intended exact coefficient field, and coefficient matching must be verified after compression; a merely numerical basis relation does not establish an exact polynomial identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the original polynomial vector is an exact linear image of a smaller basis, congruence gives a smaller Gram matrix representing the same polynomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The congruence identity and positive-semidefiniteness implication are correct and fit Basis Compression. A source locator is required for this nontrivial Gram-basis representation claim.

children.title: Kernel-Aware Compression
children.top_down_role: Compression guided by detected Gram or moment kernels.

assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\) has full column rank and represents an identified Gram-kernel subspace.
\(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) has orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker(K^\top)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(Q\succeq0\), the kernel constraint \(QK=0\) holds if and only if there exists \(R\succeq0\) such that \(Q=URU^\top\). Hence optimization and recovery may be restricted to the smaller cone \(\mathbb S_+^r\), provided the kernel is exact or is subsequently certified exactly.

notation.meaning: Basis for the orthogonal complement of that kernel

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite compression onto the orthogonal complement of a known Gram kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal K=\operatorname{range}K\) and \(\operatorname{range}U=\mathcal K^\perp\). If \(Q\succeq0\) and \(QK=0\), then \(\operatorname{range}Q\subseteq\mathcal K^\perp\), so
\[Q=URU^\top,\qquad R=U^\top QU\succeq0.
\]
Conversely, every \(R\succeq0\) defines \(Q=URU^\top\succeq0\) with \(QK=0\). Therefore the Gram variable can be compressed to \(R\). A numerically inferred kernel must be treated as provisional: imposing an incorrect kernel can remove every exact certificate from the reduced affine space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A known Gram kernel permits exact restriction to its orthogonal complement, but an incorrectly inferred numerical kernel can eliminate all valid certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Aware Compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The kernel-based positive-semidefinite representation is coherent and fits Kernel-Aware Compression, including the warning about numerically inferred kernels, but it has no supporting citation.

children.title: Exact-Recovery Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of compressed representations with exact certificate reconstruction.

assumptions_latex: The coefficient map \(\mathcal A\), target \(b\), and compression matrix \(U\) are defined over \(\mathbb Q\).
The compressed variable is \(R\in\mathbb S^r\) and its lifted Gram matrix is \(Q=URU^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compression is compatible with exact rational recovery precisely when the reduced feasible set \(\{R\in\mathbb S_+^r(\mathbb Q):\mathcal A(URU^\top)=b\}\) is nonempty. Any member lifts to an exact rational positive-semidefinite Gram certificate. Numerical feasibility alone, or an irrational compression basis, does not establish this compatibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion ensuring that reduced Gram coordinates retain an exact rational certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given rational \(\mathcal A\), \(b\), and \(U\), define the reduced affine-conic set
\[\mathcal F_U(\mathbb Q):=\{R\in\mathbb S^r(\mathbb Q):R\succeq0,\ \mathcal A(URU^\top)=b\}.
\]
The compression is exact-recovery compatible if and only if \(\mathcal F_U(\mathbb Q)\neq\varnothing\). For every \(R\in\mathcal F_U(\mathbb Q)\), the lift \(Q=URU^\top\) is rational, positive semidefinite, and satisfies the original coefficient identity exactly. Compatibility can fail when a numerical rank or kernel truncation excludes the range of every exact feasible Gram matrix, even though the discarded modes appear small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational compression supports exact recovery exactly when its reduced affine cone contains a rational positive-semidefinite point whose lift satisfies all coefficient identities.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Vector Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise bounded-denominator reconstruction followed by exact certificate validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\widetilde q\in\mathbb R^m\), a denominator bound \(B\in\mathbb N\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), find for each coordinate the unique fraction \(q_i=a_i/b_i\) satisfying \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\), \(1\le b_i\le B\), \(\gcd(a_i,b_i)=1\), and \(|q_i-\widetilde q_i|<\varepsilon\). If any coordinate lacks a unique fraction, return failure. Otherwise form \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_m)\in\mathbb Q^m\), substitute it into the defining polynomial and conic constraints of the certificate, and output \(q\) only when every equality holds exactly and every cone constraint is certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover each coordinate as a unique nearby bounded-denominator fraction, then accept the rational vector only after exact identity and conic-feasibility checks.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde q\in\mathbb R^m\) approximates an exact rational certificate vector.
\(B\in\mathbb N\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) are prescribed.

knowledge_statements.title: Lattice-Assisted Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous rational recovery through a short integer relation and exact validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\widetilde q\in\mathbb R^m\), scaling parameter \(M\in\mathbb N\), and height bound \(H\), construct an integer-relation lattice encoding vectors \((a_1,\ldots,a_m,b)\in\mathbb Z^{m+1}\) for which \(a_i-b\widetilde q_i\) is small. Apply a lattice-basis reduction method and inspect reduced short vectors with \(0<|b|\le H\). For each candidate set \(q_i=a_i/b\), reduce the fractions, and test all certificate equalities and cone constraints exactly. Output the first exactly feasible \(q\in\mathbb Q^m\); return failure if no inspected vector passes.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-SOS Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational Gram recovery for a multiplier-weighted SOS identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\), set \(g_0=1\), and let \(f,g_j\in\mathbb Q[x]\). An exact weighted-SOS certificate for \(f-\gamma\) consists of \(\gamma\in\mathbb Q\), monomial vectors \(v_j\), and matrices \(Q_j\in\mathbb S_+^{r_j}\cap\mathbb Q^{r_j\times r_j}\) such that \[f-\gamma=\sum_{j=0}^{s}g_jv_j^{\mathsf T}Q_jv_j.\] Recovery is successful only if coefficient comparison verifies this identity over \(\mathbb Q[x]\) and every \(Q_j\) is exactly positive semidefinite. Then \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover rational positive-semidefinite Gram matrices whose weighted polynomial identity holds coefficientwise; the identity certifies the recovered lower bound on the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_s\in\mathbb Q[x]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-\gamma=\sum_{j=0}^{s}g_jv_j^{\mathsf T}Q_jv_j\) implies \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) on \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Circuit-Decomposition Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SONC recovery using rational circuit supports and coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reconstruct \(p\in\mathbb Q[x]\) as \(p=\sum_{k=1}^{N}p_k\), where each \[p_k(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{r_k}c_{ki}x^{\alpha_{ki}}+d_kx^{\beta_k}\] has affinely independent even outer exponents \(\alpha_{ki}\in(2\mathbb N)^n\), positive \(c_{ki}\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\beta_k=\sum_i\lambda_{ki}\alpha_{ki}\) with exact \(\lambda_{ki}>0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_{ki}=1\). Define \(\Theta_k=\prod_i(c_{ki}/\lambda_{ki})^{\lambda_{ki}}\). Validate coefficient equality and either \(|d_k|\le\Theta_k\) when \(\beta_k\notin(2\mathbb N)^n\), or \(d_k\ge-\Theta_k\) when \(\beta_k\in(2\mathbb N)^n\). The validated decomposition certifies \(p(x)\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover an exact sum of nonnegative circuit polynomials and verify support geometry, barycentric weights, circuit-number inequalities, and coefficient equality.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb Q[x]\).
Every reconstructed circuit has even outer exponents and an inner exponent in their relative interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact circuit conditions and identity imply \(p(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Residual Verification

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p,q_1,\ldots,q_s\in\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) and let \(a_1,\ldots,a_s\in\mathbb Q\). The proposed identity \(p=\sum_j a_jq_j\) is certified exactly if and only if \(r_\alpha=0\) in \(\mathbb Q\) for every \(\alpha\in F\). A nonzero coefficient supplies a directly checkable rejection witness.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Identity Verification

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\), with \(g_0=1\). knowledge_statements.title: Exact PSD Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational-arithmetic criterion for positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^m\cap\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\). For every index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), compute the principal minor \(\det Q[I,I]\) exactly in \(\mathbb Q\), taking the empty minor as one. Then \[Q\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \det Q[I,I]\ge0\ \text{ for every }I.\] Thus the complete list of exact nonnegative principal minors is a finite PSD certificate. Any negative principal minor is an exact rejection witness. Symmetry must be checked before applying the criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational symmetric matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when all its principal minors, computed in exact arithmetic, are nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\) is exactly symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if all principal minors of \(Q\) are nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact SOC Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational test for membership in a Lorentz cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \((t,u)\in\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q^m\), membership in the Lorentz cone \(\mathcal L_{m+1}=\{(s,v)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m:s\ge\|v\|_2\}\) is equivalent to the two rational inequalities \[t\ge0,\qquad t^2-u^{\mathsf T}u\ge0.\] Both quantities can be evaluated and compared with zero exactly. Their nonnegativity is therefore a finite exact certificate of SOC feasibility, while failure of either inequality is an exact rejection witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational Lorentz-cone block is feasible exactly when its scalar coordinate and squared cone slack are both nonnegative.

A validated membership certificate for \((x,y,z)\) consists of outward-rounded intervals \(X,Y,Z\) containing the submitted data and either: (i) \(\inf X>0\), \(\inf Y>0\), and an interval evaluation \(R\supseteq X\log(X/Y)\) satisfying \(\sup R\le\inf Z\); or (ii) exact verification of a boundary case in the closure. Membership in the exponential cone follows through the fixed representation \((u,v,w)\in K_{\exp}\iff (v,w,-u)\in K_{\mathrm{re}}\). Rejection occurs whenever the validated enclosure proves the defining inequality false.

The logarithm implementation returns a rigorous interval enclosure.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified-Bound Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact consistency test for a polynomial lower-bound certificate on a basic closed semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), a claimed lower bound \(\gamma\) is consistent with certificate data \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\) when every \(\sigma_j\) is verified sum-of-squares and the coefficient identity \[f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j g_j\] holds exactly. These checks imply \(f(x)-\gamma\ge0\) for every \(x\in K\), so \(\gamma\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\). The bound stored in the certificate must equal the scalar appearing in the exact identity; a rounded or differently normalized value is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The claimed lower bound must appear in an exact SOS identity whose multipliers are independently verified, thereby proving the bound over the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Solution Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-candidate consistency with a certified lower bound for polynomial minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\), let \(\gamma\le f^*\) be an independently certified lower bound, and let \(\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n\) be a recovered candidate. A consistency certificate verifies \(g_j(\widehat x)\ge0\) for every \(j\) using exact arithmetic or rigorous lower enclosures and computes a certified scalar upper bound \(u\ge f(\widehat x)\). It then verifies \(\gamma\le u\), giving \[\gamma\le f^*\le f(\widehat x)\le u.\] For any declared \(\varepsilon\ge0\), if \(u-\gamma\le\varepsilon\), then \(f(\widehat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\), so \(\widehat x\) is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal. If a rigorously certified upper bound satisfies \(u<\gamma\), at least one feasibility, evaluation, or lower-bound certificate is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorously feasible candidate supplies an objective upper bound that cannot undercut the certified lower bound; the difference between these bounds certifies a global optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma\le f^*\) has been independently certified.
Candidate feasibility is checked exactly or by rigorous lower enclosures.
\(u\ge f(\widehat x)\) is obtained exactly or as the upper endpoint of a rigorous objective enclosure.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma\le f^*\le f(\widehat x)\le u\), and \(u-\gamma\le\varepsilon\) implies \(f(\widehat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified upper bound on the candidate objective value
