children.title: Computer-Algebra Checkers
children.top_down_role: Symbolic checking interfaces for identities and exact matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Computer-Algebra Checkers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact symbolic checker for polynomial identities and rational Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input rational polynomials, claimed identities, and symmetric rational matrices. Canonicalize each polynomial in a fixed monomial order, expand both sides, and reject unless all coefficient differences are zero. For each claimed SOS relation \(p=v^{\mathsf T}Qv\), verify symmetry of \(Q\), expand the quadratic form, and compare coefficients exactly. Verify \(Q\succeq0\) using an exact rational certificate, such as a fraction-free congruence decomposition with nonnegative pivots and explicit handling of zero pivots. Accept only if every identity and matrix condition succeeds; output the normalized data and a deterministic verification transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computer-algebra checker expands rational identities, compares every coefficient, and validates rational positive-semidefinite matrices without floating-point tolerances.
assumptions_latex: All inputs lie in \(\mathbb Q\) and use a declared monomial ordering.
The exact PSD routine correctly handles singular matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies every submitted polynomial identity and rational PSD condition exactly.

notation.meaning: polynomial represented by the Gram matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate content kind and the coefficient checks are coherent, but the asserted fraction-free PSD procedure—especially its treatment of zero pivots—requires a specific exact-linear-algebra source.

children.title: Formal Certificate Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Machine-checkable representations for independently verified certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Formal Certificate Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed, machine-checkable representation separating certificate data from a small trusted verifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A formal certificate interface represents an optimization certificate as finite typed data \(C=(M,P,Q,B)\): monomial-index maps \(M\), exact polynomial coefficient arrays \(P\), cone witnesses \(Q\), and claimed bounds \(B\). Its semantics is a predicate \(\operatorname{Valid}(I,C)\) over problem instance \(I\), requiring dimension agreement, exact coefficient identities, cone membership, and objective-bound consistency. A deterministic verifier \(V\) must satisfy the soundness contract \[V(I,C)=\mathtt{accept}\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Valid}(I,C).\] Serialization must specify coefficient domains, index bases, matrix symmetry conventions, and normalization so that independent implementations parse the same mathematical object.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formal interface gives certificates an exact typed syntax, explicit semantics, and a sound acceptance contract for a small independent verifier.
assumptions_latex: The parser enforces the declared schema and rejects malformed or ambiguous data.
Arithmetic semantics for every serialized coefficient type are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent implementations can check the same predicate \(\operatorname{Valid}(I,C)\) from the serialized certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the formal-interface leaf, but no source supports the proposed certificate fields, soundness contract, or claim that the serialization conventions suffice for independent implementations.

children.title: Certificate-Recovery Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical and geometric circumstances obstructing exact or validated recovery.

children.title: Boundary-of-Cone Certificates
children.top_down_role: Recovery difficulties caused by absent interior feasibility margins.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-of-Cone Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of rounding robustness when a conic certificate has no ambient interior margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone and let a feasible certificate component \(z\in\partial K\). No positive ambient radius is feasibility-preserving: for every \(\delta>0\), there exists \(e\in E\) with \(\lVert e\rVert<\delta\) and \(z+e\notin K\). For the PSD cone, \(Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\succeq0\), but \(Z_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,-\varepsilon)\not\succeq0\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). Thus norm-small rational rounding alone cannot validate a boundary certificate; recovery must preserve its face or reverify cone membership exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary certificate has no ambient feasibility buffer: arbitrarily small perturbations can leave the cone, as a singular PSD example shows.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional normed space.
Boundary is taken relative to the ambient space \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No error tolerance based only on \(\lVert e\rVert\) guarantees that \(z+e\in K\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional ambient-boundary statement and PSD example are mathematically consistent, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. A convex-analysis locator is still required for this nontrivial boundary characterization.

children.title: Facial-Degeneracy Feasibility Boundary
children.top_down_role: Certification difficulties associated with facial degeneracy.

children.title: Weakly Feasible Faces
children.top_down_role: Facial configurations associated with weak conic feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Feasible Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face-restricted conic feasibility without strict feasibility in the ambient cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic system \(L\cap K\ne\varnothing\), where \(L\) is an affine subspace and \(K\) a closed convex cone, let \(F\) be the minimal face of \(K\) containing \(L\cap K\). The system lies on a weakly feasible face when \(F\subsetneq K\), \(L\cap\operatorname{ri}(F)\ne\varnothing\), and \(L\cap\operatorname{ri}(K)=\varnothing\). Feasibility is then strict relative to \(F\) but not relative to \(K\). A recovery method operating in the ambient cone must identify or preserve \(F\); otherwise arbitrarily small transverse perturbations may destroy feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The system is feasible only on a proper cone face: it has relative interior points in that face but no strictly feasible ambient point.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
\(L\) is an affine subspace and \(L\cap K\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set has strict feasibility in \(F\) but fails Slater feasibility in \(K\).

notation.meaning: minimal face containing the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-face versus ambient-Slater distinction is plausible, but “weakly feasible face” is not established as standard terminology and the requirement that recovery identify or preserve the minimal face needs authoritative facial-reduction support.

children.title: Facial Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degenerate face structure affecting certificate recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic facial degeneracy expressed through the minimal face of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an affine conic feasibility system \(L\cap K\ne\varnothing\), its minimal feasible face is \[F_{\min}=\bigcap\{F:F\text{ is a face of }K,\ L\cap K\subseteq F\}.\] The system is facially degenerate when \(F_{\min}\subsetneq K\), equivalently when every feasible point lies in a proper face and no point belongs to \(\operatorname{ri}(K)\). In semidefinite form, a common manifestation is a shared nonzero null direction \(v\) satisfying \(Xv=0\) for every feasible matrix \(X\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial degeneracy means all conic feasible points lie in one proper minimal face, so ambient strict feasibility is impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
\(L\cap K\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Facial degeneracy holds exactly when \(F_{\min}\subsetneq K\).

notation.meaning: minimal face containing the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimal-face formula and equivalence with failure of ambient strict feasibility are coherent for a nonempty finite-dimensional system. A facial-reduction source is needed to confirm that this property is correctly named “facial degeneracy” in this context.

children.title: Near-Infeasible Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerically ambiguous regimes close to conic infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Infeasible Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic instances whose data lie close to the boundary between feasibility and infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) encode the affine data of a conic feasibility problem and let \(\Sigma\) denote the set of ill-posed data at the boundary between feasible and infeasible instances. For a fixed norm and scale convention, the instance is \(\varepsilon\)-near-infeasible when it is feasible and \[0<\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)\le\varepsilon\lVert d\rVert.\] Equivalently, a relative perturbation of size at most \(\varepsilon\) can reach an ill-posed instance, after which arbitrarily small further perturbations may produce infeasibility. Numerical residuals larger than this distance cannot reliably distinguish feasibility from infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible conic instance is near-infeasible when a small relative perturbation reaches the feasibility boundary, making residual-based classification unreliable.
assumptions_latex: A norm and homogeneous scaling convention for problem data are fixed.
\(d\ne0\) encodes a feasible conic instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Perturbations on the scale \(\varepsilon\lVert d\rVert\) can destroy reliable feasibility classification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition depends materially on the chosen data embedding, norm, homogenization, and precise ill-posed set. A condition-number framework must be cited before the distance formula and perturbation interpretation can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Degeneracy Certification Failures
children.top_down_role: Recovery failures caused by weak feasibility or facial degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Certification Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A singular PSD family showing simultaneous feasibility and rank-certification instability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(X(t)=\operatorname{diag}(1,t)\). At \(t=0\), the exact certificate \(X(0)\succeq0\) is feasible, singular, and confined to a proper face of the PSD cone. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the perturbation \(X(-\varepsilon)\) is infeasible, whereas \(X(\varepsilon)\) is positive definite and has larger rank. Hence no nonzero tolerance based only on entrywise or spectral proximity to \(X(0)\) can simultaneously certify cone membership, rank, and the correct minimal face. Exact nullspace or facial information is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a singular PSD certificate, equally small perturbations can produce infeasibility or full rank, so tolerance-only certification cannot recover the correct face.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
Cone membership is positive semidefiniteness in \(\mathbb S^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Norm proximity to \(X(0)\) alone cannot certify feasibility, rank, or minimal-face membership.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal family is a valid self-contained illustration and counterexample is the correct content kind, but the broader certification-failure conclusion lacks the required facial-reduction or perturbation reference.

children.title: Irrational-Certificate Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Regimes where rational recovery is structurally unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Irrational-Certificate Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural impossibility of exact rational recovery when the certificate set contains no rational point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact certificate equations and cone constraints define a feasible set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^N\). Rational exactification is possible only if \(C\cap\mathbb Q^N\ne\varnothing\). For example, \[C=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ge0,\ x^2=2\}=\{\sqrt2\}\] is nonempty but has no rational point. Any rational rounding \(r\in\mathbb Q\) violates the exact identity \(r^2=2\), regardless of its numerical accuracy. Thus an exact checker restricted to rational certificate fields cannot accept a certificate in this regime; the representation must admit algebraic numbers, interval-algebraic witnesses, or a different certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the exact feasible certificate set has only irrational points, no rational rounding can satisfy its identities, however accurate the approximation.
assumptions_latex: The checker requires every certificate coordinate to lie in \(\mathbb Q\).
Certificate equalities are enforced exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(C\cap\mathbb Q^N=\varnothing\), rational certificate recovery is impossible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rational-point obstruction and square-root example are correct, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. A source is required for its application to exact polynomial-optimization certificates and for the proposed alternative witness representations.

children.title: Rank-Tolerance Instability
children.top_down_role: Instability in numerical rank, flatness, and compression decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Tolerance Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-gap boundary for stable numerical rank, flatness, and moment-matrix compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real symmetric matrix \(M\) and threshold \(\tau\), define \(r_\tau(M)=\#\{i:\lambda_i(M)>\tau\}\). If a perturbation bound \(\lVert E\rVert_2\le\eta\) is known and every eigenvalue of \(M\) has distance greater than \(\eta\) from \(\tau\), then \(r_\tau(M+E)=r_\tau(M)\) for every such symmetric perturbation \(E\). Without a validated separation between the spectrum and \(\tau\), the norm bound alone does not give this uniform rank guarantee. For \(M_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\) with \(0<\varepsilon<1\), thresholds below \(\varepsilon\) retain two eigenvalues while thresholds at or above \(\varepsilon\) but below \(1\) retain one, and symmetric perturbations of order \(\varepsilon\) can change positive-semidefinite status. Consequently, tolerance-based flat-extension tests and rank-based compression lack a robust certificate unless an adequate spectral gap or an independent exact rank certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified spectral gap gives uniform stability of threshold rank under bounded perturbations; without such a gap or an exact rank certificate, numerical rank, flatness, and compression decisions can be unstable.
assumptions_latex: \(M,E\in\mathbb S^n\).
Eigenvalues are ordered consistently and perturbations are measured in the spectral norm.
\(\tau\in\mathbb R\) is the declared numerical-rank threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A perturbation bound alone certifies \(r_\tau(M+E)=r_\tau(M)\) uniformly when the spectrum of \(M\) is separated from \(\tau\) by more than that bound; absent such separation, tolerance-based rank conclusions require additional certification.

notation.meaning: rank determined by the declared threshold tau

children.title: Rounding Outside Certificate Cones
children.top_down_role: Loss of conic feasibility during exact approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Outside Certificate Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete loss of positive-semidefinite certificate feasibility under entrywise approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb S_+^2\) and \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\in K\). For every tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the rational matrix \(\widehat Q=\operatorname{diag}(-\delta,1)\), where \(0<\delta<\varepsilon\), satisfies \(\|\widehat Q-Q\|_2=\delta<\varepsilon\) but \(\widehat Q\notin K\), since \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)=-\delta<0\). Thus arbitrarily accurate coefficientwise or normwise rounding of a boundary Gram certificate need not preserve conic feasibility. A feasibility-preserving exactification step must instead enforce membership in the cone or operate within the certificate's minimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semidefinite certificate on the cone boundary can be rounded arbitrarily accurately to an indefinite matrix, so closeness alone does not preserve certificate feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\)
\(0<\delta<\varepsilon\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat Q-Q\|_2<\varepsilon\) while \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^2\) and \(\widehat Q\notin\mathbb S_+^2\).

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite two-by-two matrices.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct eigenvalue counterexample establishes the stated failure mechanism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically correct and fits the failure-boundary container, but no inspectable source supports the broader certificate-exactification guidance.

children.title: Certificate Selection-Complexity Landscape
children.top_down_role: Structural parameters, method-selection tradeoffs, and scalability boundaries across sparse certificate families.

children.title: Structural Complexity Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameters controlling sparse relaxation size and solver effort.

children.title: Treewidth-Clique Complexity Parameters
children.top_down_role: Graph parameters controlling local semidefinite dimensions.

children.title: Treewidth Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes indexed by interaction-graph treewidth.

knowledge_statements.title: Treewidth Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite block order induced by a chordal extension of the correlative sparsity graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a correlative sparsity graph and let \(\widetilde G\) be a chordal extension with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\). Write \(w=\max_k|C_k|-1\). In an order-\(r\) clique-sparse moment relaxation, the moment sequence restricted to clique \(C_k\) through degree \(2r\) has length \(\binom{|C_k|+2r}{2r}\), while the corresponding moment matrix \(M_r^{C_k}\) has order \(\binom{|C_k|+r}{r}\). Hence every local moment-matrix block has order at most \(\binom{w+1+r}{r}\), rather than the dense order \(\binom{|V|+r}{r}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At fixed relaxation order, the width of the selected chordal extension bounds each clique-local moment-matrix order by a binomial expression in that width rather than the total variable count.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde G\) is a chordal extension of \(G\).
\(r\in\mathbb N\) is the relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_k\operatorname{ord}(M_r^{C_k})\leq \binom{w+1+r}{r}\).

notation.meaning: Width of the selected chordal extension, equal to its maximum clique size minus one.
Order-r moment matrix restricted to variables in clique C_k.
Number of rows, equivalently columns, of a square matrix M.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monomial counting gives the corrected moment-sequence length and matrix order

children.title: Maximal Clique Size
children.top_down_role: Largest clique cardinality governing local block dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Clique Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-size parameter for a chosen chordal extension of correlative sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde G=(V,\widetilde E)\) be a chordal extension of a correlative sparsity graph, and let \(\mathcal C(\widetilde G)\) denote its maximal cliques. The maximal clique size is \[\omega(\widetilde G)=\max_{C\in\mathcal C(\widetilde G)}|C|.\] For a clique-local relaxation of order \(r\), this parameter determines the largest full monomial index set, whose cardinality is \(\binom{\omega(\widetilde G)+r}{r}\). The value depends on the selected chordal extension and may exceed the clique number of the original graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal clique size is the largest number of variables in any maximal clique of the chosen chordal extension.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde G\) is chordal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\omega(\widetilde G)=\max_{C\in\mathcal C(\widetilde G)}|C|\).

notation.meaning: Family of maximal cliques of the chordal graph.
Maximal clique size of the chosen extension.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard graph-theoretic definition with sparse-relaxation interpretation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and monomial-count consequence are precise and fit the container, but no cited source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Fill-In Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of clique growth on chordal completion choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-In Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of sparse-relaxation dimensions on edges introduced during chordal completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G=(V,E)\) and chordal extension \(\widetilde G=(V,E\cup F)\), define the fill set \(F\) and \(\omega_F=\max_{C\in\mathcal C(\widetilde G)}|C|\). At relaxation order \(r\), the largest clique-local moment block has order \(b(F)=\binom{\omega_F+r}{r}\). Consequently, two valid fill sets \(F_1,F_2\) can produce different computational dimensions even for the same polynomial problem; if \(\omega_{F_1}<\omega_{F_2}\), then \(b(F_1)<b(F_2)\). Thus chordal-completion choice is a structural complexity parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different chordal fill-ins can create different largest cliques and therefore different semidefinite block sizes for the same problem.
assumptions_latex: \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) each produce a chordal extension of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\omega_{F_1}<\omega_{F_2}\Longrightarrow \binom{\omega_{F_1}+r}{r}<\binom{\omega_{F_2}+r}{r}\).

notation.meaning: Edges added to obtain a chordal extension.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows from chordal clique construction and monomial counting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonic block-order comparison is correct for r at least one and fits fill-in sensitivity, but the sparse-relaxation interpretation lacks a cited source.

children.title: Local Cone Dimension
children.top_down_role: Local semidefinite dimensions induced by clique structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Cone Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient dimension of a clique-local positive-semidefinite cone in a sparse relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For clique \(C\) and relaxation order \(r\), let \(s_C=\binom{|C|+r}{r}\) be the number of monomials in variables indexed by \(C\) of degree at most \(r\). The associated Gram or moment block belongs to \(\mathbb S_+^{s_C}\). Its local cone dimension, meaning the dimension of the ambient symmetric-matrix space, is \[d_C=\dim\mathbb S^{s_C}=\frac{s_C(s_C+1)}{2}.\] The largest local cone dimension is \(\max_C d_C\); affine coefficient constraints may reduce the dimension of the feasible slice but not this ambient cone dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique with s local monomials produces a positive-semidefinite cone whose symmetric ambient space has dimension s(s+1)/2.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a variable clique.
\(r\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_C=\frac{1}{2}\binom{|C|+r}{r}\left(\binom{|C|+r}{r}+1\right)\).

notation.meaning: Number of clique monomials of degree at most r.
Ambient dimension of the local symmetric-matrix cone.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: symmetric-matrix dimension and monomial-count identities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ambient symmetric-space dimension is stated correctly and distinguished from a feasible affine slice, but the clique-local cone interpretation has no cited source.

children.title: Support-Pattern Complexity Parameters
children.top_down_role: Support parameters controlling term-sparse models.

children.title: Support Cardinality
children.top_down_role: Number of active exponent vectors in sparse polynomial data.

knowledge_statements.title: Support Cardinality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Number of distinct exponent vectors occurring with nonzero coefficients in a polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polynomial \(f(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}f_\alpha x^\alpha\) with finitely many nonzero coefficients, its support is \[\operatorname{supp}(f)=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:f_\alpha\neq0\}.\] The support cardinality is \(s(f)=|\operatorname{supp}(f)|\). For a polynomial optimization instance \(\mathcal P=(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m)\), the aggregate support cardinality may be recorded as \(s(\mathcal P)=\left|\bigcup_{j=0}^m\operatorname{supp}(g_j)\right|\), with \(g_0=f\), thereby counting distinct exponent vectors rather than repeated occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support cardinality counts the distinct exponent vectors having nonzero coefficients, either in one polynomial or across an optimization instance.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(f)=|\{\alpha:f_\alpha\neq0\}|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of polynomial support

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The single-polynomial definition is standard. The aggregate instance-level union is an explicit but noncanonical convention and requires a supporting source or local convention reference.

children.title: Pattern Width
children.top_down_role: Width of monomial-interaction patterns used by term-sparse models.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum variable incidence of any supported monomial, using the term-sparsity interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subset\mathbb N^n\) be a finite exponent pattern. For \(\alpha\in A\), define its variable incidence set by \(I(\alpha)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:\alpha_i>0\}\). The pattern width of \(A\) is \[w(A)=\max_{\alpha\in A}|I(\alpha)|.\] For polynomials \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\), take \(A=\bigcup_{j=0}^m\operatorname{supp}(g_j)\), where \(g_0=f\). This width measures the largest number of distinct variables jointly present in one supported monomial, not its total degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pattern width is the largest number of distinct variables appearing together in any supported monomial of the instance.
assumptions_latex: \(A\subset\mathbb N^n\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w(A)=\max_{\alpha\in A}|\{i:\alpha_i>0\}|\).

notation.meaning: Variables occurring in the monomial indexed by alpha.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula consistently defines maximum monomial variable incidence, but “pattern width” is not sufficiently standardized to identify this exact quantity without an authoritative term-sparsity source.

children.title: Support Closure Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of active support under sparse certificate construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Support Closure Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth of exponent sets under the additive closure operations used to construct certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_0\subset\mathbb N^n\) be a finite initial exponent set and let \(B\subset\mathbb N^n\) be a finite generator set. Define truncated additive closures recursively by \(A_{t+1}=A_t\cup((A_t+B)\cap D)\), where \(A_t+B=\{\alpha+\beta:\alpha\in A_t,\beta\in B\}\) and \(D\subset\mathbb N^n\) is a prescribed finite degree region. The support-closure growth at step \(t\) is \[\gamma_t=|A_{t+1}|-|A_t|,\] and the cumulative growth through step \(T\) is \(|A_T|-|A_0|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support-closure growth counts new exponent vectors introduced by repeated truncated Minkowski addition during certificate construction.
assumptions_latex: \(A_0,B,D\subset\mathbb N^n\) are finite.
\(A_0\subseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_t=|A_{t+1}\setminus A_t|\geq0\).

notation.meaning: Exponent set after t closure steps.
Number of exponents added at closure step t.
Finite truncation region for admissible exponents.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recurrence is internally consistent, but it selects one generic truncated Minkowski-closure operator without establishing that this is the intended certificate-construction closure for the terminal container.

children.title: Term-Block Dimension
children.top_down_role: Local block sizes induced by support patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Term-Block Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite block dimension induced by a block of monomial indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subset\mathbb N^n\) be a finite block of exponent indices and let \(v_B(x)=(x^\alpha)_{\alpha\in B}\). A Gram component supported on this block has the form \(v_B(x)^\mathsf TQ_Bv_B(x)\) with \(Q_B\in\mathbb S_+^{|B|}\). The term-block order is \(b_B=|B|\), and its ambient cone dimension is \[d_B=\dim\mathbb S^{b_B}=\frac{b_B(b_B+1)}{2}.\] For a block decomposition \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\), the maximum term-block order is \(\max_k|B_k|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block of b monomials yields a b-by-b Gram block and a positive-semidefinite cone of ambient dimension b(b+1)/2.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb N^n\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_B\in\mathbb S_+^{b_B}\) and \(d_B=b_B(b_B+1)/2\).

notation.meaning: Monomial vector indexed by exponent block B.
Ambient symmetric-cone dimension of the block.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Gram-block order equals monomial-block cardinality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gram-block order and ambient cone dimension are correct and fit the container, but no term-sparsity or Gram-representation source is cited.

children.title: Degree-Order Complexity Parameters
children.top_down_role: Degree parameters controlling moment and certificate dimensions.

children.title: Global Relaxation Degree
children.top_down_role: Overall degree level governing a sparse relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Relaxation Degree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single truncation order shared by every moment and localizing constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider polynomial data \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\). A global relaxation order is an integer \(r\) satisfying \(2r\geq\deg f\) and \(r\geq d_j:=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\) for every constraint. The order-\(r\) moment relaxation uses moments \(y_\alpha\) through degree \(2r\), the moment matrix \(M_r(y)\), and localizing matrices \(M_{r-d_j}(g_jy)\). Its global relaxation degree is \(2r\), the common maximum moment degree imposed across all blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global order r truncates all moment data at degree 2r and uses compatible lower-order localizing matrices for every constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(2r\geq\deg f\) and \(r\geq\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\) for all \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_r(y)\) and \(M_{r-d_j}(g_jy)\) depend only on moments of degree at most \(2r\).

notation.meaning: Half-degree rounded upward for constraint polynomial g_j.

children.title: Clique-Local Orders
children.top_down_role: Relaxation orders assigned to individual cliques.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Local Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation orders assigned separately to cliques of a sparse polynomial model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\) be variable cliques, and assign an integer order \(r_k\geq0\) to clique \(C_k\). For each polynomial \(g_j\) assigned to clique \(C_k\), admissibility requires \(r_k\geq\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\); if an objective component \(f_k\in\mathbb R[x_{C_k}]\) is represented locally, also require \(2r_k\geq\deg f_k\). The clique-local relaxation uses \(M_{r_k}^{C_k}(y)\) and localizing matrices \(M_{r_k-d_j}^{C_k}(g_jy)\), so clique \(C_k\) has block order \(\binom{|C_k|+r_k}{r_k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each variable clique may receive its own valid relaxation order, determining the clique's moment and localizing block sizes.
assumptions_latex: Every assigned polynomial involves only variables from its clique.
Each \(r_k\) satisfies the stated degree requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ord}(M_{r_k}^{C_k})=\binom{|C_k|+r_k}{r_k}\).

notation.meaning: Relaxation order assigned to clique C_k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: local monomial counting under clique-specific truncation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The degree conditions and local moment-block count are coherent, but independently assigned clique orders require a source specifying the intended heterogeneous sparse hierarchy and its compatibility conditions.

children.title: Heterogeneous Order Profiles
children.top_down_role: Nonuniform local-order assignments across sparse blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Heterogeneous Order Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector of distinct valid truncation orders across cliques or constraint blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\), a heterogeneous order profile is a vector \(\mathbf r=(r_1,\ldots,r_p)\in\mathbb N^p\) such that every polynomial assigned to \(C_k\) satisfies the local degree admissibility conditions at order \(r_k\). The profile induces moment-block orders \[s_k(\mathbf r)=\binom{|C_k|+r_k}{r_k}.\] It is heterogeneous when the entries are not all equal. Profiles are ordered componentwise: \(\mathbf r\preceq\mathbf r'\) exactly when \(r_k\leq r_k'\) for all \(k\); this implies \(s_k(\mathbf r)\leq s_k(\mathbf r')\) for every clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heterogeneous profile assigns different valid relaxation orders to different cliques and is compared by componentwise order.
assumptions_latex: \(r_k\) is degree-admissible for every polynomial assigned to \(C_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf r\preceq\mathbf r'\Longrightarrow s_k(\mathbf r)\leq s_k(\mathbf r')\) for all \(k\).

notation.meaning: Moment-block order induced on clique C_k.
Componentwise partial order on order profiles.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: componentwise truncation profile and monomial counting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise profile and block-order monotonicity are internally correct, but the exact heterogeneous-profile definition is not supported by a cited sparse-hierarchy source.

children.title: Order-Induced Dimension Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth of local moment or certificate blocks as orders increase.

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Induced Dimension Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension growth of clique-local moment and SOS matrices as relaxation order increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a clique containing \(n_k\) variables and relaxation order \(d\), the monomial vector of degree at most \(d\) has length \(b_k(d)=\binom{n_k+d}{d}\). Consequently, its moment or Gram matrix has dimension \(b_k(d)\) and \(b_k(d)(b_k(d)+1)/2\) independent symmetric entries. For fixed \(n_k\), \(b_k(d)=\Theta(d^{n_k})\) as \(d\to\infty\); for fixed \(d\), \(b_k(d)=\Theta(n_k^d)\) as \(n_k\to\infty\). Thus increasing order produces polynomial growth whose exponent is controlled by clique size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At order d, a clique with n variables produces a matrix of binomial dimension; growth is polynomial in d with exponent n and polynomial in n with exponent d.
assumptions_latex: \(n_k,d\in\mathbb{N}\)
The relaxation uses all monomials of total degree at most \(d\) on clique \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_k(d)=\binom{n_k+d}{d}\), with \(b_k(d)=\Theta(d^{n_k})\) for fixed \(n_k\).

notation.meaning: number of variables in clique k

children.title: Separator Cardinality

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Cardinality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size parameter for overlaps in a clique-based correlative sparsity decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_c=(V_c,E_c)\) be a clique-coupling graph with variable-index sets \(I_k\) attached to vertices \(k\in V_c\). For each coupling edge \(e=\{i,j\}\), its separator is \(S_e=I_i\cap I_j\), and its separator cardinality is \(s_e=|S_e|\). The maximum separator cardinality is \(s_{\max}=\max_{e\in E_c}s_e\), with \(s_{\max}=0\) when \(E_c=\varnothing\). The profile \((s_e)_{e\in E_c}\), rather than only its maximum, records heterogeneous overlap sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separator cardinality counts variables shared by adjacent cliques; its maximum and edgewise profile quantify the size of local coupling interfaces.
assumptions_latex: \(I_k\) is finite for every \(k\in V_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_e=|I_i\cap I_j|\) for \(e=\{i,j\}\), and \(s_{\max}=\max_{e\in E_c}s_e\).

notation.meaning: separator associated with coupling edge e

children.title: Consistency Constraint Count
children.top_down_role: Number of overlap constraints induced by shared entries.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency Constraint Count
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar count for pairwise agreement of truncated clique moment sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose adjacent cliques \(i\) and \(j\) carry local moment sequences through degree \(2d\). Agreement on their separator \(S_e=I_i\cap I_j\) requires one equality \(y^{(i)}_\alpha=y^{(j)}_\alpha\) for every monomial supported on \(S_e\) with \(|\alpha|\le 2d\). If \(s_e=|S_e|\), the edge contributes \(c_e(d)=\binom{s_e+2d}{2d}\) scalar equalities. Before eliminating redundancies, an edge-indexed formulation therefore contains \(C(d)=\sum_{e\in E_c}c_e(d)\) consistency equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching two order-d clique moment sequences across a separator of size s requires binomial(s+2d,2d) scalar equalities, summed over coupling edges before redundancy removal.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb{N}\)
Each coupling edge imposes equality for every separator moment of degree at most \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(d)=\sum_{e\in E_c}\binom{s_e+2d}{2d}\) before redundancy elimination.

notation.meaning: local moment indexed by alpha in clique k

children.title: Coupling Graph Density
children.top_down_role: Density of interactions among local sparse blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Graph Density
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized edge density of the graph coupling local polynomial-optimization blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a simple undirected clique-coupling graph \(G_c=(V_c,E_c)\) with \(q=|V_c|\), define its density by \(\rho(G_c)=2|E_c|/[q(q-1)]\) when \(q\ge 2\), and set \(\rho(G_c)=0\) when \(q<2\). Then \(0\le\rho(G_c)\le1\): zero represents no pairwise coupling, while one represents coupling between every distinct pair of blocks. This unweighted density records coupling incidence but not separator sizes or relaxation orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupling graph density is the fraction of possible block pairs that are coupled; it ranges from zero to one and ignores interface sizes.
assumptions_latex: \(G_c\) is finite, simple, and undirected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(G_c)=2|E_c|/[q(q-1)]\) for \(q\ge2\), with \(0\le\rho(G_c)\le1\).

children.title: Communication Burden
children.top_down_role: Coordination cost induced by separator-based coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Burden
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar communication volume for distributed synchronization of overlapping moment blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In an edge-based distributed implementation at order \(d\), suppose each synchronization round sends one copy of every shared separator moment in each direction along every coupling edge. For separator size \(s_e\), the communicated scalar count per round is \(B_{\mathrm{round}}(d)=2\sum_{e\in E_c}\binom{s_e+2d}{2d}\). After \(T\) rounds the cumulative volume is \(B_T(d)=T B_{\mathrm{round}}(d)\), excluding protocol metadata, compression, and retransmission. One-direction or coordinator-based protocols change the factor but retain the separator-moment sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bidirectional exchange of every shared separator moment costs twice the raw consistency count per round and scales linearly with the number of rounds.
assumptions_latex: \(T,d\in\mathbb{N}\)
Every edge transmits all moments through degree \(2d\) once in each direction per round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_T(d)=2T\sum_{e\in E_c}\binom{s_e+2d}{2d}\) communicated scalars.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct count under the explicitly stated bidirectional communication model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Semidefinite Cost Regime
children.top_down_role: Problems dominated by PSD block dimensions and sparse factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Cost Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost regime in which positive-semidefinite blocks govern relaxation size and solution effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial relaxation is in the semidefinite cost regime when its conic representation contains positive-semidefinite blocks \(Q_k\in\mathbb{S}_+^{b_k}\) and the storage or factorization of these blocks dominates its remaining affine and scalar-cone operations. For an order-\(d_k\) SOS block on \(n_k\) variables, \(b_k=\binom{n_k+d_k}{d_k}\). A structural size proxy is \(M_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\sum_k b_k(b_k+1)/2\); a factorization proxy is \(F_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\sum_k b_k^3\). These proxies classify the regime but are not solver-independent runtime identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The semidefinite regime occurs when PSD block storage and factorization dominate, with block dimensions determined by local variable counts and SOS orders.
assumptions_latex: Each SOS Gram block uses all monomials through its local order.
\(b_k\) denotes the dimension of PSD block \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\sum_k b_k(b_k+1)/2\) and \(F_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\sum_k b_k^3\) are structural cost proxies.

children.title: Second-Order-Cone Cost Regime
children.top_down_role: Problems aligned with SDSOS, factor-width, or SOCP-SONC models.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Cost Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost regime for relaxations represented predominantly by Lorentz or rotated-Lorentz cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial relaxation is in the second-order-cone cost regime when it admits a formulation using affine constraints and cone memberships \((t_j,z_j)\in\mathcal{Q}_{m_j}=\{(t,z):\|z\|_2\le t\}\), and processing these cones dominates other operations. SDSOS certificates enter this regime because each constrained symmetric \(2\times2\) block can be represented by a rotated second-order cone; factor-width-two Gram decompositions have the same structure. The cone-size proxy is \(M_{\mathrm{SOC}}=\sum_j m_j\), while actual factorization cost depends on affine coupling and solver choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SOCP regime covers models dominated by Lorentz-cone constraints, including SDSOS and factor-width-two Gram constructions represented through small PSD blocks.
assumptions_latex: The conic formulation contains no unreduced PSD block larger than \(2\times2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dominant memberships have the form \((t_j,z_j)\in\mathcal{Q}_{m_j}\), with aggregate cone-size proxy \(M_{\mathrm{SOC}}=\sum_jm_j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regime description and Lorentz-cone formulation are plausible, but the nontrivial claims connecting SDSOS and factor-width-two Gram decompositions to SOCP representations have no supplied source or locator.

children.title: Relative-Entropy Cost Regime
children.top_down_role: Problems aligned with SAGE and exponential-cone models.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Entropy Cost Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost regime for SAGE-type certificates dominated by relative-entropy or exponential cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the closed relative-entropy cone by \(\mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{re}}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):u>0,\ v>0,\ u\log(u/v)\le w\}\). A signomial or polynomial relaxation is in the relative-entropy cost regime when its certificate is formulated predominantly through affine constraints and memberships in products of \(\mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{re}}\), or equivalently through exponential-cone representations, and these memberships dominate computational effort. SAGE relaxations typically have this form because their AM/GM-exponential certificates impose relative-entropy inequalities on coefficient vectors. Aggregate cone dimension and affine coupling provide structural cost proxies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative-entropy regime consists of SAGE or related models whose main conic constraints encode relative entropy, equivalently using exponential cones.
assumptions_latex: The certificate has an explicit relative-entropy or exponential-cone formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dominant nonlinear constraints are memberships in a product of \(\mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{re}}\) or an equivalent product of exponential cones.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-entropy cone definition is coherent, but the equivalence to exponential-cone formulations and the characterization of SAGE certificates require an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Linear-Programming Cost Regime
children.top_down_role: Problems aligned with DSOS and classical LP positivity families.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Programming Cost Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost regime for positivity certificates expressible using affine equations and nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial relaxation is in the linear-programming cost regime when its certificate has a formulation \(Az=b\), \(z\ge0\), possibly after introducing auxiliary variables, and sparse linear-system processing dominates its cost. DSOS certificates belong to this regime because diagonal dominance of a symmetric Gram matrix \(Q\) can be imposed by linear inequalities \(Q_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}u_{ij}\), \(-u_{ij}\le Q_{ij}\le u_{ij}\), and \(u_{ij}\ge0\). Classical coefficientwise or basis-dependent positivity conditions also lie in this regime when all certificate constraints are linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The LP regime covers certificates described by affine constraints and nonnegative variables, including DSOS through a linear diagonal-dominance formulation.
assumptions_latex: All absolute values in diagonal-dominance constraints are replaced by nonnegative auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate feasible set is polyhedral and can be written as \(\{z:Az=b,\ z\ge0\}\) after adding auxiliaries.

children.title: Dense SOS Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: Dense SOS Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-d dense SOS lower bound for unconstrained polynomial minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) have degree at most \(2d\), and let \(v_d(x)\) contain every monomial of total degree at most \(d\). The order-\(d\) dense SOS lower bound is \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{dense}}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}:p-\gamma=v_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv_d(x),\ Q\succeq0\}\). Coefficient matching is linear in \((\gamma,Q)\), so this is a semidefinite program with one PSD block of dimension \(\binom{n+d}{d}\). Every feasible \(\gamma\) satisfies \(\gamma\le\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}p(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense SOS uses one Gram matrix over all degree-d monomials; feasibility certifies a global lower bound and yields an SDP with binomial block dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)
\(\deg p\le2d\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{dense}}\le\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}p(x)\), with PSD block dimension \(\binom{n+d}{d}\).

notation.meaning: vector of all monomials of degree at most d

children.title: Sparse SOS Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Structured SOS formulations exploiting correlative or term sparsity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse SOS Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-local SOS representation for a polynomial compatible with correlative sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let variable sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_q\) cover all monomial supports of \(p\), and choose local orders \(d_k\). A clique-sparse SOS lower bound is \(\rho^{\mathrm{sparse}}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}:p-\gamma=\sum_{k=1}^q v_{d_k,I_k}(x)^{\mathsf T}Q_kv_{d_k,I_k}(x),\ Q_k\succeq0\}\). Here \(v_{d_k,I_k}\) contains monomials supported on \(I_k\) of degree at most \(d_k\). The SDP has PSD blocks of dimensions \(\binom{|I_k|+d_k}{d_k}\), and every feasible \(\gamma\) is a global lower bound for \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse SOS replaces one global Gram matrix by clique-local PSD matrices; their dimensions depend on clique sizes, while every feasible value remains a valid global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Every monomial of \(p\) is supported within at least one \(I_k\).
\(2d_k\) is sufficient for the terms assigned to clique \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho^{\mathrm{sparse}}\le\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}p(x)\), using PSD blocks of size \(\binom{|I_k|+d_k}{d_k}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-sparse moment relaxation and SOS dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the block-supported moment and localizing matrices, their sparse primal relaxation, and the degree-truncated block-SOS dual under Assumption 8.2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume J=\dot\bigcup_{k=1}^pJ_k,\ g_j\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x(I_k)]\ (j\in J_k), and f=\sum_{k=1}^pf_k with f_k\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x(I_k)]. Define \mathbf M_d(\mathbf y,I_k) and \mathbf M_d(g\mathbf y,I_k) by retaining the rows and columns indexed by \alpha\in\mathbb N^n satisfying \alpha_i=0 whenever i\notin I_k. Then
\[\rho_d^{\mathrm{sparse}}=\inf_{\mathbf y}\left\{L_{\mathbf y}(f):\mathbf M_d(\mathbf y,I_k)\succeq0\ (k=1,\ldots,p),\ \mathbf M_{d-v_j}(g_j\mathbf y,I_k)\succeq0\ (j\in J_k),\ y_0=1\right\}.\]
Its dual is
\[(\rho_d^{\mathrm{sparse}})^*=\sup_{\lambda,\sigma_{kj}}\left\{\lambda:f-\lambda=\sum_{k=1}^p\left(\sigma_{k0}+\sum_{j\in J_k}\sigma_{kj}g_j\right),\ \sigma_{k0},\sigma_{kj}\in\Sigma[\mathbf x(I_k)],\ \deg\sigma_{k0}\le2d,\ \deg(\sigma_{kj}g_j)\le2d\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sparse primal uses block-supported submatrices of the full moment and localizing matrices. Its dual expresses f minus a scalar as a sum of block-supported SOS polynomials and SOS-weighted constraints, subject to degree bounds.
assumptions_latex: J=\dot\bigcup_{k=1}^pJ_k
g_j\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x(I_k)]\quad(j\in J_k)
f=\sum_{k=1}^pf_k,\quad f_k\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x(I_k)]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_d^{\mathrm{sparse}}\text{ and }(\rho_d^{\mathrm{sparse}})^*\text{ are the displayed block-moment primal and block-SOS dual programs}

children.title: Strength-Cost Crossover Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes governing the preferred balance between relaxation strength plus computational cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength-Cost Crossover Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget-dependent criterion for a strict local crossover between dense and sparse relaxation families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each family \(H\in\{D,S\}\), let \(\mathcal{R}_H\) be its set of admissible configurations, let \(c_H:\mathcal{R}_H\to[0,\infty)\) be a fixed cost proxy, and let \(\rho_H:\mathcal{R}_H\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be its certified lower bound. For \(B\ge0\), define \(\beta_H(B)=\sup\{\rho_H(r):r\in\mathcal{R}_H,\ c_H(r)\le B\}\), with \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\). A strict local strength-cost crossover occurs at \(B_*>0\) if \(\beta_D(B_*)=\beta_S(B_*)\in\mathbb{R}\) and there exist \(\varepsilon\in(0,B_*)\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\) such that \(\sigma[\beta_D(B)-\beta_S(B)]<0\) for every \(B\in(B_*-\varepsilon,B_*)\) and \(\sigma[\beta_D(B)-\beta_S(B)]>0\) for every \(B\in(B_*,B_*+\varepsilon)\). This condition compares the best certificates attainable at equal cost rather than at equal relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict dense-sparse crossover is a positive budget where the two families have the same finite best attainable bound and their ordering is strictly reversed throughout some budget interval on the two sides of that point.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{R}_D\) and \(\mathcal{R}_S\) refer to configurations for the same optimization instance and lower-bound convention.
The two cost maps \(c_D\) and \(c_S\) use one fixed, comparable cost model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strict local crossover \(B_*\) has \(\beta_D(B_*)=\beta_S(B_*)\in\mathbb{R}\) and an explicitly quantified local sign reversal of \(\beta_D-\beta_S\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Induced Bound Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order bound degradation caused by restricting SOS multipliers to a fixed clique pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\) for \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). For truncated certificate cones satisfying \(M_d^{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\subseteq M_d^{\mathrm{den}}(g)\), define \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{sp}}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in M_d^{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\}\) and \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{den}}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in M_d^{\mathrm{den}}(g)\}\). If every element of \(M_d^{\mathrm{den}}(g)\) is nonnegative on \(K\), then \[\rho_d^{\mathrm{sp}}\le \rho_d^{\mathrm{den}}\le f^*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x).\] Sparsity-induced degradation at order \(d\) occurs exactly when \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{sp}}<\rho_d^{\mathrm{den}}\), equivalently when some \(\eta>0\) satisfies \(f-\gamma\notin M_d^{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\) for every \(\gamma>\rho_d^{\mathrm{den}}-\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed relaxation order, a clique-restricted SOS cone cannot produce a stronger lower bound than the corresponding dense cone. Degradation is strict exactly when the sparse optimal value is below the dense optimal value.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m,d\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) is nonempty.
\(M_d^{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\subseteq M_d^{\mathrm{den}}(g)\), and both cones provide certificates of nonnegativity on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{sp}}\le\rho_d^{\mathrm{den}}\le f^*\), with strict sparsity-induced degradation precisely when \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{sp}}<\rho_d^{\mathrm{den}}\).

children.title: Full Semidefinite Gram Cones
children.top_down_role: Relaxation strength, scaling profile, plus certification capacity of full semidefinite Gram representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Semidefinite Gram Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The unrestricted positive-semidefinite Gram cone and its degree-bounded polynomial image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(d\in\mathbb N_0\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(z_d(x)\in\mathbb R^N\), where \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\), list all monomials of degree at most \(d\). The full semidefinite Gram cone is \(\mathbb S_+^N\), and its polynomial image is \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{PSD}}:=\{z_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_d(x):Q\in\mathbb S_+^N\}=\Sigma_{n,2d}.\] For \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\), the feasible Gram slice is \[\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{PSD}}(p):=\{Q\in\mathbb S_+^N:p(x)=z_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_d(x)\}.\] Thus \(p\) is SOS if and only if \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PSD}}(p)\neq\varnothing\), and this condition is semidefinite representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Gram cone consists of all positive semidefinite matrices. Its polynomial image is the degree-bounded SOS cone, while the matrices representing a fixed polynomial form a semidefinite feasible slice.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(d\in\mathbb N_0\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(z_d(x)\) lists every monomial in \(x\) of degree at most \(d\).
\(p\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\Sigma_{n,2d}\) if and only if \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PSD}}(p)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Vector of all monomials of degree at most d
Cone of real positive semidefinite N by N matrices
SOS cone of polynomials in n variables with degree at most 2d

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric matrix \(Q\) is scaled diagonally dominant when there exists a positive diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(DQD\) is diagonally dominant with nonnegative diagonal. The restricted SOCP Gram cone is \[\mathcal G_{\mathrm{SDD}}(p)=\{Q\in\mathrm{SDD}^N:p(x)=z_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_d(x)\}.\] Membership in \(\mathrm{SDD}^N\) admits a decomposition into positive-semidefinite matrices supported on principal \(2\times2\) blocks and is therefore SOCP-representable. Since \(\mathrm{SDD}^N\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N\), feasibility certifies that \(p\) is SOS.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring a scaled diagonally dominant Gram matrix yields an SOCP-representable sufficient, but generally restricted, SOS certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric matrix \(Q\) is diagonally dominant with nonnegative diagonal when \(Q_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}|Q_{ij}|\) for every \(i\). The restricted LP Gram cone is \[\mathcal G_{\mathrm{DD}}(p)=\{Q\in\mathrm{DD}^N:p(x)=z_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_d(x)\}.\] Introducing variables that majorize \(|Q_{ij}|\) expresses these inequalities linearly. Because \(\mathrm{DD}^N\subseteq\mathrm{SDD}^N\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N\), every feasible matrix certifies an SOS representation of \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonally dominant Gram matrix produces an LP-checkable sufficient SOS certificate, more restrictive than the SOCP and SDP versions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed coefficient-matching constraints, \[\mathrm{DD}^N\subseteq\mathrm{SDD}^N\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N.\] Maximizing \(\gamma\) subject to a Gram representation of \(f-\gamma\) therefore yields \[\rho_{\mathrm{LP}}\le\rho_{\mathrm{SOCP}}\le\rho_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le f^*.\] The corresponding feasibility models use linear inequalities, second-order cone constraints, and a full positive-semidefinite constraint, respectively. Hence enlarging the Gram cone cannot weaken the certified bound, while it generally increases per-iteration linear-algebra cost and memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DD, SDD, and PSD cone inclusion orders certified bounds from weakest to strongest, while their conic models generally become more expensive.

children.title: Restricted-Cone Certification Gaps
children.top_down_role: Certificate or bound losses caused by replacing the full semidefinite cone.

assumptions_latex: \(n\ge2\) and \(d\ge2\), so the Gram matrix dimension is nontrivial.
The monomial basis is fixed before imposing DD or SDD restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restricted Gram cones may fail to certify an SOS polynomial and may yield strictly weaker optimization bounds.

notation.meaning: Polynomial cones admitting DD, SDD, and PSD Gram matrices

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure arises from strict cone restriction and can depend on the selected polynomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed monomial basis, the restricted polynomial cones satisfy \[\Sigma_{\mathrm{DD}}\subseteq\Sigma_{\mathrm{SDD}}\subseteq\Sigma_{\mathrm{SOS}}.\] In nontrivial dimensions these inclusions can be strict: an SOS polynomial may have a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix but no scaled-diagonally-dominant Gram matrix in that basis, and an SDSOS polynomial may have no diagonally dominant Gram matrix. Consequently, replacing the PSD cone by SDD or DD can make a feasible SOS certificate infeasible and can strictly decrease the lower bound at the same relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because DD and SDD are strict, basis-dependent restrictions of PSD Gram matrices, they can miss valid SOS certificates and weaken bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Cone Certification Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, but no source or separating example supports strict DD–SDD–SOS inclusions, basis dependence, or strict bound loss. These are the central nontrivial claims and require an authoritative DSOS/SDSOS source with a precise locator.

children.title: Gram-Matrix SOS Geometry
children.top_down_role: Gram-representable positivity certificates plus their structural cost profile.

knowledge_statements.title: Gram-Matrix SOS Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Gram representation of the degree-bounded SOS cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(d\in\mathbb N_0\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(z_d(x)\in\mathbb R^N\), where \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\), list all monomials of degree at most \(d\). Define the linear Gram map \(\mathcal A_d:\mathbb S^N\to\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\) by \(\mathcal A_d(Q)=z_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_d(x)\). Then \[\Sigma_{n,2d}=\mathcal A_d(\mathbb S_+^N)=\{p\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}:\exists Q\in\mathbb S_+^N,\ p=\mathcal A_d(Q)\}.\] For each \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\), its symmetric Gram matrices form the affine fiber \(\mathcal A_d^{-1}(p)\), and \(p\) is SOS exactly when \(\mathcal A_d^{-1}(p)\cap\mathbb S_+^N\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For explicitly fixed numbers of variables and degree, the degree-bounded SOS cone is the linear image of the positive semidefinite cone under the Gram map. A polynomial is SOS exactly when its affine Gram fiber contains a positive semidefinite matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(d\in\mathbb N_0\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(z_d(x)\) lists every monomial in \(x\) of degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_{n,2d}=\mathcal A_d(\mathbb S_+^N)\), and \(p\in\Sigma_{n,2d}\) exactly when \(\mathcal A_d^{-1}(p)\cap\mathbb S_+^N\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Linear Gram map from symmetric matrices to degree-bounded polynomials
SOS cone of polynomials in n variables with degree at most 2d

children.title: Circuit-Based SONC Geometry
children.top_down_role: Support-sensitive circuit certificates plus their compatible polynomial structures.

assumptions_latex: \(A=\{\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_r,\beta\}\subset\mathbb N^n\), where \(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_r\) are affinely independent.
\(\beta\) lies in the relative interior of \(\operatorname{conv}\{\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_r\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The circuit-number inequality characterizes nonnegativity of the circuit polynomial under the stated parity convention.

notation.meaning: Positive barycentric coordinates of the inner exponent
Cone of sums of nonnegative circuit polynomials

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard polynomial circuit geometry with even outer exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta=\sum_{j=0}^r\lambda_j\alpha_j\), where \(\lambda_j>0\) and \(\sum_j\lambda_j=1\), and assume \(\alpha_j\in(2\mathbb N)^n\) with \(c_j>0\). The circuit polynomial is \[f(x)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_jx^{\alpha_j}+c_\beta x^\beta.\] With \(\Theta_f=\prod_{j=0}^r(c_j/\lambda_j)^{\lambda_j}\), it is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^n\) exactly when \(c_\beta\ge-\Theta_f\) if \(\beta\in(2\mathbb N)^n\), and \(|c_\beta|\le\Theta_f\) otherwise. The SONC cone consists of finite sums of such nonnegative circuit polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SONC geometry decomposes polynomials into sparse circuits whose nonnegativity is controlled by a weighted geometric-mean circuit number.
knowledge_statements.title: Circuit-Based SONC Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record combines a circuit-polynomial definition with a necessary-and-sufficient nonnegativity theorem. The formula appears standard and the leaf is appropriate, but no authoritative source supports the parity-dependent circuit-number characterization or the SONC-cone definition.

children.title: Exponential-Cone SAGE Geometry
children.top_down_role: SAGE certificate geometry, signomial structure, plus associated conic representations.

assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\exp(\alpha_i^{\mathsf T}x)\) has fixed exponents \(\alpha_i\in\mathbb R^n\).
An AGE component has at most one negative coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SAGE cone is a convex, exponential-cone-representable sufficient cone for global signomial nonnegativity.

notation.meaning: Arithmetic-geometric-exponential nonnegative cone with possible negative term k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global signomial SAGE geometry; polynomial applications require an explicit signomial transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For exponent matrix \(A=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)\), an AGE cone \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{AGE},k}(A)\) contains coefficient vectors with \(c_i\ge0\) for \(i\ne k\) whose signomial is globally nonnegative, equivalently admitting the standard relative-entropy certificate balancing \(\alpha_k\) against the remaining exponents. The SAGE cone is the Minkowski sum \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{SAGE}}(A)=\sum_{k=1}^m\mathcal C_{\mathrm{AGE},k}(A).\] Every \(c\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{SAGE}}(A)\) defines a globally nonnegative signomial, and membership has a relative-entropy, hence exponential-cone, formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAGE decomposes a signomial into one-negative-term nonnegative components certified by relative entropy and representable with exponential cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Cone SAGE Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definitional role fits the SAGE leaf, but the claimed AGE equivalence is only referenced as a 'standard' certificate and is not stated precisely. No source supports the relative-entropy characterization or exponential-cone representation, so the mathematical version cannot yet be verified.

children.title: Support-Driven Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Support patterns favoring SOS, SONC, or SAGE certificate families.

assumptions_latex: A polynomial or signomial has finite exponent support \(A\).
Candidate certificate cones are compared at a fixed support and relaxation level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certificate selection can be formulated by testing support-compatible conic memberships and comparing their certified bounds and costs.

notation.meaning: Candidate SOS, SONC, or SAGE cone over the chosen representation
Certified lower bound from cone C

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal selection criterion, not a universal claim that one geometry dominates another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each admissible certificate cone \(\mathcal C\), define \[\rho_{\mathcal C}=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in\mathcal C\}.\] A support-driven regime restricts attention to cones whose defining atoms are compatible with \(A=\operatorname{supp}(f)\): Gram monomial pairs for SOS, affine circuits for SONC, or AGE decompositions for SAGE. Given a computational budget \(B\) and estimated solution cost \(T_{\mathcal C}(A)\), selection is the finite optimization rule \[\max\{\rho_{\mathcal C}:T_{\mathcal C}(A)\le B,\ \mathcal C\text{ is support-compatible}\}.\] No ordering of the resulting bounds follows from support alone without cone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select among SOS, SONC, and SAGE by support compatibility, budget, and certified bound; support alone does not imply universal dominance.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Driven Selection Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the selection-regime leaf, and the record properly avoids claiming universal cone dominance. Nevertheless, the comparison mixes polynomial SOS/SONC and signomial SAGE without fully specifying a common transformation, admissible finite cone family, or cost model. A comparative source and precise representation are required.

children.title: Geometry-Specific Certification Gaps
children.top_down_role: Positivity structures missed by particular certificate geometries.

assumptions_latex: Certificate cones are embedded in a common finite-dimensional coefficient space.
No cone inclusion between two compared geometries has been established.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonnegativity certification by one geometry does not generally imply certification by another.

notation.meaning: Cone of globally nonnegative functions in the common representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract boundary for incomparable inner approximations; explicit SOS, SONC, and SAGE separators remain to be sourced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2\subseteq\mathcal P_+\) be closed convex certificate cones arising from different decompositional geometries. If neither \(\mathcal C_1\subseteq\mathcal C_2\) nor \(\mathcal C_2\subseteq\mathcal C_1\), then there exist \(p_1\in\mathcal C_1\setminus\mathcal C_2\) and \(p_2\in\mathcal C_2\setminus\mathcal C_1\). Both functions are nonnegative, but each defeats one certificate geometry. Therefore absence of a certificate in SOS, SONC, or SAGE establishes only nonmembership in that selected inner cone, not failure of nonnegativity or of certification by another geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct certificate geometries can be incomparable, so failure in one cone does not imply nonnegativity failure or failure in another cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Specific Certification Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract consequence of two incomparable cones is correct and the failure-boundary kind fits. Its application to SOS, SONC, and SAGE is unsupported because neither their common coefficient-space embedding nor pairwise incomparability is established by a source or explicit separating examples.

children.title: Bound-Certificate Speed Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Comparison of rapid approximate bounds with exact or validated certification.

children.title: Rapid Numerical Bounds
children.top_down_role: Fast approximate lower bounds intended for screening, comparison, or large-scale computation.

assumptions_latex: A conic relaxation has finite optimal value \(\rho\).
A numerical solver returns approximate primal-dual iterates and a reported value \(\widehat\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\rho\) is only a numerical bound candidate until feasibility and inequality direction are validated.

notation.meaning: Floating-point value reported by a solver

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes quickly computed floating-point bounds from independently checkable certificates.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Semidefinite Optimization p. 22
source_refs.source_title: Moment and Polynomial Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A floating-point conic solve may rapidly produce \(\widehat\rho\) together with small residual \(\|r\|\). However, \(\|r\|\le\varepsilon\) and an approximately positive-semidefinite Gram matrix do not by themselves imply exact conic feasibility. Hence the inequality \(\widehat\rho\le f^*\) is not certified solely by the solver report. It becomes a rigorous lower bound only after constructing an exactly feasible dual certificate or after validated error analysis produces \(\delta\ge0\) such that \(\widehat\rho-\delta\le\rho\le f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fast solver value is not automatically rigorous; exact feasibility or validated error correction is needed to certify its bound direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Rapid Numerical Bounds

children.title: Exact Algebraic Certificates
children.top_down_role: Symbolically exact positivity certificates suitable for definitive verification.

assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb{Q}[x]\) and \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
\(\gamma\in\mathbb{Q}\), and every displayed polynomial identity is checked by exact rational arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational quadratic-module certificate for a polynomial lower bound.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact algebraic lower-bound certificate for \(\gamma\) is a rational polynomial identity \[f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i,\qquad \sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\cap\mathbb{Q}[x].\] It is verified by expanding both sides over \(\mathbb{Q}\), checking coefficient equality, and checking an exact rational Gram decomposition for every \(\sigma_i\). Since \(g_i(x)\ge0\) on \(K\) and sums of squares are nonnegative, the verified identity certifies \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational sum-of-squares identity, checked by exact coefficient and Gram-matrix arithmetic, certifies a rigorous polynomial lower bound on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Algebraic Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
